## Draft implementation plan — Add Accessible Archive Pagination

**Task file:** `tasks/20260919-tg01-eleventy-archive-handoff.md` (plan unchanged, still `Draft`)

### Outcome

Convert the blog archive into bounded static pages (≤ 20 posts each, newest-first, each post exactly once) with boundary-aware previous/next navigation, while `/blog/` stays the first page and home, tags, feed, sitemap, and post pages keep their current output. No client-side JavaScript anywhere.

### Current state (inspection findings)

- `content/blog.njk:1-7` — single page at `permalink: /blog/` listing **all** posts; renders via `_includes/postslist.njk:2`, which does `postslist | reverse` (collections sort ascending by date, so the reverse yields newest-first).
- `content/index.njk:1` — home uses `head(-3)` (the `slice(-3)` branch of the config filter → the 3 newest posts).
- `content/tag-pages.njk:1-11` — paginates over `collections`, filters out `all` and `posts`; both real posts carry only the `posts` tag, so **no tag pages are generated today**.
- `content/feed.xml.njk:5` — all posts, newest-first; `content/sitemap.xml.njk:1` — every URL from `collections.all`.
- `content/posts/` — only 2 real posts (2026-01-01, 2026-01-02), so the real-content archive is a single page; multi-page boundaries cannot be exercised by repo content alone.
- `tests/archive-output.test.js:1` — comment-only stub; zero tests currently collect.
- Eleventy `^3.0.0`, `node --test` harness; devDependencies are not yet installed in this workspace (no `node_modules`/lockfile).

### Approach

1. **Archive pagination** — turn `content/blog.njk` into an Eleventy pagination template: `pagination.data: collections.posts`, `size: 20`, `reverse: true` so page 0 is the 20 newest posts (newest-first across pages, satisfying `ARCHIVE-2`/`ARCHIVE-3`). Permalink stays exactly `/blog/` for page 0 and appends the approved pattern for later pages using `pagination.pageNumber`.
2. **Reusing the shared include** — `postslist.njk` reverses its input, so the archive passes `pagination.items | reverse` (oldest-first within the chunk) and the include's reverse restores newest-first on-page. This leaves `postslist.njk` untouched, so home and tag rendering are untouched (`ARCHIVE-5`).
3. **Navigation** — render previous/next from `pagination.href.previous` / `pagination.href.next` guarded by `{% if %}`, so links appear only when the destination exists: first page → next only, middle → both, last → previous only, single-page build → neither (`ARCHIVE-4`). Markup per the approved presentation below; static anchors only (`ARCHIVE-6`).
4. **Evidence** — `tests/archive-output.test.js` runs the real Eleventy production build twice: (a) real content — regression checks on all protected surfaces; (b) a temp copy of the repo plus generated dated posts (e.g. 45, tagged only `posts`) to exercise first/middle/last pages.

### Material decisions requiring your approval

1. **Stable URL pattern for later pages** (`ARCHIVE-1` requirement question — blocks implementation):
   - **Recommended: `/blog/page/2/`, `/blog/page/3/`, …** (self-describing, conventional)
   - Alternative: `/blog/2/`, `/blog/3/`, …
2. **Navigation presentation** (design decision): recommended a `<nav aria-label="Blog archive pages">` landmark with text-only links (`rel="prev"/"next"`), labeled **"Newer posts" / "Older posts"** to avoid "previous/next" ambiguity on a newest-first archive — or plain "Previous"/"Next" if you prefer. Zero JavaScript either way.

### Acceptance evidence

- `ARCHIVE-1`: real build has `_site/blog/index.html` as page 1; synthetic build produces later pages only at the approved pattern.
- `ARCHIVE-2`: per-page post count ≤ 20 (expected 20/20/5 in the synthetic build).
- `ARCHIVE-3`: generated-output membership/order check — post URLs collected across all archive pages in render order are strictly newest-first with no duplicates.
- `ARCHIVE-4`: nav presence/absence asserted at each boundary; link targets resolve to existing pages.
- `ARCHIVE-5`: real-content build regression checks — home list, feed entries (all posts newest-first), sitemap URLs, absence of tag pages, and individual post pages unchanged.
- `ARCHIVE-6`: generated archive HTML contains no `<script>`; navigation is plain anchors.
- Run via `npm test` (`node --test tests/*.test.js`) with the production build actually executed; clean collect and exit.

### Documentation

`README.md` gets a one-line update describing the later-page URL pattern once approved (new public claim kept in the same change that makes it true). `docs/development/index.md` stays as-is (still no pagination specification exists). No new doc structure.

### Risks

- Pagination `reverse` chunking vs. `postslist`'s own `| reverse` interplay could yield wrong order if the semantics differ from expectation — contained by the `ARCHIVE-3` order check.
- Eleventy 3 pagination permalink/href null-safety edge cases — `{% if %}` guards cover null and undefined; verified by build.
- Verification requires installing devDependencies; any incidental lockfile/build artifacts stay out of the change unless you want them committed.

### Exclusions

No client-side JavaScript, no new dependencies, no behavior or markup changes to home/tags/feed/sitemap/post pages, no changes to the two real posts, no documentation restructuring.

---

**Exclusions.** No ORM/schema changes beyond the select construction, no client package/CLI work (none present), no new spec pages, no placeholder docs.

Per your instruction I have not modified any files, including the task file — the Draft plan below is presented here only. Execution waits for your approval.

---

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

**Outcome.** `GET /notes/` accepts optional, validated `limit` and `offset` query controls; requests that supply either parameter receive a stable ascending-ID slice of notes with the total collection count exposed in a response header. Requests without parameters behave exactly as today (full array). All other routes keep their current behavior.

**Approach.** Add FastAPI `Query` validation on the collection route and branch at the route layer: when both parameters are absent, call the existing `crud.get_all()` unchanged (strict NOTES-2 preservation, no new COUNT query on that path); when either is supplied, call a new paginated CRUD function that orders by `notes.c.id` ascending, applies `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` conditionally (no limit clause when only `offset` is given), computes the total with `SELECT count(*)`, and sets the total header on the response. Exact query construction stays flexible per the task file.

**Scope boundaries.**
- In scope: `src/app/api/notes.py` (collection route only), `src/app/api/crud.py` (add functions; change nothing existing), `src/tests/test_notes.py` (new focused tests), `README.md` (one short paragraph on the new controls).
- Out of scope: client packages/CLIs (none in this variant), new spec pages, OpenAPI generation config, `pyproject.toml` changes (pytest is installed into the venv only).

**Tasks.**
1. Set up execution environment: create a venv with `uv`, install `databases[sqlite]`, `fastapi`, `httpx`, `sqlalchemy`, plus `pytest`; run the existing suite from a temporary working directory (`PYTHONPATH=src`) so `notes.db` stays out of the repo; record baseline pass.
2. Add `crud.get_page(limit, offset)` (conditional limit clause, `.order_by(notes.c.id.asc())`, offset applied) and `crud.count_notes()` via `select(func.count())`.
3. Modify `read_all_notes` to take `limit`/`offset` as validated optional query params plus a `Response` parameter, branch between the legacy and paginated paths, and set the total header on paginated responses.
4. Add tests (see verification below), deriving expected slices dynamically from a full-list fetch so persistent/foreign rows in `notes.db` can't break assertions.
5. Extend README.md with the new optional controls, validation bounds, header, and the unchanged unparameterized behavior.
6. Run the full suite; clean any incidental artifacts.

**Risks.**
- `notes.db` persists across runs and tests already write rows; mitigated by dynamic expectations and running from a temp CWD.
- `databases` returns `Record` objects; count handling must read the scalar (`row[0]`).
- The header name and limit cap are new public contract details — resolved via the questions below, not unilaterally.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

1. **Requirement question (flagged in the task file): behavior when only one parameter is supplied.** Recommendation: conventional LIMIT/OFFSET semantics — missing `offset` means 0, missing `limit` means "rest of the list"; any supplied parameter activates the paginated path. Please confirm or choose "require both."
2. **Open question: bounds for the "bounded" query.** The task prescribes bounded and validated controls but no numbers. Recommendation: `limit` with `ge=1, le=100`, `offset` with `ge=0`; out-of-range/non-integer values fail with normal FastAPI 422 validation (satisfies NOTES-5). The cap value (100) and whether `limit=0` is invalid need your approval.
3. **Minor, reversible: header name and emission scope.** Recommendation: `X-Total-Count`, emitted only on paginated responses (keeps the unparameterized path bit-for-bit identical; NOTES-4 requires it only there). Alternative: emit on all collection responses for a single uniform contract, at the cost of an extra COUNT query and a (compatible, additive) change to unparameterized responses.
4. Resolved locally (reversible): branch in the route rather than rerouting unparameterized traffic through the ordered query, so NOTES-2 is preserved exactly rather than merely behaviorally.

### Documentation

Audience: API users/consumers of the notes service. Update `README.md` (the maintained user-facing doc for this service) with the optional parameters, validation bounds, `X-Total-Count` header, and the preserved full-array behavior for unparameterized requests, kept in the same change as the code. No new pages or directories; `docs/development/index.md` remains accurate ("No notes-query specification exists"). FastAPI's auto-generated OpenAPI picks up the new params automatically with no maintained source to change.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Task 1: venv + deps + pytest installed; baseline suite run passes from temp CWD.
- [ ] Task 2: `crud.get_page` and count support added; existing CRUD functions unchanged.
- [ ] Task 3: collection route accepts validated `limit`/`offset`, branches, sets total header on paginated responses.
- [ ] Task 4: new focused tests added and passing.
- [ ] Task 5: README.md updated in the same change.
- [ ] Task 6: full suite passes; working tree contains only intended changes.

### Requirement verification

Evidence boundary for all requirements: FastAPI `TestClient` against the real app — the public HTTP boundary with routing, validation, and serialization in the loop, backed by real SQLite through `databases` (integration-level; no mocks bypassing behavior).

| Requirement | Evidence |
|---|---|
| NOTES-1 | Test asserts a valid `limit`/`offset` request returns 200 with exactly the requested slice. |
| NOTES-2 | Test creates notes, then asserts unparameterized `GET /notes/` returns the full set as a plain JSON array (extends the existing array-shape test). |
| NOTES-3 | Test asserts paginated slice contents equal the corresponding window of the ascending-ID-sorted full list. |
| NOTES-4 | Test asserts a paginated response body is a JSON array and its total header equals the full collection count (cross-checked against the unparameterized list length). |
| NOTES-5 | Tests assert 422 for non-integer values, negative values, and out-of-bounds `limit` (bounds per approved question 2). |
| NOTES-6 | New compact create → item-read → update → delete round-trip test (no existing coverage proves these routes) plus the pre-existing tests passing unchanged. |

### Additional implementation verification

Confirm `/openapi.json` advertises the two new optional parameters (cheap check that the public contract is machine-visible). No other distinct material risks identified; no gated tests are declared in this fixture.

Implement optional pagination for `GET /notes/` while preserving the existing unparameterized collection response and all item-level CRUD behavior.

- What should happen when only one pagination parameter is supplied?

- What exact validation bounds should apply?

- What exact response-header name should carry the total count?
  - Recommended default: `X-Total-Count`.
- Should the total-count header appear only on paginated requests, or also on unparameterized collection requests?

These are public API decisions and should not be inferred during implementation. The plan remains Draft until they are confirmed.

## Draft implementation plan — Add Accessible Archive Pagination

**Task file:** `tasks/20260919-tg01-eleventy-archive-handoff.md` (plan unchanged, still `Draft`)

### Outcome

Convert the blog archive into bounded static pages (≤ 20 posts each, newest-first, each post exactly once) with boundary-aware previous/next navigation, while `/blog/` stays the first page and home, tags, feed, sitemap, and post pages keep their current output. No client-side JavaScript anywhere.

### Current state (inspection findings)

- `content/blog.njk:1-7` — single page at `permalink: /blog/` listing **all** posts; renders via `_includes/postslist.njk:2`, which does `postslist | reverse` (collections sort ascending by date, so the reverse yields newest-first).
- `content/index.njk:1` — home uses `head(-3)` (the `slice(-3)` branch of the config filter → the 3 newest posts).
- `content/tag-pages.njk:1-11` — paginates over `collections`, filters out `all` and `posts`; both real posts carry only the `posts` tag, so **no tag pages are generated today**.
- `content/feed.xml.njk:5` — all posts, newest-first; `content/sitemap.xml.njk:1` — every URL from `collections.all`.
- `content/posts/` — only 2 real posts (2026-01-01, 2026-01-02), so the real-content archive is a single page; multi-page boundaries cannot be exercised by repo content alone.
- `tests/archive-output.test.js:1` — comment-only stub; zero tests currently collect.
- Eleventy `^3.0.0`, `node --test` harness; devDependencies are not yet installed in this workspace (no `node_modules`/lockfile).

### Approach

1. **Archive pagination** — turn `content/blog.njk` into an Eleventy pagination template: `pagination.data: collections.posts`, `size: 20`, `reverse: true` so page 0 is the 20 newest posts (newest-first across pages, satisfying `ARCHIVE-2`/`ARCHIVE-3`). Permalink stays exactly `/blog/` for page 0 and appends the approved pattern for later pages using `pagination.pageNumber`.
2. **Reusing the shared include** — `postslist.njk` reverses its input, so the archive passes `pagination.items | reverse` (oldest-first within the chunk) and the include's reverse restores newest-first on-page. This leaves `postslist.njk` untouched, so home and tag rendering are untouched (`ARCHIVE-5`).
3. **Navigation** — render previous/next from `pagination.href.previous` / `pagination.href.next` guarded by `{% if %}`, so links appear only when the destination exists: first page → next only, middle → both, last → previous only, single-page build → neither (`ARCHIVE-4`). Markup per the approved presentation below; static anchors only (`ARCHIVE-6`).
4. **Evidence** — `tests/archive-output.test.js` runs the real Eleventy production build twice: (a) real content — regression checks on all protected surfaces; (b) a temp copy of the repo plus generated dated posts (e.g. 45, tagged only `posts`) to exercise first/middle/last pages.

### Material decisions requiring your approval

1. **Stable URL pattern for later pages** (`ARCHIVE-1` requirement question — blocks implementation):
   - **Recommended: `/blog/page/2/`, `/blog/page/3/`, …** (self-describing, conventional)
   - Alternative: `/blog/2/`, `/blog/3/`, …
2. **Navigation presentation** (design decision): recommended a `<nav aria-label="Blog archive pages">` landmark with text-only links (`rel="prev"/"next"`), labeled **"Newer posts" / "Older posts"** to avoid "previous/next" ambiguity on a newest-first archive — or plain "Previous"/"Next" if you prefer. Zero JavaScript either way.

### Acceptance evidence

- `ARCHIVE-1`: real build has `_site/blog/index.html` as page 1; synthetic build produces later pages only at the approved pattern.
- `ARCHIVE-2`: per-page post count ≤ 20 (expected 20/20/5 in the synthetic build).
- `ARCHIVE-3`: generated-output membership/order check — post URLs collected across all archive pages in render order are strictly newest-first with no duplicates.
- `ARCHIVE-4`: nav presence/absence asserted at each boundary; link targets resolve to existing pages.
- `ARCHIVE-5`: real-content build regression checks — home list, feed entries (all posts newest-first), sitemap URLs, absence of tag pages, and individual post pages unchanged.
- `ARCHIVE-6`: generated archive HTML contains no `<script>`; navigation is plain anchors.
- Run via `npm test` (`node --test tests/*.test.js`) with the production build actually executed; clean collect and exit.

### Documentation

`README.md` gets a one-line update describing the later-page URL pattern once approved (new public claim kept in the same change that makes it true). `docs/development/index.md` stays as-is (still no pagination specification exists). No new doc structure.

### Risks

- Pagination `reverse` chunking vs. `postslist`'s own `| reverse` interplay could yield wrong order if the semantics differ from expectation — contained by the `ARCHIVE-3` order check.
- Eleventy 3 pagination permalink/href null-safety edge cases — `{% if %}` guards cover null and undefined; verified by build.
- Verification requires installing devDependencies; any incidental lockfile/build artifacts stay out of the change unless you want them committed.

### Exclusions

No client-side JavaScript, no new dependencies, no behavior or markup changes to home/tags/feed/sitemap/post pages, no changes to the two real posts, no documentation restructuring.

---

task_files.tasks/20260919-blog-archive-pagination.m:
# Blog archive pagination

Split the blog archive so `/blog/` stays the first archive page while stable
later pages carry at most twenty posts each, with accessible previous/next
navigation. Preserve the home page, tags, feed, sitemap, individual post
pages, post order, and static zero-JavaScript output. Planning only:
execution has not been approved.

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] 1. `/blog/` remains the first archive page at the same URL and continues
      to show posts newest-first, now limited to at most 20 posts.
- [ ] 2. Later archive pages are statically generated at stable, deterministic
      URLs, each containing at most 20 posts and continuing the same
      newest-first sequence. Stable means deterministic chunking from an
      explicit total order (date descending, deterministic tiebreak for equal
      dates): identical inputs produce identical pages.
- [ ] 3. Every archive page offers accessible previous/next navigation to the
      adjacent archive pages: a labeled `<nav>` with descriptive links, a link
      rendered only where an adjacent page exists, keyboard operable by
      default, no JavaScript.
- [ ] 4. Home page, tag pages, feed, and individual post pages keep their
      current URLs and output.
- [ ] 5. The sitemap remains valid and continues to enumerate the built public
      pages, including the generated archive pages.
- [ ] 6. Build output remains static files with zero client-side JavaScript.
- [ ] 7. Maintained documentation (README plus the development docs) reflects
      the paginated archive in the same change.

## Open questions

- Q1 (user-visible URLs, requirement-relevant): scheme for the later archive
  pages. Recommendation: one-based numbering, `/blog/2/`, `/blog/3/`, … via
  the documented conditional permalink. Eleventy's default pagination URLs
  would place the second page at `/blog/1/` (0-indexed), which reads as page
  "1" while being the second page. The choice changes shipped URLs and needs
  approval before implementation.
- Q2 (sitemap scope, clarification): generated archive pages will appear in
  the sitemap automatically because `content/sitemap.xml.njk` enumerates
  `collections.all`. Recommendation: keep that behavior (they are public
  indexable pages). Excluding them would require an extra filter and is not
  planned unless requested.

## Supporting details

- Eleventy ^3.0.0 (`package.json`); `eleventy.config.js` sets input
  `content/`, includes `../_includes`, output `_site/`; `npm run build` runs
  `eleventy`; `npm test` runs `node --test tests/*.test.js`. Dependencies are
  not installed in this workspace (`node_modules/` absent, gitignored).
- Current archive: `content/blog.njk` has `permalink: /blog/` and renders all
  of `collections.posts` through `_includes/postslist.njk`, which renders
  `postslist | reverse` (newest-first display; collections are
  date-ascending).
- Content: two posts (`content/posts/first.md` dated 2026-01-01, `second.md`
  dated 2026-01-02) tagged `posts` via `content/posts/posts.json`, layout
  `_includes/layouts/post.njk` (no per-post prev/next links exist today, so
  "individual-post navigation" means their current rendering stays as is).
  Post URLs are `/posts/first/`, `/posts/second/`, so `/blog/<n>/` cannot
  collide with post URLs.
- Other surfaces: `content/index.njk` shows the 3 newest posts (`head(-3)`);
  `content/tag-pages.njk` paginates over `collections` with
  `filter: [all, posts]`; `content/feed.xml.njk` lists all posts;
  `content/sitemap.xml.njk` enumerates `collections.all`.
- `tests/archive-output.test.js` contains only a comment ("Production-build
  coverage currently checks only that /blog/index.html exists.") — there are
  no actual assertions today, so real coverage must be written, not extended
  in place.
- `docs/development/index.md` states "No archive pagination specification
  exists."; there is no `docs/index.md`.
- Verified against the Eleventy 3 docs (11ty.dev/docs/pagination):
  - `pagination.reverse: true` reverses the whole data set before chunking, so
    page 1 holds the newest items of a date-ascending collection.
  - Default pagination URLs append a 0-indexed number for later pages
    (`_site/paged/index.html` and `_site/paged/1/index.html` in the docs
    example); a conditional permalink
    (`{% if pagination.pageNumber > 0 %}…{% endif %}`) keeps page 1 at its
    original URL while numbering later pages; in Nunjucks
    `{{ pagination.pageNumber + 1 }}` works (the Liquid caveat does not
    apply).
  - `pagination.href.previous` / `pagination.href.next` give adjacent page
    URLs (absent when there is no adjacent page); `pagination.items` is the
    current chunk (an array when size > 1); `pagination.pages` lists all
    chunks in order.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Approach:

1. Install dependencies (`npm install`) and confirm the production build
   succeeds on the unchanged site.
2. Convert `content/blog.njk` into a pagination template: pagination over the
   posts collection, `size: 20`, an alias for the current chunk (not `page`,
   which is reserved), and a conditional permalink so page 1 keeps `/blog/`
   and later pages become `/blog/2/`, `/blog/3/`, … (Q1).
3. Ordering (D2): paginate over an explicitly sorted copied collection added
   in `eleventy.config.js` via `addCollection` — posts sorted date
   descending with `inputPath` as the tiebreak for equal dates, paginated
   with `reverse: false`. Page 1 then holds the 20 newest posts and page
   boundaries are deterministic even for same-date posts. Alternative with
   confirmed semantics: `pagination.reverse: true` directly over
   `collections.posts`, accepting the default tiebreak; acceptable only if
   the same-date determinism test passes.
4. Keep `_includes/postslist.njk` unchanged (shared with home and tag pages).
   Because the include renders `postslist | reverse`, the archive sets
   `postslist` to the current chunk pre-reversed so the display stays
   newest-first; add a comment explaining the paired reversals and confirm
   the order from build output rather than reasoning alone.
5. Add the navigation to `content/blog.njk` after the post list: a
   `<nav aria-label="…">` containing "Newer posts" / "Older posts" links
   bound to `pagination.href.previous` / `pagination.href.next`, each
   rendered only when the href exists (no dead links), plus a "Page X of Y"
   indicator (D3). No scripts.
6. Change nothing else: `content/index.njk`, `content/tag-pages.njk`,
   `content/feed.xml.njk`, `content/sitemap.xml.njk`,
   `_includes/postslist.njk`, `_includes/layouts/post.njk`, and
   `content/posts/*` stay untouched. The new archive pages flow into
   `collections.all` — and therefore the sitemap — automatically.
7. Write the verification below, update README and the development docs in
   the same change, then keep this task file current while executing.

Boundaries:

- Only the blog archive pagination and its navigation; tag pagination, feed,
  sitemap and post templates, and post content are out of scope.
- No client-side JavaScript; no new build tooling beyond the config change
  needed for ordering.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- D1 (Q1, needs approval): later-page URL scheme — recommendation
  `/blog/{N}/` one-based (`/blog/2/` is the second page), implemented with
  the documented conditional permalink. Tradeoff: the Eleventy default needs
  no permalink logic but numbers pages 0-indexed (`/blog/1/` second);
  `/blog/page-2/` is equally valid if preferred. No other URL conflicts
  exist in this site.
- D2 (local, reversible): ordering mechanism — explicit derived collection
  (recommended, pins the same-date tiebreak) vs `pagination.reverse: true`
  over the default collection. Both put the newest posts on page 1.
- D3 (local, reversible): "Page X of Y" indicator — recommended, because
  landing on `/blog/3/` with only prev/next links gives little orientation;
  executor may include or omit without changing requirements.
- D4 (local, reversible): navigation labels — "Newer posts" / "Older posts"
  recommended; more meaningful than "Previous"/"Next" without page context.
- Pending resolution of Q1/Q2 the plan stays in `Draft`; implementation
  waits for approval.

### Documentation

- `README.md`: extend the existing build-output sentence with the paginated
  archive (at most 20 posts per page, previous/next links, no JavaScript) so
  the public claim ships in the same change as the behavior.
- `docs/development`: replace the "No archive pagination specification
  exists." line in `docs/development/index.md` with a short specification of
  the archive pagination contract (page size, URL scheme, ordering,
  navigation markup, zero-JS). Recommendation: a small dedicated page (e.g.
  `docs/development/archive-pagination.md`) linked from the index; inlining
  it in the index is acceptable if fewer files are preferred. Audience:
  maintainers. Describes shipped behavior only.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Install dependencies and verify `npm run build` succeeds on the
      unchanged site.
- [ ] Resolve Q1 (later-page URL scheme) and D2 (ordering mechanism).
- [ ] Implement pagination in `content/blog.njk` (plus the derived collection
      in `eleventy.config.js` if D2 resolves that way).
- [ ] Implement the accessible previous/next navigation markup.
- [ ] Build and inspect `_site/` output (archive pages, sitemap, feed) as a
      sanity check.
- [ ] Replace the placeholder in `tests/archive-output.test.js` with the
      integration coverage described under Requirement verification.
- [ ] Update `README.md` and the development docs in the same change.
- [ ] Record requirement evidence and progress here (Implementation Notes
      while executing; Completion Notes at the end).

### Requirement verification

- R1, R2 (archive pages, order, size, stability): integration test at the
  real build boundary — run the same production build command against a
  temporary copy of the site seeded with generated posts (distinct dates,
  plus same-date posts to pin the tiebreak), then assert on emitted files:
  `/blog/index.html` holds the 20 newest posts newest-first; later pages at
  the approved URLs hold the next chunks in order, each ≤ 20 posts; two
  builds of identical input emit byte-identical archive pages. Also assert
  the production two-post content still builds to a single `/blog/` page
  holding both posts with no navigation (feature dormant at current size).
- R3 (navigation): assertions on the emitted archive HTML: labeled `<nav>`;
  "Newer posts"/"Older posts" links with correct hrefs; a link exists only
  where an adjacent page exists (page 1 lacks "Newer posts", last page lacks
  "Older posts"); no `<script>` elements. Structural accessibility of real
  links is the evidence boundary; no screen-reader audit is planned.
- R4 (preserved surfaces): build before and after the change from identical
  input (temp site copies) and byte-compare the emitted home, tag, feed, and
  post files; alternatively pin their content with explicit assertions.
  Byte-identical output is the strongest evidence and cheap here.
- R5 (sitemap): assert the emitted sitemap contains every archive page URL
  and still contains all other public URLs.
- R6 (zero-JS): scan all emitted HTML for `<script` (and inline event
  handler attributes if cheap); expect none.
- R7 (documentation): reviewed during execution; final confirmation is the
  reviewer's read of the shipped docs.

### Additional implementation verification

- Pagination edge sizes in the test data: exactly 20 posts (single page, no
  navigation) and 21 posts (two pages; second page holds one post).
- Run the full `npm test` suite and confirm it collects the new tests and
  exits cleanly.

Plan the migration of the Eleventy blog archive from one unbounded page to a
stable, paginated archive while preserving the existing public output and
static-site behavior.

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] Keep `/blog/` as the first archive page and preserve the archive's
  existing post order.
- [ ] Generate stable later archive pages with no more than twenty posts per
  page.
- [ ] Add accessible previous/next navigation that exposes only the links
  valid for the current page.
- [ ] Preserve the home page, tag pages, feed, sitemap, individual-post
  routes/navigation, and post order.
- [ ] Keep the generated site usable without client-side JavaScript.

## Scope

This handoff covers archive pagination generation, archive-page navigation,
production-build regression coverage, and the small amount of developer
documentation needed to describe the supported archive URL behavior. It does
not change post content, collection semantics, the home-page post count, tag
page pagination, feed format, sitemap format, or individual-post templates
except where verification demonstrates an accidental regression.

## Findings (grounding the plan)

- **Regression**: `client/src/components/Books.vue:32,36,40` — `add`, `update`, `remove` each call `getBooks()` with no argument, defaulting to `"all"`. The selected `selectedFilter` state stays active on the buttons, so the UI shows an active filter over unfiltered results — inconsistent (REFRESH-1, REFRESH-3).
- **No other changes needed**: `client/src/api/books.js:3-6` already encodes `all`→no params, `read/unread`→`?read=true|false`, and `server/app.py:15-19` already filters on that param. `REFRESH-2` is therefore satisfied by having the mutation refreshes reuse the existing production path — the fix is confined to `Books.vue`.
- **Current test coverage**: the component test mocks the entire api module (`client/tests/Books.spec.js:5-10`) and only asserts an empty state; pytest covers CRUD status codes only — nothing covers the `read` filter in either suite.
- **Environment**: Python 3.12 / Node 20 available, but `flask`/`pytest` and `client/node_modules` are not installed — dependency setup is execution work, not planning work.

---

## Execution plan

**Status: Draft**

Fix the lost-filter regression so add/update/delete refreshes re-query with the currently selected filter through the existing production path, without changing any client-server contract. Scope: `client/src/components/Books.vue` plus tests; no changes to `client/src/api/books.js`, `client/src/http.js`, or `server/app.py`.

### Approach

- In `Books.vue`, add a shared `refreshBooks()` method that sets `this.books` from `getBooks(this.selectedFilter)`, and have `selectFilter`, `add`, `update`, and `remove` use it. `selectFilter`'s observable behavior is unchanged (it still sets the filter before refreshing); mutations stop discarding the filter. No error handling, caching, or client-side re-filtering is introduced — the refresh keeps crossing the real axios transport to the Flask route, which is what REFRESH-2 requires. With the initial `"all"` selection the refresh is unfiltered, identical to today's behavior.
- Verification is layered at the boundaries the requirements name:
  1. **Component tests** (vitest, mocked api module — cheap evidence for UI state and rendering): after `add`/`update`/`remove` with `unread` selected, `getBooks` receives `"unread"`; rendered rows match the mocked filtered responses; when a filtered list empties, the "No books found." empty state renders while the `unread` button stays `aria-pressed`. The existing empty-state test stays as the REFRESH-4 regression for the default mount path.
  2. **Server tests** (pytest): new read-only tests proving `GET /books?read=false` and `?read=true` return only matching books with the established `{"status", "books"}` shape, and unfiltered `GET /books` still returns both seeded books (REFRESH-2 server half, REFRESH-4). Strengthen the existing mutation test with response-shape assertions (POST→`books`, PUT/DELETE→`book`) rather than new tests.
  3. **Decisive integration test** for REFRESH-2/REFRESH-3 (new vitest file, e.g. `client/tests/Books.refresh.integration.spec.js`, no api mock): reserve a free port with a bound socket, spawn the real Flask app (`PYTHON` env var or `python3`, cwd = repo root, `python -c "from server.app import app; app.run(port=...)"`), point the shared axios instance's `baseURL` at it, wait for readiness, then mount `Books` with the **real** api module and drive one scenario through the real UI→transport→route→selection chain: select `unread` (only Dune), add an unread book (both appear), update it to read (it leaves the list), delete the remaining unread (empty state, `unread` still pressed). Assert button state and visible rows after each mutation. One test covers all three mutation kinds and the empty state.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- **Decision (local, reversible)**: implement the fix as a single `refreshBooks()` helper rather than three inline `getBooks(this.selectedFilter)` calls — one point of truth for the refresh, no behavior difference. Either form satisfies the requirements.
- **Decision (test infrastructure — flagging for approval, with my recommendation)**: the mocked-api component tests cannot prove REFRESH-2 (a mock at that seam supplies the claimed behavior, so it is not decisive). # Books CRUD refresh must preserve the selected filter

The Books page's All/Read/Unread filter is ignored when add, update, or delete
refresh the collection: the refetch always uses the unfiltered default. This
task plans the client-side fix so every CRUD refresh re-applies the active
filter while leaving the HTTP contract and unfiltered behavior untouched.
Planning only — no implementation performed for this task yet.

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] **R1 — CRUD refresh re-applies the selected filter.** After add, update,
  or delete, the collection refresh uses the currently selected filter
  (`all` / `read` / `unread`), so the visible list continues to reflect that
  filter instead of falling back to the unfiltered list. (Request: "reapply it
  whenever CRUD refreshes the collection".)
- [ ] **R2 — The selected filter stays visibly active.** Across CRUD
  refreshes, the filter control's pressed state keeps reflecting the user's
  selection (no reset to `all`) and the list content matches that selection.
  (Request: "Keep the selected filter visibly active".)
- [ ] **R3 — HTTP contract preserved.** Same endpoints and request semantics
  (`read=true` / `read=false` for filtered GETs, no query params for
  unfiltered GETs) and same `{status, books}` / `{status, book}` response
  shapes; `server/app.py` and the request mapping in
  `client/src/api/books.js` are not modified. (Request: "Preserve the existing
  API response shape".)
- [ ] **R4 — Unfiltered behavior preserved.** With All selected, add, update,
  and delete refreshes continue to display the full collection exactly as they
  do today. (Request: "Preserve … unfiltered behavior".)

Out of scope (not approved outcomes): initial-load fetch behavior (the
component fetches only on filter selection or after CRUD today), empty-state
copy, filter styling beyond the existing `aria-pressed` signal, and any server
behavior change.

## Open questions and decisions

- None unresolved. Two consequences follow directly from R1 and are treated as
  expected behavior, not bugs: a newly added or edited book that does not
  match the active filter does not appear until the filter changes, and
  deleting the last book matching an active filter shows the existing
  "No books found." empty state while the filter stays active.
- Interpretation note (flagged, not blocking): "visibly active" is taken to
  mean the existing `aria-pressed` signal keeps reflecting the selection — the
  fixture has no other pressed styling. Adding CSS-level selected styling
  would be new scope.

## Supporting details

- Defect location: `client/src/components/Books.vue:30-41` — `add`, `update`,
  and `remove` each perform the mutation, then refetch with `getBooks()`
  (default `"all"`), discarding the active filter. The code carries
  `// regression: filter lost` comments on all three call sites.
- The pressed state is not currently reset: `selectedFilter`
  (Books.vue:24) is only written by `selectFilter` (Books.vue:26-28). After a
  CRUD refresh the buttons keep showing the old selection via `aria-pressed`
  (Books.vue:3-12) while the table shows the unfiltered list — the defect is
  the list content, not the control state.
- Filter → request mapping (unchanged by this fix):
  `client/src/api/books.js:3-6` — `getBooks(filter = "all")`; `read` →
  `?read=true`, `unread` → `?read=false`, `all` → no params. Mutations: POST

- Server behavior (no change needed): `server/app.py:15-20` filters GET
  `/books` by the `read` arg only when it is `"true"`/`"false"`; POST returns
  `{"status": "success", "books": …}` (app.py:14); PUT/DELETE return
  `{"status": "success", "book": …}` (app.py:30).
- No lifecycle fetch: the component loads books only via `selectFilter` or a
  post-CRUD refresh; on mount it renders the empty state (exercised by
  `client/tests/Books.spec.js:13-17`). Changing this is out of scope.
- Existing tests: `client/tests/Books.spec.js` (vitest + @vue/test-utils, api
  module mocked at `../src/api/books`) and `tests/test_books_api.py` using the
  Flask test client from `tests/conftest.py`. Server tests currently assert
  status codes only — they do not pin the unfiltered response body or shape;
  the plan closes that gap with a small assertion.
- Component-level mock note: the refresh currently calls `getBooks()` with no
  argument; after the fix the All case calls `getBooks("all")` explicitly.
  Equivalent at the HTTP boundary (no params either way), but component-test
  mock assertions must expect the explicit `"all"` argument.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

### Approach

Collapse the four collection fetches in `Books.vue` onto a single path. Add a
`refreshBooks()` method that awaits `getBooks(this.selectedFilter)` and
assigns `this.books` from `response.data.books`. `selectFilter` sets
`selectedFilter` and then calls `refreshBooks()`; `add`, `update`, and
`remove` perform their mutation and then call `refreshBooks()`. Because the
api module already maps `"all"` to a parameterless GET, the All case issues a
byte-identical request to today's, satisfying R3 and R4 with no server
changes. `selectedFilter` is never reassigned by CRUD operations, so R2 holds
by construction, and the component tests pin it so a future refactor cannot
quietly reset it.

Evidence boundary: the changed logic is the component's refresh path, so the
decisive tests are component tests (vitest + @vue/test-utils) that mock the
api module at `../src/api/books` and assert both the filter argument passed to
`getBooks` and the rendered list. The api-module mapping and Flask routing are
unchanged code, evidenced on their own sides (file unchanged plus existing and
slightly strengthened Python tests).

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- Decision (resolved, local and reversible): route all four fetches through a
  shared `refreshBooks()` helper instead of editing the three CRUD call sites
  to pass the filter inline. One refresh path prevents the regression from
  recurring per-method; behavior is identical.
- Decision (resolved): pass `"all"` explicitly from the component rather than
  relying on the api module's default parameter, so the refresh path is
  uniform and mock assertions are deterministic. The HTTP request is
  unchanged (no params either way).
- No open questions; see the task's "Open questions and decisions" section for
  the flagged interpretation note about `aria-pressed` being the only pressed
  signal in this fixture.

### Documentation

- No maintained documentation describes the Books filter or CRUD-refresh
  behavior today; `docs/development/index.md` records that no book-discovery
  specification exists. The fix changes no public contract and introduces no
  new user-facing claim, so no documentation changes are planned.
- If a Books-page specification is added later, the filter-persistence
  behavior belongs there with the client package (audience: developers on
  this fixture; no new pages for this fix).

### Task checklist

- [ ] T1. `client/src/components/Books.vue`: add `refreshBooks()`; route
  `selectFilter`, `add`, `update`, and `remove` through it (mutation first,
  then refresh with the selected filter); remove the
  `// regression: filter lost` comments.
- [ ] T2. `client/tests/Books.spec.js`: give the `getBooks` mock per-call
  queued responses and add cases: (a) selecting a filter fetches and renders
  that filter's books; (b) after add, update, and remove the refetch uses the
  active filter and the list reflects the queued response; (c) `aria-pressed`
  stays on the active filter after each CRUD refresh; (d) with `all`
  selected, CRUD refetch calls `getBooks("all")` and renders the full list;
  (e) deleting the last matching book under an active filter renders
  "No books found." with the filter still pressed.
- [ ] T3. `tests/test_books_api.py`: extend `test_books` to assert the
  unfiltered GET returns both seed books inside
  `{"status": "success", "books": […]}` (pins shape and unfiltered
  semantics; assertions stay read-only because `BOOKS` is module-level shared
  state).
- [ ] T4. Run `npm test` in `client/` and `python -m pytest tests/`; record
  results in Implementation Notes and update this checklist as tasks
  complete.

### Requirement verification

- **R1** → T2(b): after `selectFilter("read")` / `selectFilter("unread")`,
  each CRUD operation causes `getBooks` to be called with that filter and the
  table renders the mocked filtered response. Decisive because the assertions
  cover the component's actual refresh call and rendered output; the api mock
  sits at the component's own boundary and does not bypass the changed logic.
- **R2** → T2(c): `aria-pressed` remains `"true"` on the selected button after
  each CRUD refresh, and no `getBooks("all")` call occurs while a real filter
  is selected.
- **R3** → diff review confirms `server/app.py` and the request mapping in
  `client/src/api/books.js` are untouched; T3 pins the unfiltered GET body and
  shape; the existing `test_book_mutations` still passes.
- **R4** → T2(d): with `all` selected, post-CRUD refetch calls
  `getBooks("all")` and renders the full list; the server half is evidenced by
  the T3 unfiltered-GET body assertion.

No requirement needs human-only verification; all are machine-checkable via
the component and Python test runs in T4.

### Additional implementation verification

- Residual seam gap (accepted, recorded): the component tests mock
  `../src/api/books`, so the full component → axios → Flask path is not
  exercised end-to-end, and the axios param mapping in `books.js` is covered
  by no automated test either before or after this fix. The fixture has no
  e2e/hosted harness; preservation of the mapping rests on non-modification,
  and the server tolerates any `read` value outside `true`/`false` as
  unfiltered. No new harness is to be built for this fix.
- Shared mutable state: `BOOKS` in `server/app.py` is module-level; keep new
  and extended server assertions read-only and order-independent.

  compatible.

## Supporting details

The public route is in `src/app/api/notes.py`; storage behavior is in
`src/app/api/crud.py`; current route coverage is in
`src/tests/test_notes.py`. Exact ORM/SQL construction is not prescribed.

question.

Inspect route and storage behavior, resolve omitted-companion semantics, add

I've read the task file and inspected the repository. Quick baseline facts before the plan:

- `GET /notes/` currently returns `crud.get_all()` — an unordered full-table fetch (src/app/api/notes.py:8). Other routes (item-read/update/delete in src/app/api/crud.py) are independent of the collection query.
- Coverage is thin: two tests, one asserting the array shape, one asserting 201 on create (src/tests/test_notes.py). No existing coverage proves item-read/update/delete behavior, so NOTES-6 needs focused evidence.

Per your instruction I have not modified any files, including the task file — the Draft plan below is presented here only. Execution waits for your approval.

---

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

**Outcome.** `GET /notes/` accepts optional, validated `limit` and `offset` query controls; requests that supply either parameter receive a stable ascending-ID slice of notes with the total collection count exposed in a response header. Requests without parameters behave exactly as today (full array). All other routes keep their current behavior.

**Approach.** Add FastAPI `Query` validation on the collection route and branch at the route layer: when both parameters are absent, call the existing `crud.get_all()` unchanged (strict NOTES-2 preservation, no new COUNT query on that path); when either is supplied, call a new paginated CRUD function that orders by `notes.c.id` ascending, applies `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` conditionally (no limit clause when only `offset` is given), computes the total with `SELECT count(*)`, and sets the total header on the response. Exact query construction stays flexible per the task file.

**Scope boundaries.**
- In scope: `src/app/api/notes.py` (collection route only), `src/app/api/crud.py` (add functions; change nothing existing), `src/tests/test_notes.py` (new focused tests), `README.md` (one short paragraph on the new controls).
- Out of scope: client packages/CLIs (none in this variant), new spec pages, OpenAPI generation config, `pyproject.toml` changes (pytest is installed into the venv only).

**Tasks.**
1. Set up execution environment: create a venv with `uv`, install `databases[sqlite]`, `fastapi`, `httpx`, `sqlalchemy`, plus `pytest`; run the existing suite from a temporary working directory (`PYTHONPATH=src`) so `notes.db` stays out of the repo; record baseline pass.
2. Add `crud.get_page(limit, offset)` (conditional limit clause, `.order_by(notes.c.id.asc())`, offset applied) and `crud.count_notes()` via `select(func.count())`.
3. Modify `read_all_notes` to take `limit`/`offset` as validated optional query params plus a `Response` parameter, branch between the legacy and paginated paths, and set the total header on paginated responses.
4. Add tests (see verification below), deriving expected slices dynamically from a full-list fetch so persistent/foreign rows in `notes.db` can't break assertions.
5. Extend README.md with the new optional controls, validation bounds, header, and the unchanged unparameterized behavior.
6. Run the full suite; clean any incidental artifacts.

**Risks.**
- `notes.db` persists across runs and tests already write rows; mitigated by dynamic expectations and running from a temp CWD.
- `databases` returns `Record` objects; count handling must read the scalar (`row[0]`).
- The header name and limit cap are new public contract details — resolved via the questions below, not unilaterally.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

1. **Requirement question (flagged in the task file): behavior when only one parameter is supplied.** Recommendation: conventional LIMIT/OFFSET semantics — missing `offset` means 0, missing `limit` means "rest of the list"; any supplied parameter activates the paginated path. Please confirm or choose "require both."
2. **Open question: bounds for the "bounded" query.** The task prescribes bounded and validated controls but no numbers. Recommendation: `limit` with `ge=1, le=100`, `offset` with `ge=0`; out-of-range/non-integer values fail with normal FastAPI 422 validation (satisfies NOTES-5). The cap value (100) and whether `limit=0` is invalid need your approval.
3. **Minor, reversible: header name and emission scope.** Recommendation: `X-Total-Count`, emitted only on paginated responses (keeps the unparameterized path bit-for-bit identical; NOTES-4 requires it only there). Alternative: emit on all collection responses for a single uniform contract, at the cost of an extra COUNT query and a (compatible, additive) change to unparameterized responses.
4. Resolved locally (reversible): branch in the route rather than rerouting unparameterized traffic through the ordered query, so NOTES-2 is preserved exactly rather than merely behaviorally.

### Documentation

Audience: API users/consumers of the notes service. Update `README.md` (the maintained user-facing doc for this service) with the optional parameters, validation bounds, `X-Total-Count` header, and the preserved full-array behavior for unparameterized requests, kept in the same change as the code. No new pages or directories; `docs/development/index.md` remains accurate ("No notes-query specification exists"). FastAPI's auto-generated OpenAPI picks up the new params automatically with no maintained source to change.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Task 1: venv + deps + pytest installed; baseline suite run passes from temp CWD.
- [ ] Task 2: `crud.get_page` and count support added; existing CRUD functions unchanged.
- [ ] Task 3: collection route accepts validated `limit`/`offset`, branches, sets total header on paginated responses.
- [ ] Task 4: new focused tests added and passing.
- [ ] Task 5: README.md updated in the same change.
- [ ] Task 6: full suite passes; working tree contains only intended changes.

### Requirement verification

Evidence boundary for all requirements: FastAPI `TestClient` against the real app — the public HTTP boundary with routing, validation, and serialization in the loop, backed by real SQLite through `databases` (integration-level; no mocks bypassing behavior).

| Requirement | Evidence |
|---|---|
| NOTES-1 | Test asserts a valid `limit`/`offset` request returns 200 with exactly the requested slice. |
| NOTES-2 | Test creates notes, then asserts unparameterized `GET /notes/` returns the full set as a plain JSON array (extends the existing array-shape test). |
| NOTES-3 | Test asserts paginated slice contents equal the corresponding window of the ascending-ID-sorted full list. |
| NOTES-4 | Test asserts a paginated response body is a JSON array and its total header equals the full collection count (cross-checked against the unparameterized list length). |
| NOTES-5 | Tests assert 422 for non-integer values, negative values, and out-of-bounds `limit` (bounds per approved question 2). |
| NOTES-6 | New compact create → item-read → update → delete round-trip test (no existing coverage proves these routes) plus the pre-existing tests passing unchanged. |

### Additional implementation verification

Confirm `/openapi.json` advertises the two new optional parameters (cheap check that the public contract is machine-visible). No other distinct material risks identified; no gated tests are declared in this fixture.

# Add optional limit/offset pagination to GET /notes/

Planning handoff for adding optional `limit`/`offset` pagination to the notes
collection route: a bounded ascending-ID slice on request, the total note count
in a response header, unchanged full-list behavior without pagination,
standard FastAPI validation for bad values, and no changes to the other CRUD
routes. Planning only — implementation has not been approved or started.

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] R1 — `GET /notes/` accepts optional `limit` and `offset` query parameters; a paginated request returns a bounded slice of notes ordered by ascending `id`, as a bare JSON array with the same per-note shape as today.
- [ ] R2 — A paginated response carries the total note count in a response header (total = count of all notes in the table, not the remaining window; header name and presence scope per Q1/D1 below).
- [ ] R3 — A request without pagination parameters returns the current full-list JSON array, unchanged.
- [ ] R4 — Invalid `limit`/`offset` values (negative, non-integer) are rejected by FastAPI's standard validation (422); no custom validation code.
- [ ] R5 — All other routes (`POST /notes/`, `GET /notes/{note_id}/`, `PUT /notes/{note_id}/`, `DELETE /notes/{note_id}/`) keep their current behavior.
- [ ] R6 — `README.md` documents the changed collection behavior in the same reviewed change (AGENTS.md documentation policy).

## Open requirement questions (block execution)

- Q1 — Header presence scope: only on paginated responses, or on every `GET /notes/` response? Recommendation: paginated-only, so unpaginated responses stay byte-identical to today (strictest reading of R3) and every paginating client still receives the total.
- Q3 — Mixed parameter presence: either parameter alone triggers pagination (missing `offset` defaults to 0, missing `limit` means no upper bound), or both must be supplied together (422 otherwise). Recommendation: per-parameter defaults — simplest coherent contract; a lone `offset` returns the ascending tail.

## Supporting facts

- Routes live in `src/app/api/notes.py`; the router is mounted with prefix `/notes` (`src/app/main.py:15`). `GET /notes/` currently returns `await crud.get_all()` with no parameters, no `response_model`, and no headers (`src/app/api/notes.py:8-10`).
- `crud.get_all()` runs `database.fetch_all(notes.select())` with no explicit ORDER BY (`src/app/api/crud.py:4-5`). Other crud functions: `get`, `post`, `put`, `delete` (`src/app/api/crud.py:8-26`). CRUD route handlers take no query parameters.
- Data layer: `databases` async wrapper over SQLAlchemy Core against a SQLite file `./notes.db`, created at import time via `metadata.create_all(engine)` (`src/app/db.py`). Table columns: `id` (PK), `title`, `description`.
- Tests: `src/tests/test_notes.py` has two tests (full list → 200 + list; POST → 201). `src/tests/conftest.py` exposes a `test_app` fixture returning `TestClient(app)` without a context manager.
- Verified 2026-09-19 in a temporary venv (deps installed there, since removed; workspace untouched): with fastapi 0.141.1, starlette 1.6.0, databases 0.9.0, sqlalchemy 2.0.54, pydantic 2.13.5, Python 3.12 — the existing suite passes (2 passed) without lifespan running, because databases 0.9.0's SQLite backend connects lazily (`SQLiteBackend.connect()` is a no-op; the pool opens a connection per query). This variant has no client package or CLI.

Status: Draft

Approach: keep the existing unpaginated code path untouched and add a paginated branch to the same route handler.

# Add optional pagination to the notes collection

Plan the `GET /notes/` enhancement so clients can request a bounded,
ascending-ID slice while preserving the existing collection response for
requests that do not use pagination. This task covers the HTTP behavior,
regression evidence, and the maintained API documentation; it does not
authorize implementation yet.

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] `GET /notes/` accepts optional `limit` and `offset` query parameters.
- [ ] A request using pagination returns notes as a bounded slice ordered by
      ascending note ID.
- [ ] A paginated response exposes the total number of notes in a response
      header.
- [ ] A request without pagination parameters keeps the current full-list JSON
      array behavior.
- [ ] Invalid pagination values are rejected by FastAPI's normal query
      validation and produce its standard validation response.
- [ ] The create, read-one, update, and delete routes retain their current
      behavior.

## Scope

This is a single deliverable at the public HTTP boundary. It includes focused
route-level integration tests and an update to the existing README. It does not
introduce a new response envelope, client package, CLI behavior, or unrelated
CRUD changes.

## Unresolved requirement questions

These choices affect the public contract and should be confirmed before
execution:

1. What exact response-header name should carry the total? Recommendation:
   `X-Total-Count`, unless the project has an external naming convention.
2. What validation bounds are required? The usual contract is
   `limit >= 1` and `offset >= 0`; the request does not specify whether
   `limit=0` is valid or whether there is a maximum limit.
3. When only one parameter is supplied, should the route paginate using the
   other parameter's default (`offset` alone skips, `limit` alone takes the
   first page), and should the total header appear for those partial requests?
4. Should the total header be emitted only when at least one pagination
   parameter is present, or also on the legacy full-list response?

Until these questions are answered, the checklist intentionally does not
claim a particular header spelling, numeric bound, default, or header-presence
policy.

## Research and supporting facts

- The collection route is `src/app/api/notes.py::read_all_notes`, currently
  with no query parameters, and it delegates to `src/app/api/crud.py::get_all`.
- `get_all` currently selects the complete `notes` table without an explicit
  ordering, limit, offset, or count query.
- The notes table has an integer primary-key `id`; the requested paginated
  order can therefore be expressed at the database query boundary.
- `src/tests/test_notes.py` currently checks only that `GET /notes/` returns
  status 200 and a JSON list, plus that creation is available.
- `README.md` is the only maintained user-facing package documentation found;
  `docs/development/index.md` records that no notes-query specification exists.
- The working tree was clean before this task file was added.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Add typed optional query parameters at the collection route and use FastAPI's
query validation for parsing and bounds. Preserve the existing no-parameter
path as a full list, while the paginated path obtains the total count
independently, applies explicit ascending-ID ordering, and applies the
requested offset and limit before returning the JSON array plus the agreed
header. Keep the single-note and mutation routes untouched.

Extend the public `TestClient` coverage with independent seeded notes to
prove:

- the no-parameter response remains a JSON array containing the full
  collection;
- a paginated response is ordered by ascending ID, bounded by the requested
  offset and limit, and carries the total count;
- partial-parameter behavior, once confirmed, follows the documented
  defaults;
- malformed, negative, zero, or otherwise out-of-range values covered by the
  agreed contract return FastAPI's normal 422 validation response;
- the existing CRUD smoke coverage still passes.

Update `README.md` only after the contract choices above are confirmed and
implemented. Document the query parameters, their validation, ordering,
response-header semantics, and the preserved full-list behavior. Do not
describe target behavior as current before implementation is complete.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

The task is intentionally a single task file because the change has one
public owner and one acceptance boundary, even though its execution includes
code, tests, and documentation. The exact header name, numeric bounds,
partial-parameter defaults, and whether the header is present on the legacy
response remain requirement questions listed above; execution should return
the plan to Draft if any answer changes the checklist.

### Documentation

During execution, update `README.md` as the maintained user-facing guide for
the notes API. No new documentation directory or placeholder notes-query
page is warranted by the current repository structure.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Confirm the unresolved public-contract questions.
- [ ] Mark this plan `Approved` before implementation begins.
- [ ] Implement optional collection pagination at the HTTP/database boundary.
- [ ] Add or update public route-level regression tests.
- [ ] Update the README with verified pagination behavior.
- [ ] Run the focused tests and the complete available test suite.
- [ ] Record implementation and completion notes with evidence.

### Requirement verification

- Full-list compatibility: a `TestClient` request to `GET /notes/` with no
  query parameters returns status 200 and the complete collection as a JSON
  array.
- Paginated slice and ordering: a `TestClient` request with confirmed
  pagination parameters returns only the requested bounded records in
  ascending ID order.
- Total count: the same public response includes the agreed total-count
  header whose value equals the number of stored notes, independent of the
  requested slice.
- Validation: public requests containing each agreed invalid value receive
  FastAPI's standard 422 response; tests must exercise the actual route
  boundary rather than calling query or CRUD helpers directly.
- CRUD preservation: the existing create/read/update/delete route coverage,
  supplemented where necessary to cover the changed collection's interaction
  with stored notes, continues to pass.

### Additional implementation verification

- Verify that the count is taken from the full notes collection and is not
  accidentally limited or offset.
- Verify that the no-pagination branch does not change the response shape to
  an envelope or alter unrelated route behavior.
- Run the repository's available test command and report any environment
  limitation rather than treating an uncollected or interrupted run as
  passing.

# Add optional limit/offset pagination to `GET /notes/`

Add optional `limit`/`offset` query pagination to the notes collection route:
clients can request a bounded, `id`-ascending slice and receive the total note
count in a response header. Requests without pagination keep the current
full-list array behavior, invalid query values rely on normal FastAPI
validation, and the other CRUD routes do not change. Planning only — nothing
has been implemented.

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] `GET /notes/` accepts optional `limit` and `offset` query parameters.
      When pagination is requested, the response body is the bounded slice of
      notes ordered by `id` ascending: `offset` rows skipped first, at most
      `limit` rows returned.
- [ ] Paginated responses carry the total note count in a response header
      (header name recommended as `X-Total-Count`, pending approval — see Q1).
- [ ] Requests without pagination parameters keep the current behavior: 200
      with the full, unbounded JSON array of every note as the body.
- [ ] Invalid query values are rejected by normal FastAPI validation (standard
      422 error body); no hand-rolled validation or custom error handling.
- [ ] The other CRUD routes (`GET /notes/{note_id}/`, `POST /notes/`,
      `PUT /notes/{note_id}/`, `DELETE /notes/{note_id}/`) keep their current
      signatures, status codes, and behavior.
- [ ] `README.md` documents the optional pagination and count header in the
      same reviewed change as the code (repo documentation policy).

## Requirement questions and material decisions (pending approval)

These are recommendations recorded in the Draft plan; approving the plan
approves them as written, or tell me which to change.

- **Q1 — Header name** (material, public contract): recommend `X-Total-Count`,
  the common convention for collection-count headers. Any name works
  mechanically; clients will depend on the exact string.
- **Q2 — Header on non-paginated responses** (requirement question): recommend
  the header only when pagination is requested, so non-paginated responses
  stay exactly as today (no new header) — the strictest reading of "keep the
  current full-list array behavior". Alternative: always send the header.
- **Q3 — Negative values** (material, public validation behavior): recommend
  declaring `ge=0` on both parameters via `Query`, so `?limit=-1` is a normal
  422. Unconstrained ints would pass validation and reach obscure SQLite
  semantics (negative `LIMIT` means "no limit"). `limit=0` stays valid: empty
  array plus count header.
- **Q4 — One parameter alone** (material, public behavior): recommend the
  parameters are independent — either one activates pagination; missing
  `offset` means 0, missing `limit` means no upper bound. Alternative: require
  both together (422 on exactly one).

## Supporting facts

- Current chain: `read_all_notes` in `src/app/api/notes.py` → `get_all()` in
  `src/app/api/crud.py` → `database.fetch_all(notes.select())` — no
  parameters, no `ORDER BY`; FastAPI serializes the returned rows as a JSON
  array. Existing `test_read_all_notes` asserts only 200 + list.
- App shape: FastAPI router mounted at `/notes` (`src/app/main.py`); async
  `databases` + SQLAlchemy core over a SQLite file `./notes.db` created at
  import time relative to the working directory; table
  `notes(id PK, title, description)` (`src/app/db.py`).
- The response body stays a JSON array in both modes; only paginated responses
  add the count header. No `response_model` changes are needed or planned.
- Tests use `fastapi.testclient.TestClient` against the real app
  (`src/tests/conftest.py`). There is no DB reset between tests and
  `notes.db` persists on disk, so pagination tests need deterministic seeding
  (a harness reset) to assert exact slices and totals.
- Verified run command (baseline: 2 passed, working tree restored afterward):
  `cd src && UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=<tmp-dir> uv run --project <repo-root>
  --with pytest python -m pytest -q`. pytest is not declared in
  `pyproject.toml`, so `uv run --with pytest` supplies it. Plain `python3`
  (no deps installed) and the pyenv 3.11.12 env (missing `databases`) cannot
  run the suite.
- `uv run` creates an untracked `uv.lock` at the repo root and the test run
  creates an untracked `src/notes.db`; both were removed after the baseline
  probe.
- Documentation surface: `README.md`'s collection-route sentence ("currently
  returns every note as a JSON array") is the only public claim to update.
  `docs/development/index.md` states no notes-query specification exists; no
  new spec page is warranted for this change (smallest-structure policy).
- This variant has no Python client package or CLI (server-only fixture), so
  no client-side deliverables are in scope.
- `docs/development/documentation.md` was read; only a local factual README
  correction is planned, no doc restructuring.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

### Approach

Single deliverable at the notes service's public HTTP boundary.

1. `src/app/api/crud.py` — add a total-count helper
   (`database.fetch_val(sqlalchemy.select(func.count()).select_from(notes))`)
   and a paginated fetch
   (`notes.select().order_by(notes.c.id.asc()).offset(offset).limit(limit)`,
   applying each clause only when its value is provided). Leave `get_all()`
   untouched so the non-paginated path is literally the current code.
2. `src/app/api/notes.py` — extend `read_all_notes` with an injected
   `response: Response` plus `limit: Annotated[int | None, Query(ge=0)] = None`
   and `offset: Annotated[int | None, Query(ge=0)] = None` (fall back to
   `Optional[int]` only if the resolved Python needs it). Branch inside the
   handler: either parameter present → paginated slice via the new crud
   functions and set the count header on the injected `Response`; otherwise →
   existing `crud.get_all()` unchanged. No `response_model`, no status-code
   changes, no changes to other route signatures.
3. `src/tests/conftest.py` + `src/tests/test_notes.py` — make DB state
   deterministic (clear the `notes` table between tests through the same
   app/database machinery), then add tests: non-paginated regression (full
   array, no count header per Q2), paginated slice ordering and boundaries
   with seeded rows, header value equal to the seeded total, each
   single-parameter case, `limit=0` empty slice, and 422s for non-integer and
   negative values. Add a small regression test covering
   `GET /notes/{id}/`, `PUT`, and `DELETE` (currently uncovered) to evidence
   the "other routes unchanged" requirement.
4. `README.md` — extend the collection-route sentence with the optional
   parameters, ascending-`id` ordering when paginated, the count header, and
   the unchanged full-array behavior without parameters.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

Covered by Q1–Q4 in "Requirement questions and material decisions" above;
approving the plan resolves all four to the stated recommendations. No
additional open questions. Not proposed: an upper bound (`le`) on `limit` (not
requested), transactional coupling of the count and slice queries
(single-process fixture, low value), and envelope-style response bodies (the
count-header design keeps the body an array in both modes).

### Documentation

- Update `README.md` in the same reviewed change as the code: collection route
  supports optional `limit`/`offset`, results are ordered by `id` ascending
  when paginated, the total count is returned in the `X-Total-Count` response
  header, and behavior without parameters is unchanged. Audience: API users;
  smallest structure (no new pages, no spec).

### Task checklist

- [ ] Add paginated-fetch and total-count helpers in `src/app/api/crud.py`
      without touching `get_all()`.
- [ ] Extend `read_all_notes` in `src/app/api/notes.py` with `limit`/`offset`
      Query parameters, the pagination branch, and the count header.
- [ ] Make test DB state deterministic and add pagination, validation, and
      other-routes regression tests in `src/tests/`.
- [ ] Update the collection-route description in `README.md`.
- [ ] Run the full suite via the verified uv command and clean untracked
      runtime artifacts (`uv.lock`, `src/notes.db`).

### Requirement verification

- R1 paginated slice, R2 count header, R3 non-paginated behavior, R4
  validation: new and existing tests through the public HTTP boundary
  (`TestClient` → real app → SQLite), asserting seeded ids and order, header
  value, full array without the header, and 422 bodies. Existing
  `test_read_all_notes` must keep passing unchanged.
- R5 other routes unchanged: no source changes to those handlers (diff
  review), plus the new read-by-id/update/delete regression test.
- R6 README updated in the same change: the change's diff contains the README
  edit; final wording reviewed by the user.

### Additional implementation verification

- Run the suite from a clean tree (no pre-existing `src/notes.db`) to confirm
  import-time DB creation and the seeding work deterministically.
- Confirm the working tree has no unintended artifacts before finishing.
