The Books page filter (`all`/`read`/`unread`) is dropped when add, update, or
delete refreshes the collection: those refreshes call `getBooks()` with the
default `all` filter, so the list shows unfiltered books while the filter
control still shows the previous selection as active. The fix is client-side;
the API contract and unfiltered behavior are preserved.

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] After a successful add, update, or delete, the collection refresh reuses
  the currently selected filter (`all`/`read`/`unread`) so the displayed books
  match the active filter. Refresh moments and component method signatures
  (`selectFilter(value)`, `add(book)`, `update(book)`, `remove(id)`) are
  unchanged, and refresh still happens only after the mutation succeeds.
- [ ] The selected filter remains visibly active across CRUD refreshes: the
  filter control's active/pressed state continues to reflect the user's
  selection and is not reset or desynced from the refreshed list.
- [ ] Flask API endpoints and response shapes are unchanged: `GET /books` →
  `{"status": "success", "books": [...]}`, `POST /books` →
  `{"status": "success", "books": [...]}`, `PUT/DELETE /books/<id>` →
  `{"status": "success", "book": ...}`. The fix is client-side only.
- [ ] Unfiltered behavior is preserved: `all` (the default) continues to fetch
  every book with no `read` query parameter, both when the filter is selected
  and during CRUD refreshes while `all` is selected.

## Questions and decisions

- No unresolved requirement questions. Interpretation used for planning:
  "visibly active" means the existing active-state signal (`aria-pressed` on
  the filter buttons, `client/src/components/Books.vue:7`) stays correct and
  consistent with the list; no new styling is requested. Flagged for
  confirmation at plan approval.

## Supporting facts

- Regression location: `client/src/components/Books.vue:32,36,40` —
  add/update/remove refetch with `getBooks()` (default `all`), discarding the
  selection (marked `// regression: filter lost`). `selectedFilter` is not
  reset, so the control stays pressed while the list becomes unfiltered —
  the reported state/content mismatch.
- Filter mechanics: buttons iterate `['all', 'read', 'unread']`
  (`client/src/components/Books.vue:5`); `selectedFilter` defaults to `"all"`
  (`client/src/components/Books.vue:24`); `selectFilter` already fetches with
  the chosen value (`client/src/components/Books.vue:26-29`).
- Client transport already supports filters: `getBooks(filter = "all")` sends
  no params for `all` and `{ read: true|false }` otherwise
  (`client/src/api/books.js:3-6`). No client API change is needed.
- Server contract (`server/app.py:10-30`): GET filters via `?read=true|false`;
  POST appends and returns `{"status", "books"}`; PUT/DELETE return
  `{"status", "book"}`. This fix does not touch the server, which preserves
  the response shapes.
- There is no mounted/initial fetch; the list loads only via `selectFilter`
  or a CRUD refresh. Initial-load behavior is out of scope.
- Existing coverage: `client/tests/Books.spec.js` mocks the api module and
  only checks the empty state; `tests/test_books_api.py` covers unfiltered
  GET and the CRUD happy path. Nothing pins the CRUD-refresh filter today.
- Rejected approach: resetting the filter to `all` after mutations, or
  refetching without params — both reintroduce the reported inconsistency.
  No server-side filter persistence is needed.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Approach — single-layer client fix. The capability touches no other layer
with an independently useful or owned result, so no per-layer split.

1. `client/src/components/Books.vue`: add a `refresh()` method that sets
   `this.books = (await getBooks(this.selectedFilter)).data.books;` and call
   it from `selectFilter`, `add`, `update`, and `remove`. This makes the
   selected filter the single source of truth for every refresh and keeps the
   pressed state consistent with the list.
2. No changes to `client/src/api/books.js` or `server/app.py`; request and
   response handling is untouched, preserving API shapes and unfiltered
   behavior.

Verification:

- Extend `client/tests/Books.spec.js`: after `selectFilter("read")`, invoke
  `add`, `update`, and `remove`, asserting the mocked `getBooks` was last
  called with `"read"` after each refresh and the `read` button still has
  `aria-pressed="true"`. Add an `all`-path assertion (select `all`, then
  `add` → last call `"all"`). Keep the existing empty-state test passing.
  Tests must call methods via `wrapper.vm` because the fixture wires no CRUD
  controls to these methods.
- New `client/tests/api-books.spec.js` (mock `../src/http`): pin the
  `getBooks` mapping — `all` → `GET /books` with `{ params: {} }`, `read` →
  `{ params: { read: true } }`, `unread` → `{ params: { read: false } }`.
- Run `npm test` in `client/` and `pytest` at the repo root; existing server
  tests must pass untouched (no diffs under `server/` or `client/src/api/`).

Risks / notes:

- Component tests assert the api-client seam with a mock; they do not catch
  param-mapping regressions in `api/books.js` — mitigated by the new api spec.
- If a mutation rejects, no refresh occurs (unchanged behavior; no new error
  handling is introduced).
- No e2e layer exists in this fixture; component + api unit tests are the
  proportionate evidence.

Exclusions: initial-load fetching, filter control styling, server changes,
CRUD error handling, new documentation pages.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- Decision (local, resolved): extract `refresh()` rather than repeating
  `getBooks(this.selectedFilter)` in three methods — removes the duplication
  that caused the regression and keeps `selectedFilter` authoritative.
- Open questions: none. The "visibly active" interpretation above is the only
  judgment call; confirm it at approval.

### Documentation

None required. No maintained documentation describes the filter or refresh
behavior (`README.md:3` is generic; `docs/development/index.md:3` records that
no book-discovery specification exists). The change restores intended behavior
without introducing new public claims, so no pages are added or edited. If
maintained docs describing refresh behavior are discovered during execution,
update them in the same change.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Add `refresh()` to `Books.vue` and route `selectFilter`/`add`/`update`/
  `remove` through it; remove the stale `// regression: filter lost` markers.
- [ ] Extend `client/tests/Books.spec.js` with CRUD-refresh filter and
  `aria-pressed` coverage (read path and all path).
- [ ] Add `client/tests/api-books.spec.js` pinning the filter→params mapping.
- [ ] Run the client vitest suite and root pytest suite; confirm green and no
  server/api diffs.

### Requirement verification

- Filter reused on CRUD refresh → component test: mocked `getBooks` last
  called with the selected filter after each of add/update/remove (boundary:
  component→api-client seam; the mock records the argument the fix controls
  rather than bypassing the behavior under test).
- Filter stays visibly active → component test: `aria-pressed="true"` on the
  selected button after each CRUD refresh (boundary: rendered component DOM).
- API response shapes preserved → no diff to `server/app.py` or
  `client/src/api/books.js` handling; existing `tests/test_books_api.py`
  passes unmodified (boundary: Flask test client).
- Unfiltered behavior preserved → api spec asserts `all` → `GET /books` with
  empty params; the existing unfiltered server test passes; the component
  `all`-path assertion (boundary: client request contract + Flask test
  client).

### Additional implementation verification

- Optional, cheap server pin: extend `tests/test_books_api.py` with a
  `GET /books?read=true` assertion returning only read books. That behavior
  is pre-existing and unchanged by this fix; include it only if desired when
  executing.

# Books page discovery for larger collections

Plan and track the Books page discovery capability: read-status filtering,
title/author search, bounded pagination, and URL share/restore, with the
table, active controls, empty state, browser navigation, and CRUD refreshes
kept consistent with the selected view. Existing CRUD behavior and unfiltered
API compatibility must be preserved. Planning only — implementation is not
authorized until the plans below are approved.

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] Books can be filtered by read status (all / read / unread) on the Books page.
- [ ] Books can be searched by title or author, matching case-insensitively.
- [ ] Results can be paged with a server-enforced, bounded page size.
- [ ] The selected discovery state (filter, search, page) is encoded in the URL so it can be shared and restored.
- [ ] Opening a shared URL restores the same view, and browser back/forward moves between discovery states.
- [ ] The table, active controls, empty state, browser navigation, and CRUD refreshes stay consistent with the selected view.
- [ ] Existing CRUD behavior (POST /books, PUT/DELETE /books/<book_id>) is preserved.
- [ ] `GET /books` without discovery query params keeps returning the full unfiltered list in the current response shape.

## Requirement questions

- Q1 — Should the table show each book's read status (column or badge) so the
  active read filter is legible? This adds visible UI beyond the literal
  request. Recommendation: yes, a minimal read indicator. Unresolved; gates
  subtask 020's template scope.

## Subtasks

- [ ] tasks/20260919-books-page-discovery/010-server-discovery-query.md — API selection and compatibility (no dependency)
- [ ] tasks/20260919-books-page-discovery/020-books-page-discovery-controls.md — page controls and view consistency (depends on 010)
- [ ] tasks/20260919-books-page-discovery/030-url-discovery-state.md — URL share/restore and history (depends on 020)

## Supporting facts

Verified from the current codebase:

- `server/app.py` keeps an in-memory `BOOKS` list and serves `GET/POST /books`
  (`{"status": "success", "books": [...]}`) and `PUT/DELETE /books/<book_id>`
  (`{"status": "success", "book": ...}`). No query parameters are read today.
- `server/query.py::list_books(books)` is a passthrough and is not imported by
  `app.py` — a currently unused seam that gives selection logic an owned home.
- `client/src/api/books.js::getBooks(params = {})` already forwards params as
  query parameters, so client transport needs no change to send discovery params.
- `client/src/components/Books.vue` loads all books on mount, renders a
  title/author table with the "No books found." empty state, and re-fetches via
  `getBooks()` after each add/update/remove.
- `client/src/router.js` is vue-router 4 with `createWebHistory` and a single
  `/books` route; `client/src/http.js` is axios with baseURL
  `http://localhost:5000`.
- Existing coverage: `tests/test_books_api.py` asserts only status codes for
  the unfiltered list and CRUD (it does not prove response shape);
  `client/tests/Books.spec.js` mounts the component with a mocked api module
  and asserts the empty state; `client/tests/books.integration.js` is an empty
  placeholder with no transport integration coverage.
- `docs/development/index.md` currently states "No book-discovery
  specification exists." — the intended home for the discovery spec.

Constraints from AGENTS.md: avoid layer-only splits (each slice must leave an
independently useful or owned result); use the least expensive test that
proves behavior at the real boundary; update maintained documentation in the
same change that makes new claims true.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Decompose into three capability slices, executed in dependency order. Server
selection comes first because the page and URL slices consume its contract;
the page slice delivers user-visible discovery; the URL slice adds
share/restore on top of the stabilized state model. No slice is a layer-only
split: each leaves an independently useful or owned result (an API capability,
a working page discovery view, shareable links).

Cross-cutting verification: run the pytest suite (`tests/`) and the vitest
suite (`client/tests/`) after each slice and once at the end. Compatibility
regressions (unfiltered `GET /books`, CRUD endpoints) are asserted explicitly
in 010; existing component coverage is kept as a default-view regression
anchor with its mock updated to the new API contract. No end-to-end or hosted
harness is added in this task.

Risks:

- The discovery query parameters and response additions are public API
  surface; keep changes additive and leave the param-less path exactly as it
  is today.
- Router query sync can loop (route watcher vs control writer); bound it with
  memory-history component tests and a single source of truth.
- The existing `Books.spec.js` mock must carry the new contract (e.g.
  `total`) once the component consumes it; update the maintained test harness
  to the real contract rather than special-casing the component.
- The store is in-memory, so CRUD can shrink the filtered set; clamp the page
  after refreshes so the view never rests on an empty out-of-range page.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

These need approval before execution (public API / user-visible behavior):

- D1 — API contract (recommendation): discovery params `read` (`read` |
  `unread`), `q` (case-insensitive substring over title and author), and
  `page` (1-based); page size is a fixed server constant (10), not a client
  parameter. The response adds `total` (count of books matching filter and
  search); `books` holds the selected page's items when any discovery param is
  present and the full list when none are.
- D2 — Out-of-range page requests (recommendation): the server returns an
  empty `books` page with the correct `total`; the client clamps to the last
  valid page after refreshes (D5).
- D3 — URL encoding (recommendation): mirror the API params (`read`, `q`,
  `page`) in the router query; omit defaults (no filter value, empty `q`,
  page 1) so the default view keeps a clean URL.
- D4 — History behavior (recommendation): committed changes (filter change,
  search submission, page change) push a history entry; live typing does not.
- D5 — Post-refresh clamping (recommendation): if the current page exceeds the
  last valid page after a CRUD refresh, clamp to the last valid page and
  update the URL with `replace`.
- D6 — Invalid URL/API values (recommendation): unknown `read` values and
  non-positive or non-numeric `page` are treated as absent (defaults) rather
  than rejected; document the rule. Flagged because it is API-visible
  behavior.
- Q1 (from above, requirement question) — read-status indicator in the table.

### Documentation

Audience: developers using the API and the Books page. Replace the "No
book-discovery specification exists." placeholder in
`docs/development/index.md` with a concise book-discovery specification
covering the API contract (010), page controls and view consistency (020),
and URL share/restore behavior (030). Each subtask updates its slice in the
same change that makes the claims true. No new directories or placeholder
pages.

### Task checklist

- [ ] tasks/20260919-books-page-discovery/010-server-discovery-query.md
- [ ] tasks/20260919-books-page-discovery/020-books-page-discovery-controls.md
- [ ] tasks/20260919-books-page-discovery/030-url-discovery-state.md
- [ ] Final integration check: both test suites pass, documentation updated, requirement verification current in every subtask.

### Requirement verification

- Discovery API (filter/search/pagination/total), unfiltered compatibility,
  and CRUD preservation → subtask 010, pytest at the Flask HTTP boundary
  (`tests/test_books_api.py`). Existing coverage asserts only status codes, so
  new explicit compatibility assertions are required rather than assumed.
- Page controls, table/empty-state/CRUD view consistency → subtask 020,
  component tests at the api-module boundary (`client/tests/Books.spec.js`);
  the existing empty-state test remains the default-view regression anchor
  once its mock carries the new contract.
- URL share/restore and back/forward consistency → subtask 030, component
  tests with a vue-router memory history instance.
- No requirement is claimed complete until its subtask records passing
  evidence at the boundary named above.

# Server discovery query support for /books

Add read-status filtering, title/author search, and bounded pagination to the
books listing API while keeping the unfiltered response and all CRUD endpoints
unchanged. Independently useful: the API gains a testable selection capability
that any client can consume.

Parent Task: tasks/20260919-books-page-discovery/000-main.md

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] `GET /books` accepts an optional read-status filter returning only read or only unread books.
- [ ] `GET /books` accepts an optional case-insensitive substring search matching title or author.
- [ ] `GET /books` accepts an optional 1-based page selector served in fixed-size, server-enforced pages, applied after filter and search.
- [ ] The listing response exposes the total number of books matching the active filter and search so clients can render bounded pages.
- [ ] Filter, search, and page combine in a single request.
- [ ] `GET /books` without discovery params returns the full unfiltered list in the current response shape.
- [ ] POST /books and PUT/DELETE /books/<book_id> behavior and responses are unchanged.
- [ ] The API contract slice of the discovery documentation is updated in the same change.

## Supporting facts

- `server/app.py` currently reads no query parameters; the list response is
  `{"status": "success", "books": BOOKS}` and the item response is
  `{"status": "success", "book": current}`.
- `server/query.py::list_books` is an unused passthrough — extend this module
  so selection logic has an owned home, and route list requests through it.
- `tests/test_books_api.py` asserts status codes only; it does not prove
  response-shape compatibility, so explicit compatibility assertions are new
  work.
- The Flask test client (`tests/conftest.py`) is the maintained harness for
  HTTP-boundary evidence.
- Contract details (param names, page size, `total` field, invalid-value
  handling) are recommendations D1/D2/D6 in the main task, pending approval.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Implement selection as pure functions in `server/query.py`: filter by read
status, case-insensitive substring match over title and author, slice the
resulting list by page against the fixed page size, and return the page items
plus the match count. `app.py` parses `request.args` on GET only and passes
the values through the selection module; POST/PUT/DELETE stay untouched. The
param-less path must produce exactly the current response body.

Verification: unit tests for the selection math (filter, search
case-insensitivity, pagination bounds, combined params, out-of-range page) and
pytest HTTP tests for parameter handling, the combined case, unfiltered
compatibility (exact shape and full list), and CRUD regression. Unit tests are
appropriate for the pure selection functions; the HTTP boundary proves
routing and selection interacting.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- Contract details follow main-task D1/D2/D6 and are recommendation-level
  until approved; treat them as inputs, not settled decisions.
- Local, reversible choices: selection functions return `(page_items, total)`;
  an out-of-range page yields an empty item list with the real total.

### Documentation

Update `docs/development/index.md`: document the discovery query parameters,
the fixed page size, the `total` field, and the unchanged unfiltered behavior.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Selection logic in `server/query.py` with unit tests
- [ ] Query-param wiring in `server/app.py` (GET only)
- [ ] HTTP tests: filter, search, pagination, combined, unfiltered compatibility, CRUD regression
- [ ] API contract documented in `docs/development/index.md`

### Requirement verification

- Selection behavior → unit tests over `server/query.py` (pure boundary).
- HTTP behavior and compatibility → pytest via the Flask test client
  (`tests/test_books_api.py`), the real routing boundary. The existing tests
  remain as a status-level regression anchor only; they do not assert shape.

# Books page discovery controls and view consistency

Add read-status filter, title/author search, and bounded pagination controls
to the Books page, driven by the server discovery API, with the table, active
controls, empty state, and CRUD refreshes kept consistent with the selected
view. Independently useful: users can work a larger collection on the page.

Parent Task: tasks/20260919-books-page-discovery/000-main.md
Depends On: tasks/20260919-books-page-discovery/010-server-discovery-query.md

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] A read-status control (all / read / unread) constrains the visible table.
- [ ] A search control matches titles or authors case-insensitively.
- [ ] Pagination controls move between pages bounded by the server-reported total.
- [ ] The table always reflects the current filter, search, and page selection.
- [ ] The empty state appears whenever the selected view returns no books and stays consistent with the active selection.
- [ ] Add, update, and delete keep their existing behavior and refresh by re-applying the current discovery state; if the current page is beyond the last valid page after a refresh, the view clamps to the last valid page.
- [ ] Requests send the current discovery state through `getBooks(params)`; with defaults selected the request stays unfiltered.
- [ ] The page-usage slice of the discovery documentation is updated in the same change.

## Requirement questions

- Q1 (inherited from the main task, unresolved): read-status indicator in the
  table — affects this subtask's template scope. Do not add it without
  approval.

## Supporting facts

- `Books.vue` already re-fetches after every mutation via `getBooks()`; the
  change re-applies the current params there rather than introducing a
  separate refresh path.
- `getBooks(params = {})` already forwards query params; no transport change
  is expected (verify while implementing).
- `client/tests/Books.spec.js` mocks the api module and asserts the empty
  state; it is the maintained component boundary. Its mock data must gain the
  new contract field(s) when the component starts consuming them.
- The component currently renders title/author columns only.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Hold the discovery state (filter, search, page) as component state; derive
request params from it; bind the controls to the state; and route the
mount/refresh fetches through `getBooks(currentParams)`. Keep `total` from
the response to bound pagination (prev/next disabled at the edges, current
position shown). After each CRUD mutation, re-apply the current selection and
clamp the page to the last valid page when the selection shrinks (main-task
D5). The default view (defaults selected) must issue the same unfiltered
request as today.

Verification: extend `client/tests/Books.spec.js` — assert the param-less
default request, that control changes issue param'd requests and update the
table, the filtered empty state, and that add/update/delete re-apply the
current selection including the clamp case. The component boundary is
appropriate here: the API contract itself is proven by subtask 010's HTTP
tests, so mocking the api module does not bypass the behavior under test.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- Search commit semantics (live vs on submit/debounce) follow main-task D4
  (committed changes) and are recommendation-level until approved.
- Local choice: pagination renders as prev/next plus a current-position
  indicator — the smallest useful control for a large collection.

### Documentation

Update `docs/development/index.md`: describe the Books page controls and the
consistency rules (view, empty state, CRUD refreshes).

### Task checklist

- [ ] Discovery state and controls in `Books.vue`
- [ ] Param'd fetches and CRUD re-apply with clamping
- [ ] Component tests extended (params, table, empty state, CRUD re-apply)
- [ ] Page-usage documentation updated

### Requirement verification

- Controls, table consistency, empty state, and CRUD re-apply →
  `Books.spec.js` at the api-module boundary with a mocked `getBooks`
  capturing params (existing harness, extended — not bypassed).
- The existing empty-state test remains valid as the default-view anchor once
  its mock carries the new contract.

# URL share/restore for Books discovery state

Encode the selected discovery state (filter, search, page) in the `/books`
URL so it can be shared and restored, keep browser back/forward consistent
with the view, and keep the controls in sync with restored state.
Independently useful: any discovery view is shareable by link.

Depends On: tasks/20260919-books-page-discovery/020-books-page-discovery-controls.md

task_files.tasks/20260919-notes-query-capability/00:
# Notes query capability across API, client, and CLI

Add one supported notes-query capability (bounded pagination, stable sorting,
optional text filtering) to the notes HTTP API, the reusable `notes_client`
package, and the `notes` CLI, without changing current unparameterized
behavior. The public HTTP contract is written and approved before the client or
CLI implementation relies on it, and the CLI is proven end-to-end over the
production client-to-service path.

Planning-only handoff: execution is not authorized yet. All plans below are
`Draft`.

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] R1: One supported notes-query capability exists on all three public
      boundaries: the notes HTTP collection operation (`GET /notes/`), the
      `NotesClient` public API, and the `notes` CLI.
- [ ] R2: The capability supports bounded pagination (page size bounded by the
      approved contract; unparameterized calls remain unbounded and unchanged).
- [ ] R3: The capability supports stable sorting (deterministic total order with
      a defined tie-break, so pages are reproducible).
- [ ] R4: The capability supports optional text filtering (no filter means no
      filtering, matching current behavior).
- [ ] R5: Current unparameterized HTTP behavior is preserved: `GET /notes/`
      with no query parameters still returns every note as a JSON array.
- [ ] R6: Current unparameterized client behavior is preserved:
      `NotesClient.list_notes()` keeps its current request (no query string)
      and its JSON-array return contract.
- [ ] R7: The public HTTP query contract is specified in maintained
      documentation and approved (stable) before any client or CLI
      implementation relies on it.
- [ ] R8: The CLI is proven end-to-end over the production path — real CLI
      code, real `notes_client.NotesClient`, live notes service over HTTP, with
      no test stubs on that path.
- [ ] R9: Maintained documentation of each affected boundary reflects the
      supported behavior in the same reviewed change that makes it true (root
      `README.md`, `packages/notes_client/README.md`,
      `apps/notes_cli/README.md`, `docs/development/index.md`).

## Subtasks

- [ ] `tasks/20260919-notes-query-capability/010-query-contract.md` —
      Stabilize the public notes-query HTTP contract (specification + docs
      index). Blocks all implementation.
- [ ] `tasks/20260919-notes-query-capability/020-api-query-capability.md` —
      Implement the query capability in the notes API (HTTP boundary).
- [ ] `tasks/20260919-notes-query-capability/030-client-query-capability.md` —
      Implement the query capability in `notes_client` (package boundary).
- [ ] `tasks/20260919-notes-query-capability/040-cli-query-capability.md` —
      Add CLI query options and prove the production client-to-service path
      (application boundary).

Sequencing: 010 first. 020 and 030 are independent once 010 is approved and may
run in parallel. 040 is last because it consumes the real service (020) and the
real client method (030) for the end-to-end proof.

## Supporting facts

Established by inspection of the current workspace (all verified):

- The collection route `read_all_notes` (`src/app/api/notes.py:8`) calls
  `crud.get_all()` (`src/app/api/crud.py:4`), which runs an unsorted,
  unfiltered `database.fetch_all(notes.select())`. There are no query
  parameters today; the response is a bare JSON array of note rows.
- `NotesClient.list_notes()` (`packages/notes_client/notes_client/client.py:20`)
  issues `GET /notes/` and returns the parsed JSON array. The HTTP transport is
  constructor-injected, and `from_environment()` builds an `httpx.Client` from
  `NOTES_API_URL` (default `http://127.0.0.1:8000`).
- The CLI (`apps/notes_cli/cli.py`) exposes only `notes list`, printing
  `id: title` per note from `client.list_notes()`.
- Current tests stub one layer up each time: CLI tests stub the client,
  client tests stub the transport, API tests use the real app via
  `TestClient`. No existing test crosses the real client-to-service path.
- Storage is SQLite through `databases` + SQLAlchemy Core
  (`src/app/db.py`); `title` and `description` are `String(50)`. SQLAlchemy
  Core supports composing `.where()`, `.order_by()`, `.limit()`, `.offset()`,
  which is sufficient for pagination, sorting, and filtering without a new
  dependency.
- `docs/development/index.md` currently records "No notes-query
  specification exists." — the contract deliverable must update this line.
- The root `pyproject.toml` declares `fastapi`, `httpx`, `sqlalchemy`, and
  `databases[sqlite]`; the workspace is a single Python environment, so all
  three components are importable together (basis for the CLI end-to-end
  proof). `uvicorn` is not currently a dependency.

Assumptions:

- All three test trees run in one interpreter/workspace configuration (as
  `src/tests` already imports `app.main` and the CLI imports `notes_client`).
  If execution discovers otherwise, the affected subtask records it.
- Fixture test data shares the on-disk SQLite file `./notes.db` (cwd-relative);
  API and end-to-end tests must tolerate pre-existing rows rather than assume
  an empty database.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Approach: contract-first decomposition by public boundary, following the
fixture guidance that HTTP, package, and application compatibility boundaries
justify separate deliverables (test levels alone do not).

1. `010` writes the notes-query HTTP specification and gets it approved. This
   is the stability gate required by R7; nothing downstream starts earlier.
2. `020` (HTTP API) and `030` (client package) implement the approved contract
   on their boundaries in parallel. Each preserves its unparameterized behavior
   with explicit regression evidence and updates its own maintained docs in the
   same change.
3. `040` (CLI application) adds the user-facing flags and delivers the
   end-to-end proof over the production path (R8), which is also the first
   decisive evidence that the three boundaries compose correctly.
4. The task completes when every subtask's checklist and this main checklist
   are satisfied and all three test suites pass in a full run.

Discovery rule: if implementation of 020/030/040 exposes a gap or defect in the
approved contract, the contract change flows back through 010 (which returns to
`Draft` for re-approval) rather than being improvised downstream. Consumers
never build against an informal contract.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

Material decisions that shape the public contract are recorded and asked about
in `010-query-contract.md` (`### Implementation decisions and open questions`),
because they change user-visible behavior on the HTTP boundary:

- Whether to extend the existing collection operation with optional parameters
  or add a separate query route (recommendation: extend the existing
  operation, since defaults preserve current behavior exactly).
- Pagination bound enforcement (reject out-of-bounds `limit` vs silently cap),
  sort field whitelist / direction syntax / tie-break, filter target and
  matching semantics, and response shape (recommendation: keep the bare array).

Downstream surface decisions that are user-visible on their own boundaries
(client method surface, CLI command/flag surface) are recorded with
recommendations in `030` and `040` respectively and confirmed at those plans'
approval. Resolving the HTTP contract does not by itself authorize those
surfaces; each subtask's own plan approval does.

### Documentation

- `010`: one specification page under `docs/` (placement decided there per
  `docs/development/documentation.md`) plus the `docs/development/index.md`
  status line. Audience: HTTP API consumers and the maintainers of the two
  consuming deliverables.
- `020`: root `README.md` (audience: API users).
- `030`: `packages/notes_client/README.md` (audience: Python consumers).
- `040`: `apps/notes_cli/README.md` (audience: CLI users).
- Specification pages may describe the intended target; boundary READMEs must
  only claim supported behavior in the change that implements it (020/030/040
  own those README updates, not 010).

### Task checklist

The `## Subtasks` list above is the authoritative checklist. During execution,
update it together with each subtask file's own `### Task checklist`; a
subtask counts as done only when its requirement evidence exists, not merely
when its implementation code exists.

### Requirement verification

- R1: verified at completion by the union of boundary evidence — 020 API
  tests, 030 client tests, 040 CLI tests. No separate test; recorded when all
  three subtasks close.
- R2–R4: decisive at the HTTP boundary (020 tests through `test_app` over the
  real app and SQLite); 030 recording-transport tests prove the client forwards
  the parameters; 040 proves the composed behavior once end-to-end.
- R5: 020's unparameterized regression test at the HTTP boundary.
- R6: 030's regression test proving the no-argument call issues the identical
  request as current code (no query string).
- R7: 010's recorded approval of the specification plus the dependency
  ordering (030/040 declare `Depends On` 010 and must not start before it
  closes).
- R8: 040's end-to-end test over a live service with the real client — the
  decisive evidence; stub-based unit tests count only as supporting.
- R9: reviewed documentation diffs in each boundary's change set (010, 020,
  030, 040 respectively).

### Additional implementation verification

- Full regression run across all three suites (`src/tests`,
  `packages/notes_client/tests`, `apps/notes_cli/tests`) at 040 completion;
  existing tests must pass unmodified.
- Shared on-disk SQLite (`./notes.db`) is a real cross-test coupling risk:
  020's tests assert relative order/content of seeded notes, and 040's
  end-to-end server should isolate its database (e.g. run the server process
  with a temporary working directory) rather than mutate shared state.
task_files.tasks/20260919-notes-query-capability/01:
# Stabilize the public notes-query HTTP contract

Specify the notes-query capability's public HTTP contract — parameters,
pagination bounds, sorting, optional text filtering, response shape, error
behavior, and unparameterized compatibility — in maintained documentation, and
obtain approval so the client and CLI build against a stable contract.

This subtask changes no service behavior and no user-facing README claims. It
is the gate for `020`, `030`, and `040`.

Parent Task: `tasks/20260919-notes-query-capability/000-main.md`

Depends On: none (first subtask).

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] C1: A maintained specification describes the notes-query HTTP contract:
      the operation and route, pagination parameters with explicit bounds,
      sort parameters with deterministic (tie-broken) ordering, the optional
      text filter and its matching semantics, the response shape, and the
      validation/error behavior for invalid parameters.
- [ ] C2: The specification explicitly states the compatibility rule:
      unparameterized requests keep current behavior exactly (full collection
      returned as a bare JSON array, no sorting, no filtering, no page cap).
- [ ] C3: The specification is approved — the contract is "stable" — and the
      approval is recorded in this task file before `020`, `030`, or `040`
      begins.
- [ ] C4: `docs/development/index.md` no longer states that no notes-query
      specification exists and points to the specification.

## Supporting facts

- Current behavior being pinned (verified): `GET /notes/` (prefix configured in
  `src/app/main.py:15`) returns `crud.get_all()` — every note, DB order, no
  parameters; response is a bare JSON array.
- FastAPI's default validation behavior returns 422 for failed query-parameter
  constraints; the contract should state this explicitly rather than leave it
  implicit.
- Documentation rules (`docs/development/documentation.md`): specifications may
  describe an intended target; user documentation must only describe current
  supported behavior. Therefore the root README, client README, and CLI README
  are NOT touched here — their claims become true only with the implementing
  changes in 020/030/040. The specification page is the intended-target
  artifact.
- Smallest structure applies: a single specification page; no placeholder
  sections or directory scaffolding beyond what the content needs.
- `docs/development/index.md` currently reads "No notes-query specification
  exists." and must be updated with the spec (C4).

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

1. Decide the contract values below (open questions section), presenting them
   for approval together with this plan.
2. Write the specification as one page under `docs/` (placement by audience
   and ownership; likely a sibling of `docs/development/` serving API
   consumers, but the exact location is decided when writing, following
   `docs/development/documentation.md`).
3. Update `docs/development/index.md` (C4).
4. Record approval in this task file (turn the checklist item C3 true with a
   dated note) — this is the stability gate for 020/030/040.

Recommended contract content (to be confirmed or amended at approval):

- Operation: the existing `GET /notes/` collection operation gains optional
  query parameters; no new route. Rationale: defaults preserve current
  behavior exactly and avoid stabilizing a second route.
- Pagination: `limit` (1..max, recommendation max 100) and `offset`
  (>= 0). Parameters absent ⇒ not applied at all (unparameterized requests
  are unbounded, preserving R5). Out-of-bounds values ⇒ 422 (explicit
  rejection preferred over silent capping; the contract must pick one).
- Sorting: `sort` restricted to a whitelist (recommendation: `id`, `title`),
  optional descending form (recommendation a `-` prefix), deterministic
  tie-break on `id` ascending so pages never shuffle equal keys; `sort`
  absent ⇒ current DB order (unchanged).
- Filtering: single optional `q` parameter, case-insensitive substring match
  (recommendation: over `title` only, as the smallest useful filter; extending
  to description is a contract choice to make now, not later); `q` absent ⇒
  no filtering.
- Response shape: unchanged bare JSON array in every case (no envelope), so
  the shape never depends on which parameters were supplied.
- Error behavior: FastAPI 422 for invalid/unknown/out-of-bounds values,
  documented explicitly.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

All items below are material (user-visible HTTP contract) and need approval
before this plan is marked `Approved`; none is resolved yet:

- Parameter surface: extend `GET /notes/` with optional parameters vs a new
  query route. Recommendation: extend the existing operation.
- Pagination bounds and enforcement: 422 vs silent cap for oversized `limit`;
  the numeric maximum. Recommendation: 422, max 100.
- Sort field whitelist, direction syntax, and tie-break rule. Recommendation:
  `id` and `title`, `-` prefix for descending, `id` ascending tie-break.
- Filter target (`title` only vs title + description) and matching
  (case-insensitive substring recommended), parameter name (`q`
  recommended).
- Response shape: bare array (recommended) vs envelope when paginating.
  Recommendation: bare array always; keeps R5 trivially true.

### Documentation

- One specification page under `docs/` describing the contract above,
  including a short "current behavior preserved" section (C2) and worked
  request examples.
- `docs/development/index.md` updated (C4).
- Audience: HTTP API consumers, plus maintainers of the client and CLI who
  implement against the contract. No user README changes in this subtask.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Contract decisions approved (recorded above with date)
- [ ] Specification page written and reviewed
- [ ] `docs/development/index.md` updated
- [ ] Approval recorded (C3) — gate for 020/030/040

### Requirement verification

- C1, C2: the specification change itself is the evidence — the requirement is
  the existence of a stable documented contract at the public HTTP boundary;
  a reviewed diff of the spec page is decisive.
- C3: the dated approval note in this task file plus the `Depends On` edges
  that 020/030/040 declare; no automated test (docs-only change).
- C4: the `docs/development/index.md` diff.
- Downstream behavioral evidence of the contract arrives with 020's API tests;
  it is intentionally not produced here because nothing is implemented yet.

### Additional implementation verification

- None beyond documentation review; no code, tests, or dependency changes are
  in scope for this subtask.

# Implement the notes-query capability in the notes API

Extend the notes collection operation in `src/app` to support the approved
HTTP contract from `010` — bounded pagination, stable sorting, optional text
filtering — while preserving unparameterized behavior, with regression and
capability evidence at the public HTTP boundary and the root README updated in
the same change.

Parent Task: `tasks/20260919-notes-query-capability/000-main.md`

Depends On: `tasks/20260919-notes-query-capability/010-query-contract.md`
(the approved contract is the authority for every parameter, bound, and
default below; do not start before C3 in 010 is recorded).

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] A1: The collection operation accepts the contract's optional query
      parameters and implements bounded pagination, stable sorting, and
      optional text filtering exactly as specified (parameter names, bounds,
      whitelist, matching semantics, response shape).
- [ ] A2: Unparameterized `GET /notes/` behavior is preserved: every note,
      bare JSON array, no sorting or filtering or page cap — proven by a
      regression test, not by assertion.
- [ ] A3: Invalid parameters are rejected per the contract (expected 422 for
      out-of-bounds or unknown values as specified in 010).
- [ ] A4: The root `README.md` describes the collection route's query
      capability as current supported behavior, updated in the same reviewed
      change as the code that makes it true.

## Supporting facts

- Current code: `read_all_notes` (`src/app/api/notes.py:8`) →
  `crud.get_all` (`src/app/api/crud.py:4`) →
  `database.fetch_all(notes.select())`. Implementation point: extend the crud
  function (or add a query function it delegates to) to compose
  `.where()`, `.order_by()`, `.limit()`, `.offset()` on the SQLAlchemy Core
  select; no new dependency.
- "Absent" vs "default" matters: parameters must be declared with `None`
  defaults so that FastAPI distinguishes "not provided" (legacy path, nothing
  applied) from "provided" (contract path). A non-`None` default for `limit`
  would silently change unparameterized behavior and break A2/R5.
- Existing test fixture: `src/tests/conftest.py` provides `test_app`
  (`TestClient(app)`), which runs the real FastAPI app including lifespan
  (real `databases` connection) against SQLite — the right boundary for A1–A3
  evidence, since routing, validation, and SQL all interact.
- The tests share the on-disk SQLite file `./notes.db` (cwd-relative, created
  at import in `src/app/db.py`); existing tests already insert rows and the
  database is not reset per test. New tests must seed identifiable notes and
  assert relative order/content, never assume an empty or exclusively-owned
  table.
- Sorting/filtering interact with pagination correctness: offset paging must
  be composed with the same filter and sort in every page request — this is
  what makes "stable sorting" observable, so the tests should page through a
  seeded set and assert no overlap/gap.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

1. Extend the crud layer with the query composition (filter → sort →
   limit/offset order per the approved contract), keeping `get_all`'s
   unparameterized call path intact.
2. Extend `read_all_notes` with the contract's optional `Query` parameters,
   `None` defaults, and the contract's validation constraints (A1, A3).
3. Add tests to `src/tests/test_notes.py`:
   - Unparameterized regression (A2): seed notes, assert the full seeded set
     is returned as a bare list.
   - Pagination (R2): page through a seeded set with `limit`/`offset`,
     assert correct windowing including a final partial page; assert the
     contract's bound rejection (e.g. oversized `limit` → 422).
   - Sorting (R3): seed notes whose insertion order differs from sort order;
     assert deterministic ordering and the tie-break.
   - Filtering (R4): matching and non-matching `q` values; absence means all.
   - A combined pagination+sort+filter query paged end-to-end without
     overlap/gap.
   All tests tolerate pre-existing rows (relative assertions only).
4. Update the root `README.md` collection-route description (A4) in the same
   change as the code.
5. Run the `src/tests` suite; existing tests must pass unmodified.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- Contract-resolved values (parameter names, bounds, whitelist, matching,
  response shape) come from the approved 010 specification and are not
  re-decided here. If execution exposes a gap or defect in the contract, stop

# Add the notes-query capability to the notes_client package

Extend the reusable `NotesClient` public API with the approved contract's
optional pagination, sorting, and filtering parameters, forwarded to the
collection route, while preserving the current unparameterized call exactly,
with unit evidence at the client's HTTP-construction boundary and the package
README updated in the same change.

Parent Task: `tasks/20260919-notes-query-capability/000-main.md`

Depends On: `tasks/20260919-notes-query-capability/010-query-contract.md`
(the client is a consumer of the stable HTTP contract). It deliberately does
not depend on `020`: the client's own behavior is testable against the
contract without the server implementation, and the real client-to-service
composition is proven in `040`.

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] L1: `NotesClient` exposes the query capability per the approved
      contract: optional pagination, sort, and filter parameters are forwarded
      to `GET /notes/` as the contracted query string.
- [ ] L2: Unparameterized `list_notes()` is preserved: the request issued is
      identical to today's (path `/notes/`, no query parameters) and the
      return contract is unchanged — proven by a regression test.
- [ ] L3: `packages/notes_client/README.md` describes the capability as
      current supported behavior, updated in the same reviewed change as the
      code.

## Supporting facts

- `NotesClient` (`packages/notes_client/notes_client/client.py`) takes an
  injected transport and calls `self.transport.get("/notes/").json()`.
  `from_environment()` wraps `httpx.Client` bound to `NOTES_API_URL`.
  httpx natively supports `params=` on `get`, so parameter forwarding needs no
  new dependency and no manual query-string encoding.
- Existing test transport (`packages/notes_client/tests/conftest.py`) returns
  a fixed empty response and records nothing. The plan extends this maintained
  test harness to record `(path, params)` per call so tests can assert exact
  forwarding. Per testing guidance, shared test harnesses are maintained test
  infrastructure verified through a real consumer — the existing and new
  client tests are that consumer.
- The client's important boundary is HTTP request construction; a recording
  transport is the least expensive test that proves it without weakening the
  client code path. Full composition with the real service is intentionally
  deferred to `040`'s end-to-end proof and is recorded below as the gap this
  subtask leaves open.
- Current README states `list_notes()` "currently returns the unparameterized
  collection" — that sentence must change with the behavior (L3), not before.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

1. Decide the method surface (open questions below) and add the optional
   parameters to `list_notes()` mirroring the approved contract's names and
   semantics. Absent parameters are omitted from the request entirely — no
   defaults are sent — so an unparameterized call produces byte-identical
   requests to today's behavior (L2).
2. Extend the test harness transport to record requests, then add tests:
   - Each parameter forwarded alone, with the exact expected `params`.
   - Combined parameters in one call.
   - Unparameterized regression (L2): `list_notes()` with no arguments issues
     the request exactly as before (no `params` / no query string) and
     returns the parsed JSON body.
3. Update `packages/notes_client/README.md` (L3) in the same change.
4. Run the `packages/notes_client/tests` suite; existing tests pass
   unmodified.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- Method surface (material, user-visible for Python consumers; needs approval
  with this plan): extend `list_notes()` with optional keyword parameters
  (recommendation — one capability, one method, unparameterized default
  unchanged) vs add a separate `query_notes()` method. If the approved 010
  contract shapes parameter names differently than the client surface, the
  client surface follows the contract's names.
- No other open questions: transport injection and `from_environment()`
  behavior are preserved as-is.

### Documentation

- `packages/notes_client/README.md` (audience: Python consumers of the
  package): document the optional parameters and state that the unparameterized
  call is unchanged. Same change as the code.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Client method extended per the approved contract
- [ ] Recording-transport tests added (parameter forwarding + unparameterized
      regression)
- [ ] `packages/notes_client/README.md` updated in the same change
- [ ] `packages/notes_client/tests` suite passes, existing tests unmodified

### Requirement verification

- L1: recording-transport unit tests proving the exact query-string
  construction per parameter and in combination — the client package's public
  boundary; decisive for the client side of R1/R2–R4 forwarding.
- L2: the regression test proving the no-argument call is request-identical
  to current code (R6). Current existing test (returns a list) is kept as a
  supporting shape check, not as the evidence for L2.
- L3: the README diff reviewed with the code change.
- Known gap deferred by design: the client against the real service is proven
  in `040`'s end-to-end test (R8); this subtask's evidence is
  request-construction only and must not be cited as service-composition
  proof.

### Additional implementation verification

- Full `packages/notes_client/tests` run, existing tests unmodified.
- Confirm `from_environment()` behavior is untouched (no new configuration
  surface unless the approved contract requires one).

# Add CLI query options and prove the production client-to-service path

Extend the `notes` CLI so users can exercise the approved query capability,
preserving the default `notes list` behavior exactly, and add the end-to-end
test that proves the production path — real CLI code, real
`notes_client.NotesClient`, live notes service over HTTP — with no stubs on
that path. CLI README updated in the same change.

Parent Task: `tasks/20260919-notes-query-capability/000-main.md`

Depends On:
- `tasks/20260919-notes-query-capability/010-query-contract.md` (flag names
  and semantics mirror the approved contract),
- `tasks/20260919-notes-query-capability/020-api-query-capability.md` (the
  live service must exist for the end-to-end proof),
- `tasks/20260919-notes-query-capability/030-client-query-capability.md` (the
  CLI calls the real client method).

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] P1: The CLI exposes the query capability with optional flags mapping to
      the client capability per the approved contract; default invocation
      (no flags) preserves current output behavior exactly.
- [ ] P2: CLI-level unit tests cover flag→parameter mapping and the unchanged
      default behavior, using the existing stubbed-client harness (extended,
      still the cheap layer).
- [ ] P3: An end-to-end test proves the production client-to-service path:
      the real CLI entry point (`main`), the real `NotesClient` (no test
      stubs), and a live notes service reached over HTTP, exercising
      pagination, sorting, and filtering (R8).
- [ ] P4: `apps/notes_cli/README.md` describes the capability as current
      supported behavior, updated in the same reviewed change as the code.

## Supporting facts

- CLI today (`apps/notes_cli/cli.py`): argparse with a required `list`
  subcommand; `list_command(client)` prints `id: title` per note from
  `client.list_notes()`. `main(argv, client)` allows test injection.
- Current CLI tests stub the client entirely (`apps/notes_cli/tests/conftest.py`);
  the end-to-end proof is therefore new test infrastructure, owned by the CLI
  application because it proves the CLI's user path (top of the consumer
  stack).
- Environment: single workspace Python environment; the server is importable
  the same way `src/tests` imports `app.main`. The e2e test may import
  `app.main` for the server process without making the CLI depend on the
  server at runtime — the dependency edge exists only in tests.
- Server options for the e2e proof (decision below):
  - A real `uvicorn` server subprocess on an ephemeral loopback port — proves
    the full production path including sockets; `uvicorn` is not currently a
    dependency, so this adds one (test-scope).
  - `httpx.ASGITransport(app=app)` under the real `httpx.Client` inside
    `NotesClient` — crosses the real client and the real FastAPI app but
    bypasses the network stack.
- Shared-state risk: the server writes `./notes.db` (cwd-relative). Running
  the server with a temporary working directory gives the e2e test an
  isolated database without product changes.
- The requirement "the CLI must prove the production client-to-service path"
  makes this an important path that lower layers cannot represent faithfully —
  exactly the case the fixture's testing guidance reserves for end-to-end
  tests. One test, real components, no test-only shortcuts in product code.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

1. Extend the CLI surface (open questions below): flags `--limit`, `--offset`,
   `--sort`, `--q` (names per the approved contract) on the chosen command;
   when no flags are given, the client is called with no query arguments at
   all, preserving current behavior (P1) — the CLI must not invent defaults.
2. Extend the stubbed-client unit harness to record calls and assert:
   each flag forwarded as the contracted parameter, combined flags, and the
   default invocation calling the client with no arguments (P2). Rendering of
   existing output (`id: title`) is covered by the existing test, kept
   unmodified.
3. Add the end-to-end test in `apps/notes_cli/tests/`:
   - Start the real service (chosen server option) with an isolated temporary
     working directory and an ephemeral port.
   - Seed notes through the public API (`POST /notes/`) — realistic public
     path, no direct DB writes.
   - Build the real client via `NotesClient.from_environment()` with
     `NOTES_API_URL` pointed at the running server (the production
     configuration mechanism, exercised as in production).
   - Invoke `main([...])` with query flags; assert the printed lines match
     the expected paginated/sorted/filtered window seeded above.
   - Terminate the server and clean up (no leaked process, socket, or files).
4. Update `apps/notes_cli/README.md` (P4) in the same change.
5. Run the CLI suite; then the full three-suite pass for the parent task.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- Server option for the e2e proof (material to what the evidence proves;
  needs approval with this plan): real `uvicorn` subprocess (recommendation —
  proves the production path including the network hop; accepts `uvicorn` as
  a test dependency) vs `httpx.ASGITransport` (no new dependency, weaker
  evidence — bypasses sockets). If approved as ASGITransport, the README/task
  record must describe the evidence by the boundary actually crossed.
- CLI surface (material, user-visible; needs approval): extend `notes list`
  with optional flags (recommendation — one verb for the collection operation,
  default unchanged) vs a new `notes query` subcommand.
- Flag names: follow the approved contract's parameter names (e.g. `--q` vs
  `--filter`) — confirm at approval; local choice thereafter.

### Documentation

- `apps/notes_cli/README.md` (audience: CLI users): document the optional
  flags and the unchanged default behavior. Same change as the code.

### Task checklist

- [ ] CLI flags implemented; default invocation unchanged (no arguments sent
      by default)
- [ ] Unit tests for flag mapping + default behavior (P2)
- [ ] End-to-end production-path test added and passing (P3)
- [ ] `apps/notes_cli/README.md` updated in the same change
- [ ] CLI suite passes; full three-suite pass recorded for the parent task

### Requirement verification

- P1: unit tests at the CLI boundary (arg parsing → client call), plus the
  end-to-end assertions; the existing unmodified `test_list_command` supports
  default rendering.
- P2: those unit tests (stubbed client is appropriate at this layer; the
  stub proves the CLI's own logic only).
- P3: the end-to-end test is the decisive evidence for R8 — real CLI code,
  real `NotesClient` with its production `from_environment()` configuration,
  real HTTP, real FastAPI app, real SQLite. No stubs on that path. Stub-based
  tests and 020/030's boundary tests are supporting evidence only.
- P4: the README diff reviewed with the code change.

### Additional implementation verification

- Full regression run across `src/tests`, `packages/notes_client/tests`, and
  `apps/notes_cli/tests`; all existing tests pass unmodified.
- Confirm the e2e server runs isolated (temp working directory, ephemeral
  port) and leaves no `notes.db`, socket, or process behind; confirm no
  test-only shortcut was added to product code (`cli.py`, `client.py`, app
  code untouched by test concerns).

producer_records.prompt: Migrate post author metadata from the current single-name field to a structured multi-author form without breaking existing content or generated pages during the transition. Templates, archives, feeds, and authoring tools must move to the new model, existing posts must be migrated safely, and the legacy form may be rejected only after generated-output and content evidence show that nothing still depends on it. Plan the work and create the appropriate task structure without implementing it.
producer_records.response:
Task structure created under `tasks/20260919-author-metadata-migration/` — planning only, nothing implemented. Execution waits for your approval.

## Plan summary

**Outcome.** Post author metadata moves from the scalar `author: "Name"` field to a canonical structured multi-author form; post pages, feed, and the authoring tool consume the new model; both existing posts migrate with unchanged URLs and author output; and the legacy form is rejected only after an evidence gate proves nothing depends on it.

**Approach** (5 dependency-ordered subtasks):
1. `010-author-model-and-compat` — install deps, capture a baseline build, add the `authors` model with a normalization layer that maps both forms to one uniform view (unit-tested).
2. `020-templates-feed-and-archives` — post layout renders all authors (joined, `p.author` element retained), feed emits one `<author>` per author, archive/tag/home tests upgraded from existence-only to full listings; build-boundary tests run a fixture site (multi-author + legacy + new-form posts) so no test-only content pollutes production `content/`.
3. `030-authoring-tool` — `frontMatter` emits the structured list form (unit-pinned).
4. `040-migrate-existing-posts` — convert `first.md`/`second.md`, compare generated output against the baseline.
5. `050-legacy-gate-and-rejection` — gate (content scan + tool check + green suite) → remove legacy acceptance → explicit build error naming offending files → README updated in the same change.

**Key facts grounding the plan:** all 7 `author` touchpoints inventoried (`post.njk:2`, `feed.xml.njk:5`, both posts, `new-post.js`, both placeholder tests); archives/tags/sitemap are author-independent; `posts.json` sets no author default; existing tests assert nothing; `node_modules` is absent so execution starts with `npm install`.

**Open decisions needing your approval before the affected subtask runs:**
1. **Shape** — recommend `authors` as an ordered list of display-name strings, always a list (alternative: objects with `name`/`url` if per-author attributes are needed now).
2. **Rejection mechanism** — recommend an explicit build-time error listing files still using legacy `author:` (rather than silently stripping it).
3. **Feed semantics** — recommend preserving current bare-text `<author>` form, one element per author; Atom-validity rework (`<name>` wrapping) deferred out of this migration.

**Acceptance evidence:** unit tests (normalization, tooling) plus production-build tests over post pages, feed, and full archive listings; baseline comparison proves single-author output equivalence during transition; final suite proves the rejection error.

**Risks:** normalization must not disturb the data cascade (covered by fixture builds); feed output for multi-author posts necessarily differs from legacy; removing the legacy path early would break transition guarantees — subtask ordering enforces the gate; a fresh Eleventy 3 install must work in this worktree or the gate can't be evaluated.

**Exclusions:** no per-author archive/profile pages, no Atom-validity rework, no CI setup, no changes to tags/sitemap beyond regression evidence.

The plan is stored as `Status: Draft` in `000-main.md`. Approve it (including the three decisions above, or with corrections) and I'll mark it `Approved` and begin execution with subtask 010.

# Migrate post author metadata to a structured multi-author model Migrate the site's single-name `author` front-matter field to a structured multi-author model across post templates, the feed, archives, and the authoring tool. Existing posts are migrated safely under a compatibility window, and the legacy single-name form is rejected only after generated-output and content evidence show nothing still depends on it. Planning only: this file does not authorize implementation. ## Requirements checklist - [ ] R1: Posts support a single canonical structured author field representing an ordered list of authors; it replaces the single-name `author` field as the supported authoring model. (Exact shape per approved decision in `### Implementation decisions and open questions`.) - [ ] R2: The post page layout renders every author of a post, for both single-author and multi-author posts. - [ ] R3: The feed emits an author element for every author of every post, preserving the currently emitted author-text semantics. - [ ] R4: Archives, tag pages, the home listing, and the sitemap keep rendering all posts (title/link) unchanged through the migration; they have no author dependence and are regression-protected. - [ ] R5: The authoring tool (`scripts/new-post.js`) generates the structured form for new posts. - [ ] R6: During the transition, legacy single-name posts and structured-form posts coexist: both build and render correctly, with no content loss and no broken generated pages at any intermediate state. - [ ] R7: Existing posts (`content/posts/first.md`, `content/posts/second.md`) are migrated to the structured form with their URLs and rendered author output preserved. - [ ] R8: Evidence exists for the new model, the compatibility behavior, and the migration: unit tests for normalization and the authoring tool, plus production-build integration tests over post pages, feed, and archives that include multi-author and legacy/new mixed cases without adding test-only content to production `content/`. - [ ] R9: The legacy single-name form is rejected only after gate evidence — a content scan showing zero legacy usage and green generated-output evidence — and the rejection is an explicit, documented build failure. - [ ] R10: Maintained documentation reflects the author model, the transition state, and the final rejection state, kept in the same reviewed changes as the code that makes each claim true. ## Subtasks - [ ] tasks/20260919-author-metadata-migration/010-author-model-and-compat.md - [ ] tasks/20260919-author-metadata-migration/020-templates-feed-and-archives.md - [ ] tasks/20260919-author-metadata-migration/030-authoring-tool.md - [ ] tasks/20260919-author-metadata-migration/040-migrate-existing-posts.md - [ ] tasks/20260919-author-metadata-migration/050-legacy-gate-and-rejection.md ## Open questions and decisions These change scope or outcomes and must be resolved (by approval of this plan or explicit instruction) before the affected subtask executes. 1. **Structured shape (R1, blocks 010).** Recommend: `authors` as an ordered YAML list of display-name strings, e.g. `authors: ["Ada Example"]`, always a list (no scalar shorthand for the new field; the authoring tool always emits a list). Alternative: entries as objects with at least `name` (optionally `url`) if per-author attributes beyond the display name are required now. Choose one before 010 executes. 2. **Rejection mechanism (R9, blocks 050).** Recommend: a build-time check in the Eleventy data path that fails the build with an error listing files that still define legacy `author:`, so rejection is machine-enforced and matches documentation. Alternative: silently ignoring/stripping the legacy field (rejected recommendation: hides authoring mistakes). 3. **Feed Atom validity (R3, affects 020 scope).** The current feed emits bare text inside `` (not an Atom-valid `` child). Recommend: preserve current semantics (one `` per author, same text form) and defer any Atom-validity rework out of this migration. Confirm or expand 020 scope. ## Supporting details Verified facts from inspection (2026-09-19): - Author touchpoints (complete): - `content/posts/first.md:3` — legacy scalar `author: "Ada Example"`. - `content/posts/second.md:3` — legacy scalar `author: "Grace Example"`. - `_includes/layouts/post.njk:2` — renders scalar `{{ author }}` inside `

`. - `content/feed.xml.njk:5` — `{{ post.data.author }}` per post in `collections.posts`. - `scripts/new-post.js:1-3` — pure `frontMatter(title, author)` emits the legacy scalar string form. - `tests/author-output.test.js`, `tests/archive-output.test.js` — comment-only placeholders, no assertions. - Author-independent generated surfaces: `_includes/postslist.njk` renders title + url only; `content/index.njk`, `content/blog.njk`, and `content/tag-pages.njk` all include `postslist.njk`; `content/sitemap.xml.njk` renders URLs only. - Data cascade: `content/posts/posts.json` sets only `layout` and `tags: ["posts"]`; there is no directory-level author default. - Build config (`eleventy.config.js`): input `content`, includes `../_includes`, output `_site`; provides a `head` filter; passthrough-copies `public` (directory does not exist — pre-existing condition, not in scope). - Test harness: `npm test` runs `node --test tests/*.test.js`; both files currently collect and exit cleanly (verified with node v20.19.5) but assert nothing. Generated output (`_site/`) is gitignored. - Dependencies are not installed in this worktree (`node_modules` absent); execution must start with `npm install` (`@11ty/eleventy ^3.0.0`). - Documentation surface: root `README.md` describes build outputs; `docs/development/index.md` and `docs/development/documentation.md` are maintainer guidance; there is no `docs/index.md`. Author-model documentation belongs in the author-facing surface (`README.md`) per `docs/development/documentation.md` rules. - `UPSTREAM.md`: fixture adapted from Eleventy Base Blog. Constraints: - No test-only posts may be added to production `content/`; multi-author and mixed-form build coverage must come from a separate fixture site (see 020). - For single-author posts, the new pipeline must produce equivalent generated output to the current build, which allows before/after comparison as transition evidence. - New public documentation claims must land in the same reviewed change as the code that makes them true (repository documentation guidance). ## Execution plan Status: Draft Layered migration: normalize both author forms behind one data view, migrate all consumers (post layout, feed) to that view with generated-output tests, migrate the authoring tool, migrate existing content, then evaluate the legacy-dependency gate and reject the legacy form. Consumers are changed before content so that migrated posts render correctly the moment they are converted; the legacy path is removed last, after evidence. Sequence and boundaries: 1. **010 — model + compatibility.** Install dependencies, capture a baseline production build of the current content (comparison artifact), then introduce the canonical `authors` model with a normalization step that yields a uniform authors list from either the new form or the legacy scalar. Templates do not change yet. Unit tests cover normalization of both forms. 2. **020 — consumers.** Post layout renders all authors (joined display, existing `p.author` element class retained); feed emits one author element per author with current text semantics; archives are regression-covered (posts listed with titles/links, not just existence). Generated-output tests cross the real build boundary via a fixture site that includes a multi-author post, a new-form single-author post, and a legacy post, so the compat path is exercised; real-content build checks cover first/second. 3. **030 — authoring tool.** `frontMatter` emits the structured list form; unit test pins the exact emitted front matter. 4. **040 — content migration.** Convert `first.md` and `second.md` to the structured form; compare generated output against the 010 baseline (same URLs, same rendered author text, archive/feed/sitemap intact). 5. **050 — gate + rejection.** Evidence gate: content scan shows zero legacy `author:` usage in `content/`, authoring tool no longer emits it, all build-boundary tests green. Only then remove legacy acceptance from the normalization path, add the explicit build-time rejection error, re-run the full suite and production build, and update `README.md` to the final rejection state (removing the transitional note added earlier). Risks: - Normalization must integrate with the Eleventy data cascade without shadowing unrelated post data; `posts.json` has no author keys, so risk is low but the integration tests must catch regressions. - Feed output for multi-author posts necessarily differs from the legacy single-element output; single-author output must remain text-equivalent (R3/R7 comparison evidence). - Removing the legacy path before the gate would break transition guarantees; subtask ordering (050 strictly after 030/040 evidence) enforces the gate. - Fresh `npm install` and an Eleventy 3 build in this worktree are prerequisites; if the build cannot run, the gate cannot be evaluated and the plan stops at the blocked subtask with the blocker reported. ### Implementation decisions and open questions - D1 (open, needs approval): field shape — recommend `authors` list of display-name strings, always a list. # Paginated blog archive

Plan the Eleventy archive change so a growing post collection remains browseable
through stable static pages while all existing site surfaces continue to use
the same post collection and ordering.

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] Keep `/blog/` as the first archive page.
- [ ] Generate deterministic later archive URLs with at most twenty posts per
      page.
- [ ] Preserve the existing newest-first post order across page boundaries,
      without dropping or duplicating posts.
- [ ] Add accessible previous/next navigation to archive pages, with only the
      links valid for the current page exposed.
- [ ] Preserve the home page, tag pages, feed, sitemap, and individual-post
      pages and navigation.
- [ ] Keep the archive output static and usable without client-side JavaScript.

## Open requirement questions and decisions

- Requirement question: confirm the public URL shape for later pages. The
  recommended convention is `/blog/2/`, `/blog/3/`, and so on, with the
  existing trailing-slash style; this is user-visible and should be confirmed
  before execution.
- Decision: scope pagination to the archive template. Do not paginate or
  reorder the global `collections.posts` collection, because the home page,
  tags, feed, sitemap, and individual posts consume it independently.
- Decision: use Eleventy’s build-time pagination and rendered links. No
  browser-side state, fetches, or JavaScript navigation is part of the
  design.
- Decision: the archive must render one canonical post list per page. The
  current template invokes the shared list include and then emits another
  archive list; retaining both would make a twenty-post page contain duplicate
  entries and would violate the page-size requirement.

## Supporting facts

- `content/blog.njk` currently owns `/blog/`, passes the complete
  `collections.posts` collection to `_includes/postslist.njk`, and separately
  loops over the reversed collection.
- `_includes/postslist.njk` reverses its `postslist` input before rendering.
  Pagination must therefore establish newest-first page boundaries before the
  include’s local ordering behavior is applied; reversing each already-sliced
  page would group the wrong posts.
- `content/index.njk`, `content/tag-pages.njk`, `content/feed.xml.njk`, and
  `content/sitemap.xml.njk` consume the collection through separate templates.
  `content/posts/posts.json` and `_includes/layouts/post.njk` own individual
  post rendering.
- The existing archive test only documents that `/blog/index.html` exists; it
  does not currently build and inspect page contents or any preservation
  surfaces.
- `README.md` describes the generated site at a high level, while
  `docs/development/index.md` explicitly notes that no archive pagination
  specification exists. `docs/development/documentation.md` was reviewed
  before planning this documentation change.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Implement archive-only Eleventy pagination using the confirmed later-page URL
convention. Feed the paginator an ordering that preserves the current
newest-first archive semantics, partition into pages of twenty, and retain
the `/blog/` permalink for page one. Render the page’s posts once through the
existing presentation conventions, then add a semantic navigation region with
visible Previous/Next links, appropriate `rel` values, and no invalid link on
the first or final page.

Extend the production-build test to use enough deterministic posts to exercise
the first, middle, and final page states. Assert page size, URL stability,
boundary navigation, cross-page ordering, complete non-overlapping coverage,
and absence of archive JavaScript. In the same build, assert that the home
page, tags, feed, sitemap, and individual-post output remain present and
consistent with the pre-pagination collection behavior.

Update the maintained README and development archive note after the behavior
is implemented, documenting the public archive URL pattern, twenty-post
limit, and static navigation. Do not publish the target behavior as current
documentation while this plan remains unimplemented.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- Resolve the later-page permalink question before marking this plan
  `Approved`; `/blog/2/` is the working recommendation.
- Prefer Eleventy pagination metadata for previous/next targets so links are
  generated from the same page graph as the output. The exact Nunjucks
  property names should be verified against the installed Eleventy version
  during implementation.
- Keep collection order and all non-archive templates unchanged. If the
  shared include cannot express the required archive ordering without
  affecting home or tag output, use archive-local rendering rather than
  changing those consumers’ contracts.
- Use a realistic production build with a collection large enough to exercise
  all navigation states. Do not mock pagination metadata or test a
  JavaScript-only fallback.

### Documentation

- Update `README.md` with the supported archive pagination behavior once it is
  implemented and verified.
- Replace the stale archive note in `docs/development/index.md` with the
  current URL and page-size contract, or remove it if the maintained
  documentation no longer needs a separate archive specification.
- No documentation files are changed during this planning-only request.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Confirm the later-page URL convention and approve this execution plan.
- [ ] Implement archive-only build-time pagination with a twenty-post page
      size and stable first-page permalink.
- [ ] Preserve newest-first ordering and eliminate duplicate archive entries
      while leaving other collection consumers unchanged.
- [ ] Add semantic, visible previous/next archive navigation with correct
      first/middle/final-page behavior.
- [ ] Expand or arrange realistic build input and update production-build
      regression coverage for pagination and preserved site surfaces.
- [ ] Update maintained README/development documentation.
- [ ] Run the focused test and production build, then record evidence and any
      deviations in the task file.

### Requirement verification

- First-page and later-page URL requirements: inspect the built `_site` paths
  and assert the first archive is `/blog/` while later pages follow the
  approved stable convention.
- Page-size and ordering requirements: parse every generated archive page,
  assert no page contains more than twenty post entries, and compare the
  concatenated links against the expected newest-first collection with no
  gaps or duplicates.
- Navigation requirement: assert first, middle, and final pages expose the
  correct visible Previous/Next links and omit links that have no destination.
- Preservation requirements: build and inspect home, tag, feed, sitemap, and
  representative individual-post URLs and content; compare their post order
  or membership to the unpaginated collection contract where applicable.
- Static-output requirement: inspect generated archive HTML and the output
  asset set for absence of client-side JavaScript dependencies.
