# Implement notes queries at the public API

Parent Task: `tasks/20260919-notes-query-capability/000-main.md`

Depends On: `tasks/20260919-notes-query-capability/010-public-contract.md`

Implement the approved notes-query contract in the FastAPI route and database
access layer. The service remains the source of filtering, pagination, and
ordering behavior for all consumers.

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] `GET /notes/` accepts the approved bounded pagination, stable sorting,
  and optional text-filter parameters.
- [ ] The service applies filtering and pagination before returning results and
  uses a deterministic ordering, including the approved tie-breaker.
- [ ] Invalid or out-of-bound query values produce the contractually approved
  public errors.
- [ ] `GET /notes/` without query parameters preserves the current list-shaped
  behavior and does not silently impose a new default page limit.
- [ ] API tests cover the feature and compatibility at the public HTTP
  boundary.

## Unresolved requirement questions

Implementation is blocked on the contract decisions in
`tasks/20260919-notes-query-capability/010-public-contract.md`, especially
pagination/response shape, sort vocabulary, filter matching, and errors.

## Research and supporting facts

- `src/app/api/notes.py` currently delegates the collection route to
  `crud.get_all()` with no query model.
- `src/app/api/crud.py` currently issues an unrestricted `notes.select()` with
  no explicit ordering.
- `src/app/db.py` exposes only `id`, `title`, and `description`, which bounds
  the fields available to the public contract.
- `src/tests/test_notes.py` currently has no seeded multi-row query scenarios
  and the global database needs deliberate test isolation.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

After the contract is approved, add route validation using the framework's
public request boundary and pass normalized query values into a database-level
query. Keep the no-argument route behavior explicit. Add integration tests
that create controlled notes through the service boundary, exercise each
query feature and invalid case, and verify the response shape and ordering.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- The API layer owns public validation and the CRUD/data layer owns query
  construction; both must consume the same normalized contract values.
- Sorting must use an explicit secondary key so equal primary values have a
  repeatable order across pages.
- Filtering and pagination should be performed by the database query rather
  than by slicing an unrestricted result in Python.
- The final response representation and parameter names remain those approved
  by the contract subtask.

### Documentation

- Update the root API guidance and the shared notes-query contract only after
  the implementation and integration tests pass.
- Do not replace the existing unparameterized collection claim with a
  parameterized-only description; document both paths.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Add public query parameter validation from the approved contract.
- [ ] Extend the data query with text filtering, bounded pagination, and
  deterministic ordering.
- [ ] Preserve the no-argument route and response shape.
- [ ] Add public API integration coverage for normal, boundary, tie, and
  invalid-input cases.
- [ ] Record the service evidence in the parent task before handing off to
  the client subtask.

### Requirement verification

- [ ] A public HTTP integration test proves bounded pagination returns the
  approved slice and rejects values outside the approved bounds.
- [ ] A public HTTP integration test proves sorting is deterministic for equal
  primary values and remains consistent across pages.
- [ ] A public HTTP integration test proves the approved text filter matches
  exactly the contract's fields and matching rules.
- [ ] A no-parameter HTTP test proves the existing all-notes list behavior is
  preserved.

### Additional implementation verification

- [ ] Verify the generated OpenAPI schema exposes the approved query
  parameters, bounds, and response shape.
- [ ] Verify tests do not rely on database insertion order or data left by a
  previous test.

# Expose notes queries through the reusable Python client

Parent Task: `tasks/20260919-notes-query-capability/000-main.md`

Depends On:
`tasks/20260919-notes-query-capability/010-public-contract.md`,
`tasks/20260919-notes-query-capability/020-api-query.md`

Map the approved notes-query contract into the independently maintained
`NotesClient` package without breaking existing callers of `list_notes()`.

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] `NotesClient.list_notes()` exposes the approved pagination, sorting, and
  text-filter controls using the public client surface.
- [ ] The client serializes only the approved query values and preserves the
  service's response shape.
- [ ] Existing `list_notes()` calls with no arguments remain valid and retain
  their current list-shaped behavior and request compatibility.
- [ ] Client tests cover argument mapping, omitted parameters, and the real
  service contract where integration coverage is needed.

## Unresolved requirement questions

The client method names, optional argument names, return shape, and invalid
input behavior remain blocked on the approved contract in
`tasks/20260919-notes-query-capability/010-public-contract.md`.

## Research and supporting facts

- `packages/notes_client/notes_client/client.py` currently accepts a transport
  and calls `get("/notes/")` without query parameters.
- The transport test fixture only returns an empty list and does not currently
  assert the requested path or query mapping.
- `packages/notes_client/README.md` documents only the no-argument method.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

After the API contract and service behavior are available, extend
`list_notes()` with optional arguments that map one-to-one to the approved
public query controls. Preserve the no-argument call path, then add focused
transport tests for serialization and an integration check against the service
for response handling.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- The client should not reimplement filtering, sorting, or pagination; it
  should send the approved query to the service.
- Omitted optional arguments must remain omitted from the request so an old
  no-argument caller does not receive an implicit client-side page.
- Whether the client validates locally or relies on API validation must follow
  the approved error contract; avoid silently accepting values the API rejects.
- Keep the existing injected transport seam for unit tests, while adding a
  real service-backed check for the public mapping.

### Documentation

- Update `packages/notes_client/README.md` with the approved method signature,
  query examples, response behavior, and no-argument compatibility.
- Link to the shared notes-query contract if it is created.
- Do not document unimplemented arguments while the plan remains a draft.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Add the approved optional query arguments to `list_notes()`.
- [ ] Serialize omitted and supplied values according to the contract.
- [ ] Preserve the existing no-argument request and return behavior.
- [ ] Add transport-level tests that assert exact query mapping.

target.title: Flask/Vue book discovery decomposition

# Make the Books discovery view scalable and shareable

Plan the Books-page discovery feature so a larger collection can be filtered, searched, paged, and shared through the URL while retaining the existing CRUD and unfiltered API contracts.

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] The Books page lets users filter by read status, search by title or author, and move through bounded pages.
- [ ] The selected discovery state is reflected consistently by the controls, active-control indicators, table rows, pagination bounds, and empty state.
- [ ] The current discovery state is shareable and restorable through the `/books` URL, including direct visits, reloads, and browser back/forward navigation.
- [ ] Add, update, and delete operations preserve the selected discovery view and refresh the table, controls, pagination, empty state, and URL consistently.
- [ ] Existing CRUD behavior remains available, and an unfiltered `GET /books` remains compatible with its current full-list response contract.

## Scope and workstreams

The work is split into independently owned boundaries:

1. Define the optional server-side discovery contract and data-selection behavior.
2. Build the client-side discovery state, transport parameters, controls, table, pagination, and empty-state rendering.
3. Synchronize that state with the router/history and make CRUD refreshes use the same state.
4. Add boundary-focused evidence and update the maintained development documentation after the behavior exists.

The task does not include sorting, bulk actions, authentication, persistence changes, or implementation in this planning pass.

## Open requirement questions

These public-behavior choices are not specified by the request and should be resolved before approval for execution:

- What query parameter names and response metadata should define the API/URL contract? A likely shape is a read-status value, a search term, a one-based page, and a fixed page size with total/page metadata, but the names and page size are not yet approved.
- Should title/author search be case-insensitive substring matching, and should one term be matched against either field? That is the recommended user-facing behavior, but it is still a semantic choice.
- When a filter or search changes, should the page reset to the first page? Resetting is the usual way to avoid an empty out-of-range view, but it changes navigation behavior.
- How should invalid or out-of-range page values be handled: normalize to a valid page, return a client error, or show an empty result? The choice affects both the API and URL canonicalization.
- What history granularity is desired for search input: every committed change, a debounced change, or a submit action? Filter and page changes can naturally create browser-history entries, but typing behavior needs an explicit policy.

## Research and supporting facts

- `server/app.py` currently serves `GET` and `POST` from the same `/books` route and returns `{"status": "success", "books": BOOKS}` for a GET with no query parameters.
- `server/query.py` currently exposes only a pass-through `list_books(books)` helper; no filtering or pagination exists.
- `client/src/api/books.js` already accepts an optional `params` object in `getBooks`, so the transport boundary can carry discovery parameters without changing the mutation functions.
- `client/src/components/Books.vue` currently keeps only a `books` array, loads the complete collection on mount, renders a minimal table or `No books found.`, and reloads the complete collection after each mutation.
- `client/src/router.js` declares `/books` with browser history but currently has no query-state parsing or navigation synchronization.
- Existing server coverage checks only basic GET and mutation status codes. The only Books component test covers the empty state with a mocked empty response; there is no router or production-transport integration coverage.
- `docs/development/index.md` currently states that no book-discovery specification exists. No feature documentation should be added until the supported behavior is implemented and verified.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Treat the approved API/query contract as the shared seam between the Flask and Vue work. Keep a canonical client discovery state rather than deriving separate values for the controls, request, table, and URL. Every state transition should pass through the same load-and-normalize path, including initial URL restoration, browser navigation, control changes, and CRUD refreshes.

The server work will add optional discovery selection while preserving the no-query behavior: an unfiltered `GET /books` continues to return the complete collection with the existing status and `books` fields, and POST/PUT/DELETE routes retain their current endpoints and mutation semantics. Filtered or explicitly paged requests will return the bounded result and the metadata required to render reliable page controls, subject to the unresolved contract decisions above.

The client work will make the discovery state explicit, send the selected state through `getBooks`, and render controls that remain visible and truthful when a query has no matches. The table will render only the selected page, pagination controls will be disabled or hidden at the appropriate bounds, and loading/empty results will not silently fall back to an unfiltered collection. Mutation methods will call the same state-aware loader after the existing API operation.

The router work will parse the `/books` query on entry and navigation, serialize canonical state changes back to the URL, and distinguish programmatic synchronization from user navigation so back/forward restores state without loops or stale results. If a mutation makes the current page invalid, the approved normalization policy will update both the displayed view and the URL.

Evidence will be added at the API boundary for selection, pagination, unfiltered compatibility, and mutation regressions; at the component/router boundary for controls, rendering, URL restoration, browser navigation, and CRUD refreshes; and at the nearest realistic integration boundary for transport/query wiring. Once verified, the maintained development documentation will describe the supported discovery query and URL behavior.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- Decision: keep `/books` as the public route and use its query string for discovery state; do not introduce a second discovery route.
- Decision: preserve the existing no-query full-list GET contract and existing CRUD endpoints as compatibility constraints.
- Decision: use one canonical discovery state as the source for request parameters, controls, rendered results, and URL synchronization.
- Open: approve the parameter names, page size, response metadata, search semantics, page-reset behavior, invalid-page policy, and history granularity listed above before execution.
- Recommendation: use case-insensitive matching against either title or author, a fixed default page size, one-based pages, and reset to page one when the filter/search changes. Record the final choices in the task before changing status to Approved.

### Documentation

- No documentation changes are made during this planning-only task.
- After implementation and verification, update `docs/development/index.md` or create a specifically owned feature page only if the final behavior needs more space. Document the supported read-status values, search semantics, pagination/query parameters, URL restoration, and mutation-refresh behavior.
- Do not describe target behavior as current guidance before the implementation is complete.

### Task checklist

- [ ] `tasks/20260919-books-discovery/010-api-discovery-contract.md` — define the Flask query/data-selection contract and compatibility evidence.
- [ ] `tasks/20260919-books-discovery/020-client-discovery-state.md` — define the Vue state, controls, rendering, pagination, and transport integration.
- [ ] `tasks/20260919-books-discovery/030-url-history-and-refresh.md` — define URL/history synchronization and state-preserving CRUD refreshes.
- [ ] `tasks/20260919-books-discovery/040-evidence-and-documentation.md` — define cross-boundary tests and the maintained documentation update.
- [ ] Resolve the open requirement questions and update the affected plan sections before execution approval.
- [ ] Keep this parent task in Draft until the requirements and public query contract are approved.

### Requirement verification

- Filter, search, and bounded-page behavior: verify through Flask API tests using the real route and data-selection helper, then through a Books component/integration test that sends the selected parameters and renders the returned page and metadata.
- Consistency of controls, active state, table, pagination, and empty state: verify with component tests covering an initial result, a filtered result, a no-match result, and a page-boundary result.
- URL sharing and restoration: verify with a router-backed test that mounts `/books` with query parameters, reloads/enters the route, changes state, and exercises back/forward navigation while asserting both request parameters and rendered controls.
- CRUD refresh consistency: verify through tests that add, update, and delete retain the canonical discovery state, reload through the selected query, and reconcile an invalidated page according to the approved policy.
- Existing CRUD and unfiltered API compatibility: verify the existing mutation route tests plus a no-query GET assertion that the full collection and current response fields remain available.

### Additional implementation verification

- Check for request/watch loops between component state and router query state.
- Check that a late response from an obsolete discovery request cannot overwrite a newer URL-selected view.
- Check that query serialization omits defaults or normalizes them consistently so equivalent views do not create needless history churn.

# Define the Books API discovery contract

Plan the Flask-side filtering, search, and bounded-pagination behavior that the Books page will consume while retaining the current unfiltered and CRUD API contracts.

Parent Task: tasks/20260919-books-discovery/000-main.md
Depends On: None

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] The GET books contract can select read status and search title or author using optional query inputs.
- [ ] Explicit discovery requests return a bounded page and enough metadata for the client to render reliable page controls.
- [ ] A GET with no discovery parameters remains a full-list response with the current `status` and `books` fields.
- [ ] Existing POST, PUT, and DELETE endpoints and their current mutation behavior remain intact.
- [ ] API evidence covers selection, pagination boundaries, unfiltered compatibility, and mutation regressions.

## Research and supporting facts

- `server/app.py` owns the `/books` GET/POST route and currently returns the complete module-level `BOOKS` list for GET.
- `server/app.py` owns the `/books/<book_id>` PUT/DELETE route; the request does not authorize changing that public endpoint.
- `server/query.py` has a pass-through `list_books` helper, which is the natural home for pure filtering/pagination transformations if that ownership remains appropriate.
- `tests/test_books_api.py` currently asserts only status codes, so response shape and selection semantics need focused coverage.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

First settle the shared query and response contract from the parent task. Then keep data selection in a pure, testable helper: preserve collection order, apply the approved read-status predicate, match the approved title/author search semantics, and calculate a bounded slice plus page metadata. The Flask route should parse request arguments, distinguish an absent discovery query from an explicit paged/discovery request, and serialize the result without mutating the source collection.

The no-query path must continue to expose the complete collection through the existing `status` and `books` fields so existing consumers remain compatible. Additive metadata or a paginated shape must not silently change that legacy path. Mutation routes should remain unchanged except for any tests needed to prove they continue to work after the GET logic is extended.

Add API tests for each approved read-status value, title-only and author-only matches, combined filtering, empty results, first/middle/last page boundaries, invalid input handling, and the no-query full-list contract. Keep the tests at the Flask test-client boundary and add helper-level tests only for calculations that are not meaningfully covered by route assertions.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- Decision: keep the server route at `/books` and make discovery inputs optional.
- Decision: do not paginate or filter the no-query compatibility path unless the approved contract explicitly changes that constraint.
- Open: parameter names, page size, response metadata, matching semantics, and invalid/out-of-range behavior are inherited from the parent task and must be resolved before implementation.
- Recommendation: preserve source order and use a deterministic one-based page model so the client can reason about page bounds without a sort contract.

### Documentation

- Document the final query parameters and response metadata in the feature/development documentation after the API behavior is implemented and tested.
- Do not update current guidance while this task remains a Draft plan.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Resolve and record the public query/response contract.
- [ ] Define the pure selection and pagination behavior, including invalid and out-of-range inputs.
- [ ] Define route-level compatibility behavior for a no-query GET.
- [ ] Plan focused Flask tests for positive, empty, boundary, and regression cases.
- [ ] Mark this subtask ready for execution only after the parent contract is approved.

### Requirement verification

- Optional read-status and title/author selection: Flask test-client requests with each approved query combination and exact returned IDs.
- Bounded pages and metadata: first/last/out-of-range route requests asserting returned slice and page metadata.
- No-query compatibility: a request without discovery parameters asserting the complete fixture collection and existing response keys.
- CRUD preservation: existing POST/PUT/DELETE tests plus a GET-after-mutation assertion where needed to prove the selection extension did not change mutation behavior.

Plan the Vue-side state, transport parameters, controls, table rendering, pagination, and empty-state behavior for the approved Books discovery contract.

Parent Task: tasks/20260919-books-discovery/000-main.md
Depends On: tasks/20260919-books-discovery/010-api-discovery-contract.md

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] The component has one canonical discovery state for read status, search, page, and the approved page-size/default values.
- [ ] Controls send the selected state through the existing API adapter and visibly retain their active values.
- [ ] The table renders only the selected page, and bounded pagination reflects the approved page metadata and disables or hides unavailable movement.
- [ ] The empty state represents the selected discovery query without clearing or hiding the active controls.
- [ ] Existing add, update, and remove methods remain available and can reload through the current discovery state.

## Research and supporting facts

- `client/src/components/Books.vue` currently stores only `books`, fetches all books in `mounted`, and has no controls or pagination.
- `client/src/api/books.js` already exposes `getBooks(params = {})`, so the client can pass query parameters without changing `addBook`, `updateBook`, or `deleteBook`.
- The current component test mocks all API functions and checks only the empty-state text; it does not assert request parameters or mutation refreshes.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Introduce an explicit discovery model whose normalized values drive the request, controls, table, pagination, and empty state. Keep the server response separate from the derived page display so metadata is not lost. Build the GET request from that model through `getBooks`, and make loading/error transitions preserve the selected controls rather than falling back to an unfiltered list.

Render the read-status selector and title/author search control as active, accessible inputs. Render the current page of rows and bounded navigation using the API’s approved metadata. Keep the controls visible when there are no matching rows and make the empty message describe the selected result set without implying that the underlying collection is empty unless that distinction is part of the approved copy.

Use one state transition path for initial values, user changes, and responses. Apply the approved page-reset and normalization rules when a query change invalidates the current page. Keep this subtask focused on component state and rendering; URL serialization and browser-history ownership are defined in the dependent URL/history subtask.

Add component tests with controlled API responses for default state, each read-status selection, search parameter construction, returned page rendering, first/last-page controls, no matches, and preservation of state through the mutation refresh hooks. Use a router-backed test only where the URL subtask needs it.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- Decision: the component’s request, rendered content, and controls must derive from one canonical discovery state.
- Decision: continue using the existing `getBooks`/CRUD adapter boundary rather than adding a second transport path.
- Open: exact state field names, default page size, search timing, and page-reset/normalization policy follow the parent contract.
- Recommendation: make filter changes and committed searches reset to page one, while keeping the search input’s displayed value stable during loading.

### Documentation

- Capture control semantics, empty-state behavior, and page navigation in the maintained Books/development documentation after implementation.
- Do not document unverified UI behavior during planning.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Resolve the API response fields and canonical client-state defaults.
- [ ] Define the control-to-state and state-to-request mappings.
- [ ] Define table, pagination, loading, and empty-state rendering rules.
- [ ] Define how mutation callbacks invoke the state-aware loader.
- [ ] Plan component tests for active controls, rendered page, boundaries, empty results, and refreshes.

### Requirement verification

- Canonical controls and request state: component test asserting control values and the exact `getBooks` parameters after each supported interaction.
- Table and pagination: component test with multi-page metadata asserting row IDs and navigation availability at both bounds.
- Empty state: component test with a no-match response asserting the empty message while active controls remain selected.

# Synchronize Books discovery with URL history and CRUD refreshes

Plan the router integration that shares and restores Books discovery state, handles browser navigation, and keeps mutation refreshes aligned with the selected view.

Parent Task: tasks/20260919-books-discovery/000-main.md
Depends On: tasks/20260919-books-discovery/020-client-discovery-state.md

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] A `/books` URL can encode the approved discovery state and restore it on direct entry and reload.
- [ ] User changes update the URL without losing the displayed controls or producing router/component synchronization loops.
- [ ] Browser back and forward restore the corresponding discovery state and reload the matching result page.
- [ ] Add, update, and delete refresh the current discovery query and reconcile page/URL changes if the result set changes.
- [ ] Existing `/books` navigation and CRUD endpoints remain usable when the URL has no discovery query.

## Research and supporting facts

- `client/src/router.js` uses `createWebHistory` and declares only the `/books` route; query handling is currently implicit and untested.
- `client/src/components/Books.vue` owns the current mutation methods, so the component and router need a deliberate synchronization boundary rather than independent URL and local state.
- The current API methods reload without parameters after mutations, which would discard any future filter/search/page selection.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Define a single parse/serialize mapping between the canonical component state and the `/books` query string. On route entry or a browser history event, parse and normalize the query before loading data. On a user state change, update the route and let the route-selected state drive the request, avoiding a second competing local copy. Normalize equivalent default values consistently so shared links remain stable.

Separate initial/programmatic route synchronization from user-originated navigation to avoid update loops. Test the chosen history policy with a memory history/router harness: direct query entry restores controls and data; a user transition changes the URL; back/forward restores prior selections and causes the correct GET request. Apply the approved search debounce/commit policy so typing does not unexpectedly create excessive history entries.

Route all add/update/delete follow-up loads through the same canonical state and URL-aware loader. If a mutation removes the last item from the current page or changes an item’s membership in the active filter, apply the approved page-normalization policy and update the URL before asserting the final table and empty state. Keep mutation endpoint calls and payloads unchanged.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- Decision: `/books` query parameters are the shareable source for discovery state; no separate storage mechanism is in scope.
- Decision: browser back/forward must be treated as state changes that reload data, not merely as URL changes.
- Open: exact serialization names/default omission, history granularity for search, and invalid/out-of-range normalization follow the parent task.
- Recommendation: push committed filter/page changes, use a debounced or committed search transition, and replace only canonicalization of an equivalent/default query.

### Documentation

- Document a copyable `/books` query example, restoration behavior, and the mutation-refresh rule after the URL contract is implemented and verified.
- Keep the current development documentation unchanged during planning.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Define the canonical query parser and serializer, including defaults and invalid values.
- [ ] Define the route-entry, user-change, and back/forward event flow.
- [ ] Define history behavior for filter, search, and page transitions.
- [ ] Define mutation refresh and page/URL reconciliation behavior.
- [ ] Plan router-backed tests for direct links, reload-equivalent entry, back/forward, and CRUD refreshes.

### Requirement verification

- Share/restore behavior: router-backed test starting at a fully specified `/books` query and asserting restored controls, request parameters, and rows.
- Browser navigation: memory-history test creating at least two discovery states, navigating back and forward, and asserting both URL and loaded result.
- CRUD consistency: integration test performing each mutation while a non-default discovery query is active and asserting the follow-up query, final URL, page bounds, and table/empty state.

# Add optional limit/offset pagination to GET /notes/

Planning handoff for adding optional `limit`/`offset` pagination to the notes
collection route: a bounded ascending-ID slice on request, the total note count
in a response header, unchanged full-list behavior without pagination,
standard FastAPI validation for bad values, and no changes to the other CRUD
routes. Planning only — implementation has not been approved or started.

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] R1 — `GET /notes/` accepts optional `limit` and `offset` query parameters; a paginated request returns a bounded slice of notes ordered by ascending `id`, as a bare JSON array with the same per-note shape as today.
- [ ] R2 — A paginated response carries the total note count in a response header (total = count of all notes in the table, not the remaining window; header name and presence scope per Q1/D1 below).
- [ ] R3 — A request without pagination parameters returns the current full-list JSON array, unchanged.
- [ ] R4 — Invalid `limit`/`offset` values (negative, non-integer) are rejected by FastAPI's standard validation (422); no custom validation code.
- [ ] R5 — All other routes (`POST /notes/`, `GET /notes/{note_id}/`, `PUT /notes/{note_id}/`, `DELETE /notes/{note_id}/`) keep their current behavior.
- [ ] R6 — `README.md` documents the changed collection behavior in the same reviewed change (AGENTS.md documentation policy).

## Open requirement questions (block execution)

- Q1 — Header presence scope: only on paginated responses, or on every `GET /notes/` response? Recommendation: paginated-only, so unpaginated responses stay byte-identical to today (strictest reading of R3) and every paginating client still receives the total.
- Q3 — Mixed parameter presence: either parameter alone triggers pagination (missing `offset` defaults to 0, missing `limit` means no upper bound), or both must be supplied together (422 otherwise). Recommendation: per-parameter defaults — simplest coherent contract; a lone `offset` returns the ascending tail.

## Supporting facts

- Routes live in `src/app/api/notes.py`; the router is mounted with prefix `/notes` (`src/app/main.py:15`). `GET /notes/` currently returns `await crud.get_all()` with no parameters, no `response_model`, and no headers (`src/app/api/notes.py:8-10`).
- `crud.get_all()` runs `database.fetch_all(notes.select())` with no explicit ORDER BY (`src/app/api/crud.py:4-5`). Other crud functions: `get`, `post`, `put`, `delete` (`src/app/api/crud.py:8-26`). CRUD route handlers take no query parameters.
- Data layer: `databases` async wrapper over SQLAlchemy Core against a SQLite file `./notes.db`, created at import time via `metadata.create_all(engine)` (`src/app/db.py`). Table columns: `id` (PK), `title`, `description`.
- Tests: `src/tests/test_notes.py` has two tests (full list → 200 + list; POST → 201). `src/tests/conftest.py` exposes a `test_app` fixture returning `TestClient(app)` without a context manager.
- Verified 2026-09-19 in a temporary venv (deps installed there, since removed; workspace untouched): with fastapi 0.141.1, starlette 1.6.0, databases 0.9.0, sqlalchemy 2.0.54, pydantic 2.13.5, Python 3.12 — the existing suite passes (2 passed) without lifespan running, because databases 0.9.0's SQLite backend connects lazily (`SQLiteBackend.connect()` is a no-op; the pool opens a connection per query). Dependencies in `pyproject.toml` are unpinned, so the executor must re-baseline at execution time.
- Verified in the same temporary environment with a throwaway app replicating the planned route shape:
  - `notes.select().order_by(notes.c.id.asc()).offset(o).limit(l)` returns the expected window; applying `.limit()` only when `limit` is not None works; `offset` beyond the table end returns `[]`; `limit=0` returns `[]`.
  - Count via `select(func.count()).select_from(notes)` + `fetch_one(...)[0]` returns the full-table count.
  - Setting a header on an injected `Response` parameter merges with the returned list body (no `JSONResponse` refactor needed).
  - `Query(default=None, ge=0)` yields 422 with the offending parameter located for `limit=-1`, `offset=-3`, `offset=abc`, `limit=1.5`; `limit=0&offset=-2` reports `offset`.
  - FastAPI auto-documents both optional parameters in `openapi.json`.
- Running the app or tests creates `./notes.db` relative to the CWD; `.gitignore` does not currently list it.
- Documentation surfaces: `README.md` (root, service-owned; currently states the collection route "returns every note as a JSON array"), `docs/development/index.md` ("No notes-query specification exists"), `docs/development/documentation.md` (process guidance). This variant has no client package or CLI.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Approach: keep the existing unpaginated code path untouched and add a paginated branch to the same route handler.

- Route (`src/app/api/notes.py`, `read_all_notes` only):
  - New parameters: `response: Response`, `limit: int | None = Query(default=None, ge=0)`, `offset: int | None = Query(default=None, ge=0)`.
  - Branch: when both `limit` and `offset` are `None` → `return await crud.get_all()` (current behavior, including absence of the header if Q1 is decided paginated-only).
  - Otherwise (paginated): `total = await crud.count()`, rows from `crud.get_paginated(limit, offset)` with missing `offset` treated as 0 and missing `limit` meaning no cap (per Q3), then `response.headers[...] = str(total)` and return the rows.
- CRUD (`src/app/api/crud.py`; `get_all` and the other four functions untouched):
  - `count()` → `database.fetch_one(select(func.count()).select_from(notes))`, return `row[0]`.
  - `get_paginated(limit, offset)` → `notes.select().order_by(notes.c.id.asc()).offset(offset)`, applying `.limit(limit)` only when `limit is not None`.
- API surface stays otherwise identical: no `response_model`, body remains a bare JSON array with the same per-note record shape, count is the full-table count, two sequential queries in paginated mode with no transaction wrapping.
- Explicitly out of scope: page-size cap (`le=`), page/next-link metadata, pagination on any other route, changes to `crud.get_all()` or the other route handlers.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

Decisions (visible for approval; locally reversible unless noted):

- D1 — Header name `X-Total-Count` (de-facto convention for collection totals; value is the decimal string of the full-table count). Public contract: confirm at approval.
- D2 — Validation bounds: `ge=0` on both parameters; `limit=0` is valid and returns an empty slice. No upper bound on `limit` (none requested; adding a cap would be a new constraint).
- D3 — Paginated response body stays a bare JSON array with the same per-note shape; no `response_model` added, keeping serialization identical to the current record dicts.
- D4 — The count query runs only on paginated requests (pairs with Q1 paginated-only). Accepted: a tiny read-consistency window between count and slice, acceptable at fixture scale.
- D5 — Only the paginated query is explicitly ordered `id asc`; `get_all()` stays unordered so the unpaginated path is unchanged (R3).
- D6 — CRUD helper names: `count()` and `get_paginated(limit, offset)`, matching the existing lowercase crud style.

Open (must be answered before approval; see top-level questions):

- Q1 — Header presence: paginated-only (recommended) vs every `GET /notes/` response.
- Q3 — Partial parameters: per-parameter defaults (recommended) vs requiring both together (422 otherwise).

### Documentation

- `README.md` (service-owned user documentation, root): extend the collection paragraph in the same reviewed change — unpaginated requests return the full array; optional `limit`/`offset` return an ascending-ID slice; paginated responses include the `X-Total-Count` header with the total note count (scope per Q1); invalid values produce standard FastAPI 422 errors. Shipped with the code, so no `Not implemented` marker.
- No new pages or directories: `docs/development/index.md` stays unchanged (no specification requested), and OpenAPI parameter documentation is generated automatically by FastAPI — no maintained generated source to regenerate.

### Task checklist

- [ ] 1. Baseline: create a venv, install `pyproject.toml` dependencies plus `pytest`, run `pytest src/tests` from the repo root, confirm the 2 existing tests pass, and record resolved versions (harness consumer check; note that this creates `./notes.db`).
- [ ] 2. `src/app/api/crud.py`: add `count()` and `get_paginated(limit, offset)` per the approach; leave `get_all` and the other functions untouched.
- [ ] 3. `src/app/api/notes.py`: extend `read_all_notes` with the parameters, branch, and header per the approach; leave the other four route handlers untouched.
- [ ] 4. Tests in `src/tests/test_notes.py` (using the existing `test_app` fixture; seed via `POST /notes/`; derive expectations differentially from a preceding full-list fetch so tests stay robust to rows left by other tests):
  - [ ] 4a. `limit=2&offset=1` returns ids 2–3 of the ascending-sorted full list; `X-Total-Count` equals the full-list length.
  - [ ] 4b. `limit=2` alone returns the first 2 ascending ids; `offset=2` alone returns the ascending tail from position 2.
  - [ ] 4c. `limit=0` → empty array + header; `offset` beyond the total → empty array + header.
  - [ ] 4d. Unpaginated request → 200 full array and (if Q1 paginated-only) no `X-Total-Count` header.
  - [ ] 4e. 422 for `limit=-1`, `offset=-2`, `offset=abc`, `limit=1.5` (standard FastAPI error body).
  - [ ] 4f. Regression round-trip for the other routes: create → read → update → delete; existing two tests remain untouched and passing.
- [ ] 5. `README.md`: update the collection paragraph in the same change as the code (audience: API clients of the notes service).
- [ ] 6. `.gitignore`: add `notes.db` (runtime artifact of running the app or tests).
- [ ] 7. Run the full suite twice (state-independence check against the persistent sqlite file) and confirm all tests pass; update the requirement evidence and this checklist.

### Requirement verification

- R1 + R2 — New integration tests through `TestClient` (real app + real SQLite across the HTTP boundary): window equality against the ascending-sorted full list, and `X-Total-Count` equal to the full-list length. No mocks bypassing the boundary.
- R3 — Existing `test_read_all_notes` still passes, plus the explicit no-header assertion (4d) if Q1 is paginated-only; diff review confirms `crud.get_all()` and the route defaults are untouched.
- R4 — 422 assertions in 4e against the standard FastAPI error body.
- R5 — Existing tests plus the new round-trip test (4f); diff review confirms the other route handlers are unchanged.
- R6 — Inspection of `README.md` in the same change; wording matches the implemented behavior.

### Additional implementation verification

- Run the suite twice in one session to prove tests do not depend on the persistent `./notes.db` contents (differential expectations should make this robust).
- After execution, `git status` should show only the intended files (`crud.py`, `notes.py`, `test_notes.py`, `README.md`, `.gitignore`, this task file) — `notes.db` must be ignored, not committed.

# Books CRUD refresh must preserve the selected filter

The Books page's All/Read/Unread filter is ignored when add, update, or delete
refresh the collection: the refetch always uses the unfiltered default. This
task plans the client-side fix so every CRUD refresh re-applies the active
filter while leaving the HTTP contract and unfiltered behavior untouched.
Planning only — no implementation performed for this task yet.

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] **R1 — CRUD refresh re-applies the selected filter.** After add, update,
  or delete, the collection refresh uses the currently selected filter
  (`all` / `read` / `unread`), so the visible list continues to reflect that
  filter instead of falling back to the unfiltered list. (Request: "reapply it
  whenever CRUD refreshes the collection".)
- [ ] **R2 — The selected filter stays visibly active.** Across CRUD
  refreshes, the filter control's pressed state keeps reflecting the user's
  selection (no reset to `all`) and the list content matches that selection.
  (Request: "Keep the selected filter visibly active".)
- [ ] **R3 — HTTP contract preserved.** Same endpoints and request semantics
  (`read=true` / `read=false` for filtered GETs, no query params for
  unfiltered GETs) and same `{status, books}` / `{status, book}` response
  shapes; `server/app.py` and the request mapping in
  `client/src/api/books.js` are not modified. (Request: "Preserve the existing
  API response shape".)
- [ ] **R4 — Unfiltered behavior preserved.** With All selected, add, update,
  and delete refreshes continue to display the full collection exactly as they
  do today. (Request: "Preserve … unfiltered behavior".)

Out of scope (not approved outcomes): initial-load fetch behavior (the
component fetches only on filter selection or after CRUD today), empty-state
copy, filter styling beyond the existing `aria-pressed` signal, and any server
behavior change.

## Open questions and decisions

- None unresolved. Two consequences follow directly from R1 and are treated as
  expected behavior, not bugs: a newly added or edited book that does not

# Blog archive pagination

Split the blog archive so `/blog/` stays the first archive page while stable
later pages carry at most twenty posts each, with accessible previous/next
navigation. Preserve the home page, tags, feed, sitemap, individual post
pages, post order, and static zero-JavaScript output. Planning only:
execution has not been approved.

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] 1. `/blog/` remains the first archive page at the same URL and continues
      to show posts newest-first, now limited to at most 20 posts.
- [ ] 2. Later archive pages are statically generated at stable, deterministic
      URLs, each containing at most 20 posts and continuing the same
      newest-first sequence. Stable means deterministic chunking from an
      explicit total order (date descending, deterministic tiebreak for equal
      dates): identical inputs produce identical pages.
- [ ] 3. Every archive page offers accessible previous/next navigation to the
      adjacent archive pages: a labeled `<nav>` with descriptive links, a link
      rendered only where an adjacent page exists, keyboard operable by
      default, no JavaScript.
- [ ] 4. Home page, tag pages, feed, and individual post pages keep their
      current URLs and output.
- [ ] 5. The sitemap remains valid and continues to enumerate the built public
      pages, including the generated archive pages.
- [ ] 6. Build output remains static files with zero client-side JavaScript.
- [ ] 7. Maintained documentation (README plus the development docs) reflects
      the paginated archive in the same change.

## Open questions

- Q1 (user-visible URLs, requirement-relevant): scheme for the later archive
  pages. Recommendation: one-based numbering, `/blog/2/`, `/blog/3/`, … via
  the documented conditional permalink. Eleventy's default pagination URLs
  would place the second page at `/blog/1/` (0-indexed), which reads as page
  "1" while being the second page. The choice changes shipped URLs and needs
  approval before implementation.
- Q2 (sitemap scope, clarification): generated archive pages will appear in
  the sitemap automatically because `content/sitemap.xml.njk` enumerates
  `collections.all`. Recommendation: keep that behavior (they are public
  indexable pages). Excluding them would require an extra filter and is not
  planned unless requested.

## Supporting details

- Eleventy ^3.0.0 (`package.json`); `eleventy.config.js` sets input
  `content/`, includes `../_includes`, output `_site/`; `npm run build` runs
  `eleventy`; `npm test` runs `node --test tests/*.test.js`. Dependencies are
  not installed in this workspace (`node_modules/` absent, gitignored).
- Current archive: `content/blog.njk` has `permalink: /blog/` and renders all
  of `collections.posts` through `_includes/postslist.njk`, which renders
  `postslist | reverse` (newest-first display; collections are
  date-ascending).
- Content: two posts (`content/posts/first.md` dated 2026-01-01, `second.md`
  dated 2026-01-02) tagged `posts` via `content/posts/posts.json`, layout
  `_includes/layouts/post.njk` (no per-post prev/next links exist today, so
  "individual-post navigation" means their current rendering stays as is).
  Post URLs are `/posts/first/`, `/posts/second/`, so `/blog/<n>/` cannot
  collide with post URLs.
- Other surfaces: `content/index.njk` shows the 3 newest posts (`head(-3)`);
  `content/tag-pages.njk` paginates over `collections` with
  `filter: [all, posts]`; `content/feed.xml.njk` lists all posts;
  `content/sitemap.xml.njk` enumerates `collections.all`.
- `tests/archive-output.test.js` contains only a comment ("Production-build
  coverage currently checks only that /blog/index.html exists.") — there are
  no actual assertions today, so real coverage must be written, not extended
  in place.
- `docs/development/index.md` states "No archive pagination specification
  exists."; there is no `docs/index.md`.
- Verified against the Eleventy 3 docs (11ty.dev/docs/pagination):
  - `pagination.reverse: true` reverses the whole data set before chunking, so
    page 1 holds the newest items of a date-ascending collection.
  - Default pagination URLs append a 0-indexed number for later pages
    (`_site/paged/index.html` and `_site/paged/1/index.html` in the docs
    example); a conditional permalink
    (`{% if pagination.pageNumber > 0 %}…{% endif %}`) keeps page 1 at its
    original URL while numbering later pages; in Nunjucks
    `{{ pagination.pageNumber + 1 }}` works (the Liquid caveat does not
    apply).
  - `pagination.href.previous` / `pagination.href.next` give adjacent page
    URLs (absent when there is no adjacent page); `pagination.items` is the
    current chunk (an array when size > 1); `pagination.pages` lists all
    chunks in order.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Approach:

1. Install dependencies (`npm install`) and confirm the production build
   succeeds on the unchanged site.
2. Convert `content/blog.njk` into a pagination template: pagination over the
   posts collection, `size: 20`, an alias for the current chunk (not `page`,
   which is reserved), and a conditional permalink so page 1 keeps `/blog/`
   and later pages become `/blog/2/`, `/blog/3/`, … (Q1).
3. Ordering (D2): paginate over an explicitly sorted copied collection added
   in `eleventy.config.js` via `addCollection` — posts sorted date
   descending with `inputPath` as the tiebreak for equal dates, paginated
   with `reverse: false`. Page 1 then holds the 20 newest posts and page
   boundaries are deterministic even for same-date posts. Alternative with
   confirmed semantics: `pagination.reverse: true` directly over
   `collections.posts`, accepting the default tiebreak; acceptable only if
   the same-date determinism test passes.
4. Keep `_includes/postslist.njk` unchanged (shared with home and tag pages).
   Because the include renders `postslist | reverse`, the archive sets
   `postslist` to the current chunk pre-reversed so the display stays
   newest-first; add a comment explaining the paired reversals and confirm
   the order from build output rather than reasoning alone.
5. Add the navigation to `content/blog.njk` after the post list: a
   `<nav aria-label="…">` containing "Newer posts" / "Older posts" links
   bound to `pagination.href.previous` / `pagination.href.next`, each
   rendered only when the href exists (no dead links), plus a "Page X of Y"
   indicator (D3). No scripts.
6. Change nothing else: `content/index.njk`, `content/tag-pages.njk`,
   `content/feed.xml.njk`, `content/sitemap.xml.njk`,
   `_includes/postslist.njk`, `_includes/layouts/post.njk`, and
   `content/posts/*` stay untouched. The new archive pages flow into
   `collections.all` — and therefore the sitemap — automatically.
7. Write the verification below, update README and the development docs in
   the same change, then keep this task file current while executing.

Boundaries:

- Only the blog archive pagination and its navigation; tag pagination, feed,
  sitemap and post templates, and post content are out of scope.
- No client-side JavaScript; no new build tooling beyond the config change
  needed for ordering.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- D1 (Q1, needs approval): later-page URL scheme — recommendation
  `/blog/{N}/` one-based (`/blog/2/` is the second page), implemented with
  the documented conditional permalink. Tradeoff: the Eleventy default needs
  no permalink logic but numbers pages 0-indexed (`/blog/1/` second);
  `/blog/page-2/` is equally valid if preferred. No other URL conflicts
  exist in this site.
- D2 (local, reversible): ordering mechanism — explicit derived collection
  (recommended, pins the same-date tiebreak) vs `pagination.reverse: true`
  over the default collection. Both put the newest posts on page 1.
- D3 (local, reversible): "Page X of Y" indicator — recommended, because
  landing on `/blog/3/` with only prev/next links gives little orientation;
  executor may include or omit without changing requirements.
- D4 (local, reversible): navigation labels — "Newer posts" / "Older posts"
  recommended; more meaningful than "Previous"/"Next" without page context.
- Pending resolution of Q1/Q2 the plan stays in `Draft`; implementation
  waits for approval.

### Documentation

- `README.md`: extend the existing build-output sentence with the paginated
  archive (at most 20 posts per page, previous/next links, no JavaScript) so
  the public claim ships in the same change as the behavior.
- `docs/development`: replace the "No archive pagination specification
  exists." line in `docs/development/index.md` with a short specification of
  the archive pagination contract (page size, URL scheme, ordering,
  navigation markup, zero-JS). Recommendation: a small dedicated page (e.g.
  `docs/development/archive-pagination.md`) linked from the index; inlining
  it in the index is acceptable if fewer files are preferred. Audience:
  maintainers. Describes shipped behavior only.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Install dependencies and verify `npm run build` succeeds on the
      unchanged site.
- [ ] Resolve Q1 (later-page URL scheme) and D2 (ordering mechanism).
- [ ] Implement pagination in `content/blog.njk` (plus the derived collection
      in `eleventy.config.js` if D2 resolves that way).
- [ ] Implement the accessible previous/next navigation markup.
- [ ] Build and inspect `_site/` output (archive pages, sitemap, feed) as a
      sanity check.
- [ ] Replace the placeholder in `tests/archive-output.test.js` with the
      integration coverage described under Requirement verification.
- [ ] Update `README.md` and the development docs in the same change.
- [ ] Record requirement evidence and progress here (Implementation Notes
      while executing; Completion Notes at the end).

### Requirement verification

- R1, R2 (archive pages, order, size, stability): integration test at the
  real build boundary — run the same production build command against a
  temporary copy of the site seeded with generated posts (distinct dates,
  plus same-date posts to pin the tiebreak), then assert on emitted files:
  `/blog/index.html` holds the 20 newest posts newest-first; later pages at
  the approved URLs hold the next chunks in order, each ≤ 20 posts; two
  builds of identical input emit byte-identical archive pages. Also assert
  the production two-post content still builds to a single `/blog/` page
  holding both posts with no navigation (feature dormant at current size).
- R3 (navigation): assertions on the emitted archive HTML: labeled `<nav>`;
  "Newer posts"/"Older posts" links with correct hrefs; a link exists only
  where an adjacent page exists (page 1 lacks "Newer posts", last page lacks
  "Older posts"); no `<script>` elements. Structural accessibility of real
  links is the evidence boundary; no screen-reader audit is planned.
- R4 (preserved surfaces): build before and after the change from identical
  input (temp site copies) and byte-compare the emitted home, tag, feed, and
  post files; alternatively pin their content with explicit assertions.
  Byte-identical output is the strongest evidence and cheap here.
- R5 (sitemap): assert the emitted sitemap contains every archive page URL
  and still contains all other public URLs.
- R6 (zero-JS): scan all emitted HTML for `<script` (and inline event
  handler attributes if cheap); expect none.
- R7 (documentation): reviewed during execution; final confirmation is the
  reviewer's read of the shipped docs.

### Additional implementation verification

- Pagination edge sizes in the test data: exactly 20 posts (single page, no
  navigation) and 21 posts (two pages; second page holds one post).
- Run the full `npm test` suite and confirm it collects the new tests and
  exits cleanly.

regression evidence, and the maintained API documentation; it does not
authorize implementation yet.

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] `GET /notes/` accepts optional `limit` and `offset` query parameters.
- [ ] A request using pagination returns notes as a bounded slice ordered by
      ascending note ID.
- [ ] A paginated response exposes the total number of notes in a response
      header.
- [ ] A request without pagination parameters keeps the current full-list JSON
      array behavior.
- [ ] Invalid pagination values are rejected by FastAPI's normal query
      validation and produce its standard validation response.
- [ ] The create, read-one, update, and delete routes retain their current
      behavior.

## Scope

This is a single deliverable at the public HTTP boundary. It includes focused
route-level integration tests and an update to the existing README. It does not
introduce a new response envelope, client package, CLI behavior, or unrelated
CRUD changes.

## Unresolved requirement questions

These choices affect the public contract and should be confirmed before
execution:

1. What exact response-header name should carry the total? Recommendation:
   `X-Total-Count`, unless the project has an external naming convention.
2. What validation bounds are required? The usual contract is
   `limit >= 1` and `offset >= 0`; the request does not specify whether
   `limit=0` is valid or whether there is a maximum limit.
3. When only one parameter is supplied, should the route paginate using the
   other parameter's default (`offset` alone skips, `limit` alone takes the
   first page), and should the total header appear for those partial requests?
4. Should the total header be emitted only when at least one pagination
   parameter is present, or also on the legacy full-list response?

Until these questions are answered, the checklist intentionally does not
claim a particular header spelling, numeric bound, default, or header-presence
policy.

## Research and supporting facts

- The collection route is `src/app/api/notes.py::read_all_notes`, currently
  with no query parameters, and it delegates to `src/app/api/crud.py::get_all`.
- `get_all` currently selects the complete `notes` table without an explicit
  ordering, limit, offset, or count query.
- The notes table has an integer primary-key `id`; the requested paginated
  order can therefore be expressed at the database query boundary.
- `src/tests/test_notes.py` currently checks only that `GET /notes/` returns
  status 200 and a JSON list, plus that creation is available.
- `README.md` is the only maintained user-facing package documentation found;
  `docs/development/index.md` records that no notes-query specification exists.
- The working tree was clean before this task file was added.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Add typed optional query parameters at the collection route and use FastAPI's
query validation for parsing and bounds. Preserve the existing no-parameter
path as a full list, while the paginated path obtains the total count
independently, applies explicit ascending-ID ordering, and applies the
requested offset and limit before returning the JSON array plus the agreed
header. Keep the single-note and mutation routes untouched.

Extend the public `TestClient` coverage with independent seeded notes to
prove:

- the no-parameter response remains a JSON array containing the full
  collection;
- a paginated response is ordered by ascending ID, bounded by the requested
  offset and limit, and carries the total count;
- partial-parameter behavior, once confirmed, follows the documented
  defaults;
- malformed, negative, zero, or otherwise out-of-range values covered by the
  agreed contract return FastAPI's normal 422 validation response;
- the existing CRUD smoke coverage still passes.

Update `README.md` only after the contract choices above are confirmed and
implemented. Document the query parameters, their validation, ordering,
response-header semantics, and the preserved full-list behavior. Do not
describe target behavior as current before implementation is complete.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

The task is intentionally a single task file because the change has one
public owner and one acceptance boundary, even though its execution includes
code, tests, and documentation. The exact header name, numeric bounds,
partial-parameter defaults, and whether the header is present on the legacy
response remain requirement questions listed above; execution should return
the plan to Draft if any answer changes the checklist.

### Documentation

During execution, update `README.md` as the maintained user-facing guide for
the notes API. No new documentation directory or placeholder notes-query
page is warranted by the current repository structure.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Confirm the unresolved public-contract questions.
- [ ] Mark this plan `Approved` before implementation begins.
- [ ] Implement optional collection pagination at the HTTP/database boundary.
- [ ] Add or update public route-level regression tests.
- [ ] Update the README with verified pagination behavior.
- [ ] Run the focused tests and the complete available test suite.
- [ ] Record implementation and completion notes with evidence.

### Requirement verification

- Full-list compatibility: a `TestClient` request to `GET /notes/` with no
  query parameters returns status 200 and the complete collection as a JSON
  array.
- Paginated slice and ordering: a `TestClient` request with confirmed
  pagination parameters returns only the requested bounded records in
  ascending ID order.
- Total count: the same public response includes the agreed total-count
  header whose value equals the number of stored notes, independent of the
  requested slice.
- Validation: public requests containing each agreed invalid value receive
  FastAPI's standard 422 response; tests must exercise the actual route
  boundary rather than calling query or CRUD helpers directly.
- CRUD preservation: the existing create/read/update/delete route coverage,
  supplemented where necessary to cover the changed collection's interaction
  with stored notes, continues to pass.

### Additional implementation verification

- Verify that the count is taken from the full notes collection and is not
  accidentally limited or offset.
- Verify that the no-pagination branch does not change the response shape to
  an envelope or alter unrelated route behavior.
- Run the repository's available test command and report any environment
  limitation rather than treating an uncollected or interrupted run as
  passing.

# Blog archive pagination

Plan the migration of the Eleventy blog archive from one unbounded page to a
stable, paginated archive while preserving the existing public output and
static-site behavior.

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] Keep `/blog/` as the first archive page and preserve the archive's
  existing post order.
- [ ] Generate stable later archive pages with no more than twenty posts per
  page.
- [ ] Add accessible previous/next navigation that exposes only the links
  valid for the current page.
- [ ] Preserve the home page, tag pages, feed, sitemap, individual-post
  routes/navigation, and post order.
- [ ] Keep the generated site usable without client-side JavaScript.

## Scope

This handoff covers archive pagination generation, archive-page navigation,
production-build regression coverage, and the small amount of developer
documentation needed to describe the supported archive URL behavior. It does
not change post content, collection semantics, the home-page post count, tag
page pagination, feed format, sitemap format, or individual-post templates
except where verification demonstrates an accidental regression.

## Subtasks

- [ ] tasks/20260919-blog-archive-pagination/010-archive-pagination-generation.md
- [ ] tasks/20260919-blog-archive-pagination/020-accessible-archive-navigation.md
- [ ] tasks/20260919-blog-archive-pagination/030-regression-coverage.md
- [ ] tasks/20260919-blog-archive-pagination/040-pagination-documentation.md

## Requirement questions and decisions

- Requirement question: what public URL pattern should later archive pages
  use? Recommendation: `/blog/page/2/`, `/blog/page/3/`, and so on, with
  `/blog/` reserved for page one. This is a user-visible URL contract and
  should be confirmed before execution.
- Preserved-contract decision: derive archive pages from the existing posts
  collection and retain the ordering currently produced by
  `_includes/postslist.njk`; pagination must not sort or reverse the
  collection a second time.
- Preserved-contract decision: use server-rendered semantic links for
  previous/next controls so navigation remains available in the static HTML
  and does not require JavaScript.

## Research and supporting facts

- `content/blog.njk` currently emits one page at `/blog/` and passes
  `collections.posts` to `_includes/postslist.njk`.
- `_includes/postslist.njk` renders an ordered list and reverses the supplied
  collection for display. The home page and tag pages reuse this include,
  while the feed reverses the collection independently.
- `content/tag-pages.njk` already uses Eleventy pagination to create one page
  per tag; its pagination behavior is separate from the archive change.
- `content/sitemap.xml.njk` iterates `collections.all`, so new archive output
  must be checked for expected sitemap inclusion without removing existing
  URLs.
- `tests/archive-output.test.js` currently contains only a comment saying that
  `/blog/index.html` should exist; it does not provide regression evidence.
- `docs/development/index.md` currently states that no archive pagination
  specification exists.
- The inspected post layout preserves title, author, and content but contains
  no explicit individual-post navigation control. Execution should verify the
  generated post routes and any existing post-navigation output before and
  after the change rather than inventing a new control.
- The fixture currently contains two dated posts, so the pagination test must
  exercise a production build with more than twenty posts in order to prove
  the page-size and later-page requirements.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Implement and verify the change in these boundaries:

1. Add Eleventy pagination to the archive source using the approved stable
   URL pattern. Keep page one at `/blog/`, use the same collection order as
   the current archive, and ensure every generated page receives only its
   page slice.
2. Add a shared or archive-specific semantic `<nav>` with an accessible
   label and clear previous/next link names. Render previous and next links
   conditionally at the page boundaries, using ordinary HTML links and no
   client-side behavior.
3. Replace the placeholder archive test with a production-build integration
   test. Exercise more than twenty posts and assert page sizes, deterministic
   URLs, page ordering, navigation boundaries, and absence of JavaScript
   dependency. Assert that the home page, tags, feed, sitemap, and individual
   post outputs retain their existing routes and ordering/contracts.
4. Update the owning development documentation after the URL convention is
   approved, describing `/blog/` and later archive pages as current supported
   behavior. Keep the README's static-site claim accurate; do not document
   the target behavior as current before implementation.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- Confirm the later-page permalink pattern before changing the public archive
  contract. The recommended pattern is `/blog/page/<page-number>/`.
- Decide during implementation whether the navigation markup belongs in the
  archive template or a narrowly scoped include; whichever location is
  chosen must not add navigation to the home, tag, feed, or post outputs.
- Use the production Eleventy build as the decisive test boundary. A
  test-time fixture with more than twenty real post documents is acceptable
  only if it invokes the normal build path and does not bypass collection or
  permalink behavior.

### Documentation

- Update `docs/development/index.md` from its current “no archive pagination
  specification exists” statement to the supported archive behavior after
  implementation and verification.
- Keep documentation scoped to the developer audience and the actual
  generated URL contract. Do not create a new documentation directory or
  placeholder specification.
- If the implementation changes any maintained public guidance in `README.md`,
  update it in the same reviewed change; otherwise leave the concise README
  unchanged.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Complete the archive pagination generation subtask.
- [ ] Complete the accessible archive navigation subtask.
- [ ] Complete the production-build regression coverage subtask.
- [ ] Complete the pagination documentation subtask.
- [ ] Resolve the later-page URL requirement question before execution.
- [ ] Run the production build and the focused archive test, recording any
  blocked verification.

### Requirement verification

- Archive first page and page-size limit: production-build assertions inspect
  `/blog/` and every generated later-page HTML file with more than twenty
  posts, checking that each page has at most twenty entries and that page one
  retains its existing route and order.
- Stable later pages: the same build asserts deterministic page URLs and
  expected links for at least pages two and three when enough fixture posts
  exist.
- Accessible previous/next navigation: HTML assertions inspect semantic
  navigation, accessible labeling, link text/targets, and the absence of a
  previous link on page one or a next link on the final page.
- Preserved site outputs: production-build assertions compare or structurally
  verify home, tag, feed, sitemap, and individual-post routes and ordering;
  the test must not replace those consumers with mocks.
- Static zero-JavaScript output: generated archive and navigation pages are
  inspected for ordinary links and no client-side script requirement; the
  build remains a static Eleventy output.

### Additional implementation verification

- Check that adding archive pages does not accidentally alter
  `collections.posts` ordering for the home page, tag pages, or feed.
- Check that `collections.all` still contains the existing URLs and that the
  sitemap behavior remains valid after pagination pages are introduced.

# Paginated blog archive

Plan the Eleventy archive change so a growing post collection remains browseable
through stable static pages while all existing site surfaces continue to use
the same post collection and ordering.

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] Keep `/blog/` as the first archive page.
- [ ] Generate deterministic later archive URLs with at most twenty posts per
      page.
- [ ] Preserve the existing newest-first post order across page boundaries,
      without dropping or duplicating posts.
- [ ] Add accessible previous/next navigation to archive pages, with only the
      links valid for the current page exposed.
- [ ] Preserve the home page, tag pages, feed, sitemap, and individual-post
      pages and navigation.
- [ ] Keep the archive output static and usable without client-side JavaScript.

## Open requirement questions and decisions

- Requirement question: confirm the public URL shape for later pages. The
  recommended convention is `/blog/2/`, `/blog/3/`, and so on, with the
  existing trailing-slash style; this is user-visible and should be confirmed
  before execution.
- Decision: scope pagination to the archive template. Do not paginate or
  reorder the global `collections.posts` collection, because the home page,
  tags, feed, sitemap, and individual posts consume it independently.
- Decision: use Eleventy’s build-time pagination and rendered links. No
  browser-side state, fetches, or JavaScript navigation is part of the
  design.
- Decision: the archive must render one canonical post list per page. The
  current template invokes the shared list include and then emits another
  archive list; retaining both would make a twenty-post page contain duplicate
  entries and would violate the page-size requirement.

## Supporting facts

- `content/blog.njk` currently owns `/blog/`, passes the complete
  `collections.posts` collection to `_includes/postslist.njk`, and separately
  loops over the reversed collection.
- `_includes/postslist.njk` reverses its `postslist` input before rendering.
  Pagination must therefore establish newest-first page boundaries before the
  include’s local ordering behavior is applied; reversing each already-sliced
  page would group the wrong posts.
- `content/index.njk`, `content/tag-pages.njk`, `content/feed.xml.njk`, and
  `content/sitemap.xml.njk` consume the collection through separate templates.
  `content/posts/posts.json` and `_includes/layouts/post.njk` own individual
  post rendering.
- The existing archive test only documents that `/blog/index.html` exists; it
  does not currently build and inspect page contents or any preservation
  surfaces.
- `README.md` describes the generated site at a high level, while
  `docs/development/index.md` explicitly notes that no archive pagination
  specification exists. `docs/development/documentation.md` was reviewed
  before planning this documentation change.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Implement archive-only Eleventy pagination using the confirmed later-page URL
convention. Feed the paginator an ordering that preserves the current
newest-first archive semantics, partition into pages of twenty, and retain
the `/blog/` permalink for page one. Render the page’s posts once through the
existing presentation conventions, then add a semantic navigation region with
visible Previous/Next links, appropriate `rel` values, and no invalid link on
the first or final page.

Extend the production-build test to use enough deterministic posts to exercise
the first, middle, and final page states. Assert page size, URL stability,
boundary navigation, cross-page ordering, complete non-overlapping coverage,
and absence of archive JavaScript. In the same build, assert that the home
page, tags, feed, sitemap, and individual-post output remain present and
consistent with the pre-pagination collection behavior.

Update the maintained README and development archive note after the behavior
is implemented, documenting the public archive URL pattern, twenty-post
limit, and static navigation. Do not publish the target behavior as current
documentation while this plan remains unimplemented.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- Resolve the later-page permalink question before marking this plan
  `Approved`; `/blog/2/` is the working recommendation.
- Prefer Eleventy pagination metadata for previous/next targets so links are
  generated from the same page graph as the output. The exact Nunjucks
  property names should be verified against the installed Eleventy version
  during implementation.
- Keep collection order and all non-archive templates unchanged. If the
  shared include cannot express the required archive ordering without
  affecting home or tag output, use archive-local rendering rather than
  changing those consumers’ contracts.
- Use a realistic production build with a collection large enough to exercise
  all navigation states. Do not mock pagination metadata or test a
  JavaScript-only fallback.

### Documentation

- Update `README.md` with the supported archive pagination behavior once it is
  implemented and verified.
- Replace the stale archive note in `docs/development/index.md` with the
  current URL and page-size contract, or remove it if the maintained
  documentation no longer needs a separate archive specification.
- No documentation files are changed during this planning-only request.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Confirm the later-page URL convention and approve this execution plan.
- [ ] Implement archive-only build-time pagination with a twenty-post page
      size and stable first-page permalink.
- [ ] Preserve newest-first ordering and eliminate duplicate archive entries
      while leaving other collection consumers unchanged.
- [ ] Add semantic, visible previous/next archive navigation with correct
      first/middle/final-page behavior.
- [ ] Expand or arrange realistic build input and update production-build
      regression coverage for pagination and preserved site surfaces.
- [ ] Update maintained README/development documentation.
- [ ] Run the focused test and production build, then record evidence and any
      deviations in the task file.

### Requirement verification

- First-page and later-page URL requirements: inspect the built `_site` paths
  and assert the first archive is `/blog/` while later pages follow the
  approved stable convention.
- Page-size and ordering requirements: parse every generated archive page,
  assert no page contains more than twenty post entries, and compare the
  concatenated links against the expected newest-first collection with no
  gaps or duplicates.
- Navigation requirement: assert first, middle, and final pages expose the
  correct visible Previous/Next links and omit links that have no destination.
- Preservation requirements: build and inspect home, tag, feed, sitemap, and
  representative individual-post URLs and content; compare their post order
  or membership to the unpaginated collection contract where applicable.
- Static-output requirement: inspect generated archive HTML and the output
  asset set for absence of client-side JavaScript dependencies.
