task_files.tasks/books-discovery/000-main.md:
# Books discovery for larger collections

Plan the cross-layer work that makes the Books page usable with a larger
collection while preserving existing CRUD behavior and callers of the
unfiltered API.

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] The Books page lets users filter books by read status.
- [ ] The Books page searches by title or author.
- [ ] The Books page lets users move through bounded result pages.
- [ ] The current discovery state can be shared and restored through the URL,
  including after a reload or a direct visit to a copied URL.
- [ ] The table reflects the selected discovery view, including its current
  page of results.
- [ ] The filter and search controls visibly reflect the selected discovery
  state.
- [ ] The empty state accurately describes the selected view when it has no
  matching books and updates after navigation or a mutation without showing
  stale rows.
- [ ] Browser back and forward navigation restore the corresponding discovery
  state and results.
- [ ] Add, update, and delete refreshes retain the active discovery state and
  leave the table, controls, pagination, and empty state consistent with the
  refreshed collection.
- [ ] Existing CRUD operations and endpoint behavior remain usable.
- [ ] A request to the books API without discovery parameters remains
  compatible with existing callers and returns the unfiltered collection in
  its current response shape.

## Unresolved requirement questions and decisions

- **Question — discovery parameter vocabulary:** What public query keys and
  values should represent read status, text search, and page selection? The
  working recommendation is `read`, `q`, and `page`, with an omitted `read`
  meaning all books and a one-based `page`.
- **Question — search semantics:** Should title/author matching be
  case-insensitive substring matching, and should surrounding whitespace be
  trimmed? The working recommendation is trimmed, case-insensitive matching
  against either field, combined with the read-status filter.
- **Question — page size:** Should the page size be fixed by the API or
  user-selectable? The working recommendation is a fixed bounded page size so
  the URL only represents discovery choices named in the request.
- **Question — response metadata:** How should filtered requests expose total
  results and page bounds? The working recommendation is to add pagination
  metadata for parameterized requests while leaving the no-parameter response
  shape unchanged.
- **Question — canonical URL and mutations:** Should default values be omitted
  from the URL, and should a mutation that removes the last item on a page
  clamp to the final valid page or return to page one? The working
  recommendation is to omit defaults, reset to page one when search/filter
  criteria change, and clamp a now-invalid page to the final valid page.

These questions must be resolved before execution because their answers affect
the public API, shareable URLs, and visible navigation behavior.

## Research and supporting facts

- `server/app.py` currently returns the entire `BOOKS` list for every GET
  request to `/books`; it does not inspect query parameters. The no-parameter
  response is `{"status": "success", "books": ...}`.
- `server/query.py` currently contains only `list_books(books)`, which returns
  a copy of its input and is an available ownership point for selection
  logic.
- `client/src/api/books.js` already accepts an optional `params` object for
  `getBooks`, but `Books.vue` only calls it without parameters.
- `client/src/components/Books.vue` stores only the loaded books, renders a
  table or `No books found.`, and refreshes after add, update, and delete
  without preserving a discovery context.
- `client/src/router.js` currently defines only the `/books` route and uses
  Vue Router history mode; no query-state behavior is configured or tested.
- Existing server coverage checks only the GET status and basic mutation
  status codes. The Books component has one empty-state test, and the client
  integration file contains no production transport coverage.
- `docs/development/index.md` states that no book-discovery specification
  exists. No implementation or documentation changes are authorized by this
  planning request.

## Scope and workstreams

The work is intentionally split at independently owned boundaries:

1. Define and test optional server-side selection and pagination while keeping
   the no-parameter API contract intact.
2. Connect the selection contract to URL query state, including initialization,
   canonical updates, and browser navigation.
3. Integrate the state into the Books view so rendering and CRUD refreshes use
   one selected view.

Cross-boundary verification and documentation remain part of the main task
because they validate the complete user-visible behavior rather than
constituting another independently useful product layer.

## Subtasks

- [ ] [tasks/books-discovery/010-api-discovery-contract.md](010-api-discovery-contract.md)
  — define server-side filtering, search, pagination, and compatibility
  coverage.
- [ ] [tasks/books-discovery/020-url-state-transport.md](020-url-state-transport.md)
  — connect API selection parameters to shareable URL state and browser
  navigation.
- [ ] [tasks/books-discovery/030-books-view-discovery.md](030-books-view-discovery.md)
  — render controls and bounded navigation and keep table, empty state, and
  CRUD refreshes synchronized.

## Execution plan
Status: Draft

Resolve the public query vocabulary, matching rules, page-size policy, response
metadata, and mutation clamping behavior before implementation begins. Then
execute the subtasks in dependency order:

1. Implement and test the optional API selection contract in the Flask layer.
2. Use that contract in the client transport and Books route/view URL state,
   with browser navigation driving the same state-to-fetch path as initial
   loading.
3. Add the visible controls, active-state presentation, bounded page
   navigation, no-match handling, and mutation refresh behavior.
4. Verify the full path at server, component, and router/integration
   boundaries. Confirm that unfiltered API callers and existing CRUD behavior
   remain covered.
5. Update the maintained development documentation with the implemented API
   query contract and URL behavior; do not present the target behavior as
   current guidance before implementation is complete.

The implementation should have one normalized discovery-state representation
used for URL serialization, API requests, rendering, and post-mutation
refreshes. Criteria changes should invalidate an old page selection, while
browser navigation should restore the exact state encoded by each history
entry. The final behavior should make no-match results distinguishable from a
successful page containing books without introducing a second, contradictory
state source.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

The proposed main-task-plus-three-subtask structure matches the ownership
boundaries already present in the repository: `server/query.py` and the Flask
route own selection, the API adapter/router own transport and URL state, and
`Books.vue` owns rendering and mutation refreshes. The split should be
reconsidered if the resolved API contract makes selection entirely client-side,
because that would remove the independently useful server workstream.

The material open questions are the five questions listed above. In
particular, changing the no-parameter response shape would violate the
compatibility requirement, while changing query names or default omission
rules would change shareable URLs. Resolve these with the product owner before
marking the plan Approved.

### Documentation

After implementation, add the smallest maintained developer-facing
documentation needed for the new public behavior under `docs/development/`.
It should cover the optional `/books` query parameters, response pagination
metadata, URL query state, default omission/canonicalization, and how CRUD
refreshes preserve the selected view. Update
`docs/development/index.md` if a new focused guide is added. Do not create
documentation during this planning-only task.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Resolve the requirement questions and approve the API/URL contract.
- [ ] Complete `010-api-discovery-contract.md`.
- [ ] Complete `020-url-state-transport.md`.
- [ ] Complete `030-books-view-discovery.md`.
- [ ] Add cross-boundary evidence for shared URLs, browser navigation, and
  mutation refreshes.
- [ ] Update maintained development documentation after the behavior exists.
- [ ] Append completion notes only after all requirements have evidence.

### Requirement verification

- **Filtering, search, bounded pages:** server API tests should exercise each
  supported read-status and search combination, page boundaries, empty
  results, and metadata used by the client. Component or integration tests
  should prove the controls issue the selected request and render its result.
- **Share/restore and browser navigation:** router-level tests should start
  from a URL, verify controls and results, navigate to another state, and
  exercise back/forward restoration through the real route/query mechanism.
- **Consistent table, active controls, and empty state:** Books view tests
  should cover a populated page, no matches for active criteria, and a valid
  empty page after a refresh or clamped navigation state.
- **CRUD refresh consistency:** view tests should invoke add, update, and
  delete with a non-default discovery state and assert that the subsequent
  GET uses that same normalized state and updates all visible regions.
- **Compatibility:** Flask API tests should assert the existing no-parameter
  response shape and full collection, alongside unchanged POST, PUT, and
  DELETE behavior. Existing tests count as evidence only when the enhanced
  implementation still satisfies their original boundary.

# Define the Books discovery API

Own the server-side filtering, title/author search, bounded pagination, and
unfiltered compatibility contract needed by the larger-collection Books page.

Parent Task: tasks/books-discovery/000-main.md

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] `GET /books` supports the agreed optional read-status filter.
- [ ] `GET /books` supports the agreed title-or-author search behavior.
- [ ] Parameterized requests return bounded pages and enough metadata for the
  client to render valid navigation.
- [ ] Requests without discovery parameters remain compatible with existing
  callers, including the current unfiltered response shape and collection.
- [ ] Existing POST, PUT, and DELETE behavior remains available to current
  callers.

## Supporting facts

- The route in `server/app.py` currently ignores `request.args` and returns
  the mutable global collection directly in a `status`/`books` envelope.
- `server/query.py` is the existing home for list-selection logic but currently
  only copies an input iterable.
- `tests/test_books_api.py` has no assertions for response contents, query
  parameters, pagination, or mutation effects beyond HTTP status.

## Execution plan
Status: Draft

Define the optional query contract first, including accepted values,
case/whitespace behavior, page numbering, page size, ordering, and metadata.
Keep the no-argument branch compatible with the current response contract.
Place reusable filtering/search/pagination calculations in the query module and
keep the Flask route responsible for request parsing and response assembly.
Do not alter mutation endpoint shapes unless the resolved discovery contract
shows a necessary compatibility-preserving correction.

Add server tests at the Flask test-client boundary for unfiltered
compatibility, each selection dimension, combined selection, page limits,
out-of-range behavior, and no-match responses. Retain the existing mutation
tests and add assertions only where needed to demonstrate that CRUD endpoints
remain usable.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

This subtask recommends server-side selection because the requested use case is
a larger collection and the repository already exposes an API query-parameter
hook. The public parameter names, matching rules, page-size policy, metadata
shape, and out-of-range behavior remain unresolved in the parent task and
must be approved before this subtask starts.

### Documentation

Provide the API facts needed by the parent task's maintained development guide
after the contract is implemented. Do not update current documentation during
the planning-only phase.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Resolve the API contract questions from the parent task.
- [ ] Implement selection logic and route parsing.
- [ ] Preserve and test the no-parameter response contract.
- [ ] Add or update server API tests for selection and pagination.
- [ ] Report response and ordering facts back to the parent task.

### Requirement verification

- The Flask test client must prove filtered and paginated results at the
  public `/books` boundary, not only test a helper in isolation.
- A no-parameter request must prove the existing envelope and full collection
  remain available.
- Existing POST, PUT, and DELETE tests must continue to collect and pass.

# Connect Books discovery to URL state

Own client query serialization, route initialization, share/restore behavior,
and browser history navigation for the Books discovery state.

Parent Task: tasks/books-discovery/000-main.md

Depends On: tasks/books-discovery/010-api-discovery-contract.md

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] The client sends the normalized discovery state using the agreed API
  query keys and values.
- [ ] A direct `/books` URL initializes the default discovery view.
- [ ] A URL containing discovery state restores the same filter, search, and
  page after reload or sharing.
- [ ] State changes produce canonical browser URLs and history entries
  according to the approved navigation policy.
- [ ] Browser back and forward restore the corresponding URL state and trigger
  the matching data view.
- [ ] Unfiltered loading remains compatible with the existing API adapter and
  no-parameter endpoint behavior.

## Supporting facts

- `client/src/api/books.js` already accepts `getBooks(params = {})` and passes
  `params` to Axios, so the transport boundary can be extended without
  changing mutation functions.
- `client/src/router.js` has a single `/books` route using
  `createWebHistory()` but currently has no query-state logic.
- `Books.vue` owns the current fetch calls, so URL-driven state must be made
  available there without creating a second independent state representation.

## Execution plan
Status: Draft

Create one normalized representation for read status, search text, and page.
Define parsing and serialization rules that reject or normalize invalid
values consistently with the approved API contract. Initialize it from the
route query, serialize user changes using the approved push/replace policy,
and ensure route-query changes from browser navigation reuse the same fetch
path as direct user changes.

Keep default state canonical and avoid emitting redundant query keys when the
approved policy says they are omitted. Preserve the active state across
ordinary API refreshes and expose the normalized request parameters to the
Books view so CRUD refreshes cannot accidentally fall back to an unfiltered
request.

Add client tests for direct URL restoration, query serialization, criteria
changes, page changes, back/forward navigation, invalid or missing defaults,
and the no-parameter path. Use router-level coverage for history behavior and
unit/component coverage for pure normalization where useful.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

The parent task recommends `read`, `q`, and `page` as the URL/API vocabulary,
omitting default values and resetting page to one when criteria change. Those
choices are material because they define URLs users can bookmark and share;
do not hard-code them until the parent task resolves the corresponding
questions.

The API dependency is intentional: this subtask must consume the server's
approved metadata and bounds rather than infer page validity from the current
page alone.

### Documentation

Record the final URL query keys, default omission, history behavior, and
reload/share semantics for the parent task's development documentation after
implementation. No current guidance is changed during planning.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Confirm the server query contract and URL vocabulary.
- [ ] Implement normalization, parsing, and serialization.
- [ ] Wire route-query changes to data loading and browser navigation.
- [ ] Preserve the no-parameter client/API path.
- [ ] Add router and client tests for share/restore and history behavior.

### Requirement verification

- A router-level test must mount the real `/books` route, start from a
  parameterized URL, and prove the corresponding API request and visible state.
- The same test boundary must exercise back and forward navigation and prove
  that both URL and results are restored.
- Client transport tests must prove omitted defaults do not create accidental
  query parameters and that the unfiltered call remains valid.

# Integrate discovery into the Books view

Own the Books page controls, active-state rendering, bounded navigation,
empty-state behavior, and CRUD refresh consistency.

Parent Task: tasks/books-discovery/000-main.md

Depends On: tasks/books-discovery/010-api-discovery-contract.md,
tasks/books-discovery/020-url-state-transport.md

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] The page renders a read-status control whose active value matches the
  normalized discovery state.
- [ ] The page renders title/author search and keeps its displayed value
  synchronized with discovery state.
- [ ] The table renders only the selected page of matching books.
- [ ] Bounded pagination controls expose valid navigation and active position
  using API metadata.
- [ ] The no-match empty state reflects the active view without displaying a
  stale prior page.
- [ ] Add, update, and delete refreshes request and render the active
  discovery view, including the approved behavior when a mutation invalidates
  the current page.
- [ ] Existing CRUD methods and behavior remain usable.

## Supporting facts

- `Books.vue` currently has only a `books` array in component data and no
  controls, pagination state, loading state, or route state.
- The component already refreshes after `add`, `update`, and `remove`, but
  every refresh calls `getBooks()` without parameters.
- The existing component test covers only the empty text and mocks all API
  methods; there is no evidence for populated rows, controls, URL state, or
  mutation refreshes.

## Execution plan
Status: Draft

Render controls from the normalized route/discovery state and route all
criteria and page changes through the URL-state owner. Render the table from
the current response page and use the approved pagination metadata to disable
or hide invalid navigation. Keep the empty state tied to the current
response, so no-match results cannot leave stale rows visible and a valid
non-empty page cannot show the no-match message.

Refactor the existing post-CRUD reload path to reuse the active normalized
discovery state. Apply the approved page correction when a mutation changes
the result count, then update the URL and reload once through the same path
used by navigation. Preserve the existing mutation API calls and their
successful refresh behavior.

Extend component tests for active controls, filtered/search results, page
navigation, no-match state, page-boundary behavior, and each CRUD refresh
under a non-default view. Add the smallest router-backed integration coverage
needed to ensure this component responds to browser navigation rather than
only to synthetic local state changes.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

The visible page behavior depends on the parent decisions about read values,
search matching, page size/metadata, URL canonicalization, and mutation
clamping. In particular, the page should not invent a separate local page
calculation if the API is the source of truth for bounds.

The current template has no visible add/edit/delete controls, although the
component exposes mutation methods. This plan preserves those methods and
their refresh behavior; adding new CRUD affordances is out of scope unless
the product owner separately requires them.

### Documentation

Document the final control labels, empty-state meaning, pagination behavior,
and mutation refresh semantics in the maintained Books/discovery development
guide after implementation. Do not add user-facing claims during planning.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Consume the approved normalized discovery state and API metadata.
- [ ] Add read-status and title/author search controls.
- [ ] Add bounded pagination and active-state presentation.
- [ ] Keep table and empty state synchronized with the selected response.
- [ ] Preserve active state during add, update, and delete refreshes.
- [ ] Add component and router-backed integration coverage.

### Requirement verification

- Component tests must prove control values and table rows correspond to the
  selected state for populated and no-match responses.
- Pagination tests must prove first/last-page bounds and the approved behavior
  for an invalidated page after mutation.
- CRUD tests must invoke each existing mutation method while a non-default
  filter/search/page is active and assert the follow-up GET retains that state.
- Router-backed tests must verify that view rendering changes when browser
  history restores a different discovery state.

# Make the Books discovery view scalable and shareable

Plan the Books-page discovery feature so a larger collection can be filtered, searched, paged, and shared through the URL while retaining the existing CRUD and unfiltered API contracts.

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] The Books page lets users filter by read status, search by title or author, and move through bounded pages.
- [ ] The selected discovery state is reflected consistently by the controls, active-control indicators, table rows, pagination bounds, and empty state.
- [ ] The current discovery state is shareable and restorable through the `/books` URL, including direct visits, reloads, and browser back/forward navigation.
- [ ] Add, update, and delete operations preserve the selected discovery view and refresh the table, controls, pagination, empty state, and URL consistently.
- [ ] Existing CRUD behavior remains available, and an unfiltered `GET /books` remains compatible with its current full-list response contract.

## Scope and workstreams

The work is split into independently owned boundaries:

1. Define the optional server-side discovery contract and data-selection behavior.
2. Build the client-side discovery state, transport parameters, controls, table, pagination, and empty-state rendering.
3. Synchronize that state with the router/history and make CRUD refreshes use the same state.
4. Add boundary-focused evidence and update the maintained development documentation after the behavior exists.

The task does not include sorting, bulk actions, authentication, persistence changes, or implementation in this planning pass.

## Open requirement questions

These public-behavior choices are not specified by the request and should be resolved before approval for execution:

- What query parameter names and response metadata should define the API/URL contract? A likely shape is a read-status value, a search term, a one-based page, and a fixed page size with total/page metadata, but the names and page size are not yet approved.
- Should title/author search be case-insensitive substring matching, and should one term be matched against either field? That is the recommended user-facing behavior, but it is still a semantic choice.
- When a filter or search changes, should the page reset to the first page? Resetting is the usual way to avoid an empty out-of-range view, but it changes navigation behavior.
- How should invalid or out-of-range page values be handled: normalize to a valid page, return a client error, or show an empty result? The choice affects both the API and URL canonicalization.
- What history granularity is desired for search input: every committed change, a debounced change, or a submit action? Filter and page changes can naturally create browser-history entries, but typing behavior needs an explicit policy.

## Research and supporting facts

- `server/app.py` currently serves `GET` and `POST` from the same `/books` route and returns `{"status": "success", "books": BOOKS}` for a GET with no query parameters.
- `server/query.py` currently exposes only a pass-through `list_books(books)` helper; no filtering or pagination exists.
- `client/src/api/books.js` already accepts an optional `params` object in `getBooks`, so the transport boundary can carry discovery parameters without changing the mutation functions.
- `client/src/components/Books.vue` currently keeps only a `books` array, loads the complete collection on mount, renders a minimal table or `No books found.`, and reloads the complete collection after each mutation.
- `client/src/router.js` declares `/books` with browser history but currently has no query-state parsing or navigation synchronization.
- Existing server coverage checks only basic GET and mutation status codes. The only Books component test covers the empty state with a mocked empty response; there is no router or production-transport integration coverage.
- `docs/development/index.md` currently states that no book-discovery specification exists. No feature documentation should be added until the supported behavior is implemented and verified.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Treat the approved API/query contract as the shared seam between the Flask and Vue work. Keep a canonical client discovery state rather than deriving separate values for the controls, request, table, and URL. Every state transition should pass through the same load-and-normalize path, including initial URL restoration, browser navigation, control changes, and CRUD refreshes.

The server work will add optional discovery selection while preserving the no-query behavior: an unfiltered `GET /books` continues to return the complete collection with the existing status and `books` fields, and POST/PUT/DELETE routes retain their current endpoints and mutation semantics. Filtered or explicitly paged requests will return the bounded result and the metadata required to render reliable page controls, subject to the unresolved contract decisions above.

The client work will make the discovery state explicit, send the selected state through `getBooks`, and render controls that remain visible and truthful when a query has no matches. The table will render only the selected page, pagination controls will be disabled or hidden at the appropriate bounds, and loading/empty results will not silently fall back to an unfiltered collection. Mutation methods will call the same state-aware loader after the existing API operation.

The router work will parse the `/books` query on entry and navigation, serialize canonical state changes back to the URL, and distinguish programmatic synchronization from user navigation so back/forward restores state without loops or stale results. If a mutation makes the current page invalid, the approved normalization policy will update both the displayed view and the URL.

Evidence will be added at the API boundary for selection, pagination, unfiltered compatibility, and mutation regressions; at the component/router boundary for controls, rendering, URL restoration, browser navigation, and CRUD refreshes; and at the nearest realistic integration boundary for transport/query wiring. Once verified, the maintained development documentation will describe the supported discovery query and URL behavior.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- Decision: keep `/books` as the public route and use its query string for discovery state; do not introduce a second discovery route.
- Decision: preserve the existing no-query full-list GET contract and existing CRUD endpoints as compatibility constraints.
- Decision: use one canonical discovery state as the source for request parameters, controls, rendered results, and URL synchronization.
- Open: approve the parameter names, page size, response metadata, search semantics, page-reset behavior, invalid-page policy, and history granularity listed above before execution.
- Recommendation: use case-insensitive matching against either title or author, a fixed default page size, one-based pages, and reset to page one when the filter/search changes. Record the final choices in the task before changing status to Approved.

### Documentation

- No documentation changes are made during this planning-only task.
- After implementation and verification, update `docs/development/index.md` or create a specifically owned feature page only if the final behavior needs more space. Document the supported read-status values, search semantics, pagination/query parameters, URL restoration, and mutation-refresh behavior.
- Do not describe target behavior as current guidance before the implementation is complete.

### Task checklist

- [ ] `tasks/20260919-books-discovery/010-api-discovery-contract.md` — define the Flask query/data-selection contract and compatibility evidence.
- [ ] `tasks/20260919-books-discovery/020-client-discovery-state.md` — define the Vue state, controls, rendering, pagination, and transport integration.
- [ ] `tasks/20260919-books-discovery/030-url-history-and-refresh.md` — define URL/history synchronization and state-preserving CRUD refreshes.
- [ ] `tasks/20260919-books-discovery/040-evidence-and-documentation.md` — define cross-boundary tests and the maintained documentation update.
- [ ] Resolve the open requirement questions and update the affected plan sections before execution approval.
- [ ] Keep this parent task in Draft until the requirements and public query contract are approved.

### Requirement verification

- Filter, search, and bounded-page behavior: verify through Flask API tests using the real route and data-selection helper, then through a Books component/integration test that sends the selected parameters and renders the returned page and metadata.
- Consistency of controls, active state, table, pagination, and empty state: verify with component tests covering an initial result, a filtered result, a no-match result, and a page-boundary result.
- URL sharing and restoration: verify with a router-backed test that mounts `/books` with query parameters, reloads/enters the route, changes state, and exercises back/forward navigation while asserting both request parameters and rendered controls.
- CRUD refresh consistency: verify through tests that add, update, and delete retain the canonical discovery state, reload through the selected query, and reconcile an invalidated page according to the approved policy.
- Existing CRUD and unfiltered API compatibility: verify the existing mutation route tests plus a no-query GET assertion that the full collection and current response fields remain available.

### Additional implementation verification

- Check for request/watch loops between component state and router query state.
- Check that a late response from an obsolete discovery request cannot overwrite a newer URL-selected view.
- Check that query serialization omits defaults or normalizes them consistently so equivalent views do not create needless history churn.

# Define the Books API discovery contract

Plan the Flask-side filtering, search, and bounded-pagination behavior that the Books page will consume while retaining the current unfiltered and CRUD API contracts.

Parent Task: tasks/20260919-books-discovery/000-main.md
Depends On: None

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] The GET books contract can select read status and search title or author using optional query inputs.
- [ ] Explicit discovery requests return a bounded page and enough metadata for the client to render reliable page controls.
- [ ] A GET with no discovery parameters remains a full-list response with the current `status` and `books` fields.
- [ ] Existing POST, PUT, and DELETE endpoints and their current mutation behavior remain intact.
- [ ] API evidence covers selection, pagination boundaries, unfiltered compatibility, and mutation regressions.

## Research and supporting facts

- `server/app.py` owns the `/books` GET/POST route and currently returns the complete module-level `BOOKS` list for GET.
- `server/app.py` owns the `/books/<book_id>` PUT/DELETE route; the request does not authorize changing that public endpoint.
- `server/query.py` has a pass-through `list_books` helper, which is the natural home for pure filtering/pagination transformations if that ownership remains appropriate.
- `tests/test_books_api.py` currently asserts only status codes, so response shape and selection semantics need focused coverage.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

First settle the shared query and response contract from the parent task. Then keep data selection in a pure, testable helper: preserve collection order, apply the approved read-status predicate, match the approved title/author search semantics, and calculate a bounded slice plus page metadata. The Flask route should parse request arguments, distinguish an absent discovery query from an explicit paged/discovery request, and serialize the result without mutating the source collection.

The no-query path must continue to expose the complete collection through the existing `status` and `books` fields so existing consumers remain compatible. Additive metadata or a paginated shape must not silently change that legacy path. Mutation routes should remain unchanged except for any tests needed to prove they continue to work after the GET logic is extended.

Add API tests for each approved read-status value, title-only and author-only matches, combined filtering, empty results, first/middle/last page boundaries, invalid input handling, and the no-query full-list contract. Keep the tests at the Flask test-client boundary and add helper-level tests only for calculations that are not meaningfully covered by route assertions.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- Decision: keep the server route at `/books` and make discovery inputs optional.
- Decision: do not paginate or filter the no-query compatibility path unless the approved contract explicitly changes that constraint.
- Open: parameter names, page size, response metadata, matching semantics, and invalid/out-of-range behavior are inherited from the parent task and must be resolved before implementation.
- Recommendation: preserve source order and use a deterministic one-based page model so the client can reason about page bounds without a sort contract.

### Documentation

- Document the final query parameters and response metadata in the feature/development documentation after the API behavior is implemented and tested.
- Do not update current guidance while this task remains a Draft plan.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Resolve and record the public query/response contract.
- [ ] Define the pure selection and pagination behavior, including invalid and out-of-range inputs.
- [ ] Define route-level compatibility behavior for a no-query GET.
- [ ] Plan focused Flask tests for positive, empty, boundary, and regression cases.
- [ ] Mark this subtask ready for execution only after the parent contract is approved.

### Requirement verification

- Optional read-status and title/author selection: Flask test-client requests with each approved query combination and exact returned IDs.
- Bounded pages and metadata: first/last/out-of-range route requests asserting returned slice and page metadata.
- No-query compatibility: a request without discovery parameters asserting the complete fixture collection and existing response keys.
- CRUD preservation: existing POST/PUT/DELETE tests plus a GET-after-mutation assertion where needed to prove the selection extension did not change mutation behavior.

# Build the client Books discovery state and view

Plan the Vue-side state, transport parameters, controls, table rendering, pagination, and empty-state behavior for the approved Books discovery contract.

Parent Task: tasks/20260919-books-discovery/000-main.md
Depends On: tasks/20260919-books-discovery/010-api-discovery-contract.md

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] The component has one canonical discovery state for read status, search, page, and the approved page-size/default values.
- [ ] Controls send the selected state through the existing API adapter and visibly retain their active values.
- [ ] The table renders only the selected page, and bounded pagination reflects the approved page metadata and disables or hides unavailable movement.
- [ ] The empty state represents the selected discovery query without clearing or hiding the active controls.
- [ ] Existing add, update, and remove methods remain available and can reload through the current discovery state.

## Research and supporting facts

- `client/src/components/Books.vue` currently stores only `books`, fetches all books in `mounted`, and has no controls or pagination.
- `client/src/api/books.js` already exposes `getBooks(params = {})`, so the client can pass query parameters without changing `addBook`, `updateBook`, or `deleteBook`.
- The current component test mocks all API functions and checks only the empty-state text; it does not assert request parameters or mutation refreshes.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Introduce an explicit discovery model whose normalized values drive the request, controls, table, pagination, and empty state. Keep the server response separate from the derived page display so metadata is not lost. Build the GET request from that model through `getBooks`, and make loading/error transitions preserve the selected controls rather than falling back to an unfiltered list.

Render the read-status selector and title/author search control as active, accessible inputs. Render the current page of rows and bounded navigation using the API’s approved metadata. Keep the controls visible when there are no matching rows and make the empty message describe the selected result set without implying that the underlying collection is empty unless that distinction is part of the approved copy.

Use one state transition path for initial values, user changes, and responses. Apply the approved page-reset and normalization rules when a query change invalidates the current page. Keep this subtask focused on component state and rendering; URL serialization and browser-history ownership are defined in the dependent URL/history subtask.

Add component tests with controlled API responses for default state, each read-status selection, search parameter construction, returned page rendering, first/last-page controls, no matches, and preservation of state through the mutation refresh hooks. Use a router-backed test only where the URL subtask needs it.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- Decision: the component’s request, rendered content, and controls must derive from one canonical discovery state.
- Decision: continue using the existing `getBooks`/CRUD adapter boundary rather than adding a second transport path.
- Open: exact state field names, default page size, search timing, and page-reset/normalization policy follow the parent contract.
- Recommendation: make filter changes and committed searches reset to page one, while keeping the search input’s displayed value stable during loading.

### Documentation

- Capture control semantics, empty-state behavior, and page navigation in the maintained Books/development documentation after implementation.
- Do not document unverified UI behavior during planning.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Resolve the API response fields and canonical client-state defaults.
- [ ] Define the control-to-state and state-to-request mappings.
- [ ] Define table, pagination, loading, and empty-state rendering rules.
- [ ] Define how mutation callbacks invoke the state-aware loader.
- [ ] Plan component tests for active controls, rendered page, boundaries, empty results, and refreshes.

### Requirement verification

- Canonical controls and request state: component test asserting control values and the exact `getBooks` parameters after each supported interaction.
- Table and pagination: component test with multi-page metadata asserting row IDs and navigation availability at both bounds.
- Empty state: component test with a no-match response asserting the empty message while active controls remain selected.
- CRUD refresh behavior: component test stubbing each mutation and asserting the follow-up GET uses the unchanged canonical discovery state.
task_files.tasks/20260919-books-discovery/030-url-h:
# Synchronize Books discovery with URL history and CRUD refreshes

Plan the router integration that shares and restores Books discovery state, handles browser navigation, and keeps mutation refreshes aligned with the selected view.

Parent Task: tasks/20260919-books-discovery/000-main.md
Depends On: tasks/20260919-books-discovery/020-client-discovery-state.md

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] A `/books` URL can encode the approved discovery state and restore it on direct entry and reload.
- [ ] User changes update the URL without losing the displayed controls or producing router/component synchronization loops.
- [ ] Browser back and forward restore the corresponding discovery state and reload the matching result page.
- [ ] Add, update, and delete refresh the current discovery query and reconcile page/URL changes if the result set changes.
- [ ] Existing `/books` navigation and CRUD endpoints remain usable when the URL has no discovery query.

## Research and supporting facts

- `client/src/router.js` uses `createWebHistory` and declares only the `/books` route; query handling is currently implicit and untested.
- `client/src/components/Books.vue` owns the current mutation methods, so the component and router need a deliberate synchronization boundary rather than independent URL and local state.
- The current API methods reload without parameters after mutations, which would discard any future filter/search/page selection.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Define a single parse/serialize mapping between the canonical component state and the `/books` query string. On route entry or a browser history event, parse and normalize the query before loading data. On a user state change, update the route and let the route-selected state drive the request, avoiding a second competing local copy. Normalize equivalent default values consistently so shared links remain stable.

Separate initial/programmatic route synchronization from user-originated navigation to avoid update loops. Test the chosen history policy with a memory history/router harness: direct query entry restores controls and data; a user transition changes the URL; back/forward restores prior selections and causes the correct GET request. Apply the approved search debounce/commit policy so typing does not unexpectedly create excessive history entries.

Route all add/update/delete follow-up loads through the same canonical state and URL-aware loader. If a mutation removes the last item from the current page or changes an item’s membership in the active filter, apply the approved page-normalization policy and update the URL before asserting the final table and empty state. Keep mutation endpoint calls and payloads unchanged.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- Decision: `/books` query parameters are the shareable source for discovery state; no separate storage mechanism is in scope.
- Decision: browser back/forward must be treated as state changes that reload data, not merely as URL changes.
- Open: exact serialization names/default omission, history granularity for search, and invalid/out-of-range normalization follow the parent task.
- Recommendation: push committed filter/page changes, use a debounced or committed search transition, and replace only canonicalization of an equivalent/default query.

### Documentation

- Document a copyable `/books` query example, restoration behavior, and the mutation-refresh rule after the URL contract is implemented and verified.
- Keep the current development documentation unchanged during planning.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Define the canonical query parser and serializer, including defaults and invalid values.
- [ ] Define the route-entry, user-change, and back/forward event flow.
- [ ] Define history behavior for filter, search, and page transitions.
- [ ] Define mutation refresh and page/URL reconciliation behavior.
- [ ] Plan router-backed tests for direct links, reload-equivalent entry, back/forward, and CRUD refreshes.

### Requirement verification

- Share/restore behavior: router-backed test starting at a fully specified `/books` query and asserting restored controls, request parameters, and rows.
- Browser navigation: memory-history test creating at least two discovery states, navigating back and forward, and asserting both URL and loaded result.
- CRUD consistency: integration test performing each mutation while a non-default discovery query is active and asserting the follow-up query, final URL, page bounds, and table/empty state.
- Legacy navigation: test entering `/books` without a query and confirming the existing default view still loads.

# Verify and document Books discovery behavior

Plan the cross-boundary evidence and maintained documentation update needed to make the Books discovery feature reviewable and current once implementation is approved.

Parent Task: tasks/20260919-books-discovery/000-main.md
Depends On: tasks/20260919-books-discovery/010-api-discovery-contract.md, tasks/20260919-books-discovery/020-client-discovery-state.md, tasks/20260919-books-discovery/030-url-history-and-refresh.md

## Requirements checklist

- [ ] API tests prove filtering, title/author search, bounded pagination, empty results, and no-query compatibility at the Flask route boundary.
- [ ] Client tests prove active controls, table/page rendering, empty-state consistency, URL restoration, browser navigation, and CRUD refreshes.
- [ ] Regression evidence proves existing add/update/delete operations and unfiltered loading remain available.
- [ ] Maintained development documentation describes the verified supported discovery behavior and URL contract after implementation.

## Research and supporting facts

- Python tests live under `tests/` and use the Flask test client fixture in `tests/conftest.py`.
- JavaScript tests live under `client/tests/` and run with `vitest run`; current component coverage mocks the API and has no router integration harness.
- `client/tests/books.integration.js` explicitly records that production transport integration coverage does not yet exist.
- `docs/development/index.md` is the current development documentation index and currently says no book-discovery specification exists.

## Execution plan

Status: Draft

Keep evidence at the smallest boundary that proves each requirement. Extend the Flask test-client suite for the public API contract and compatibility. Extend component tests for local state and rendering. Add a router-backed integration test with a realistic memory-history setup for URL restoration and browser navigation, and include the real API adapter boundary where query parameter wiring is part of the claim rather than mocking it away.

Organize regression cases around user-visible transitions: default unfiltered load, filter/search change, first/last page movement, no matches, direct shared URL, back/forward, add/update/delete while filtered, and a mutation that invalidates the current page. Assert both state/request facts and visible output so a passing test cannot hide a stale table or URL.

After implementation passes the focused tests, update the smallest maintained documentation location. Replace the current “no book-discovery specification exists” statement with verified guidance or link to a focused page only if the behavior needs a longer contract. Include the final status values, search semantics, pagination parameters/metadata, URL example, browser restoration, and CRUD-refresh behavior. Record any gated test that could not be run rather than implying completion.

### Implementation decisions and open questions

- Decision: verification must cross the Flask route, Vue rendering, and router/history boundaries; isolated mocks alone are not sufficient for the URL/transport claims.
- Decision: documentation is updated only after behavior is implemented and evidence passes.
- Open: test fixtures, query names, and exact user-facing copy must follow the approved parent/API/client decisions.
- Recommendation: keep the no-match and page-boundary cases explicit in both API and UI coverage because they are the most likely places for stale controls or out-of-range URLs.

### Documentation

- Planned target: `docs/development/index.md`, with a new focused feature page only if the final contract exceeds the index’s intended scope.
- Document only verified current behavior; do not turn this Draft plan into user guidance.
- Include a concise example of a shareable `/books` URL and explain how browser navigation and CRUD refreshes preserve discovery state.

### Task checklist

- [ ] Map each approved requirement to an API, component, or router-backed test.
- [ ] Add regression cases for unfiltered GET and existing CRUD behavior.
- [ ] Add focused edge cases for empty results, page bounds, invalid URLs, and mutation membership changes according to the approved policy.
- [ ] Run the applicable Python and Vitest suites and record the actual commands/results.
- [ ] Update the maintained documentation after implementation and verification.

### Requirement verification

- API discovery requirements: Flask test-client suite with real route parsing and response assertions.
- UI consistency requirements: Vue component suite asserting active controls, current-page rows, pagination bounds, and empty state together.
- URL/history requirements: router-backed integration suite using memory history and actual route query transitions.
- CRUD/compatibility requirements: mutation regression suite plus no-query GET coverage, with the selected discovery query retained during refresh.
- Documentation requirement: human review of the updated maintained page against the verified test-backed contract.

producer_records.prompt: Migrate post author metadata from the current single-name field to a structured multi-author form without breaking existing content or generated pages during the transition. Templates, archives, feeds, and authoring tools must move to the new model, existing posts must be migrated safely, and the legacy form may be rejected only after generated-output and content evidence show that nothing still depends on it. Plan the work and create the appropriate task structure without implementing it.
producer_records.response:
Task structure created under `tasks/20260919-author-metadata-migration/` — planning only, nothing implemented. Execution waits for your approval.

## Plan summary

**Outcome.** Post author metadata moves from the scalar `author: "Name"` field to a canonical structured multi-author form; post pages, feed, and the authoring tool consume the new model; both existing posts migrate with unchanged URLs and author output; and the legacy form is rejected only after an evidence gate proves nothing depends on it.

**Approach** (5 dependency-ordered subtasks):
1. `010-author-model-and-compat` — install deps, capture a baseline build, add the `authors` model with a normalization layer that maps both forms to one uniform view (unit-tested).
2. `020-templates-feed-and-archives` — post layout renders all authors (joined, `p.author` element retained), feed emits one `<author>` per author, archive/tag/home tests upgraded from existence-only to full listings; build-boundary tests run a fixture site (multi-author + legacy + new-form posts) so no test-only content pollutes production `content/`.
3. `030-authoring-tool` — `frontMatter` emits the structured list form (unit-pinned).
4. `040-migrate-existing-posts` — convert `first.md`/`second.md`, compare generated output against the baseline.
5. `050-legacy-gate-and-rejection` — gate (content scan + tool check + green suite) → remove legacy acceptance → explicit build error naming offending files → README updated in the same change.

**Key facts grounding the plan:** all 7 `author` touchpoints inventoried (`post.njk:2`, `feed.xml.njk:5`, both posts, `new-post.js`, both placeholder tests); archives/tags/sitemap are author-independent; `posts.json` sets no author default; existing tests assert nothing; `node_modules` is absent so execution starts with `npm install`.

**Open decisions needing your approval before the affected subtask runs:**
1. **Shape** — recommend `authors` as an ordered list of display-name strings, always a list (alternative: objects with `name`/`url` if per-author attributes are needed now).
2. **Rejection mechanism** — recommend an explicit build-time error listing files still using legacy `author:` (rather than silently stripping it).
3. **Feed semantics** — recommend preserving current bare-text `<author>` form, one element per author; Atom-validity rework (`<name>` wrapping) deferred out of this migration.

**Acceptance evidence:** unit tests (normalization, tooling) plus production-build tests over post pages, feed, and full archive listings; baseline comparison proves single-author output equivalence during transition; final suite proves the rejection error.

**Risks:** normalization must not disturb the data cascade (covered by fixture builds); feed output for multi-author posts necessarily differs from legacy; removing the legacy path early would break transition guarantees — subtask ordering enforces the gate; a fresh Eleventy 3 install must work in this worktree or the gate can't be evaluated.

**Exclusions:** no per-author archive/profile pages, no Atom-validity rework, no CI setup, no changes to tags/sitemap beyond regression evidence.

The plan is stored as `Status: Draft` in `000-main.md`. Approve it (including the three decisions above, or with corrections) and I'll mark it `Approved` and begin execution with subtask 010.

# Migrate post author metadata to a structured multi-author model Migrate the site's single-name `author` front-matter field to a structured multi-author model across post templates, the feed, archives, and the authoring tool. Existing posts are migrated safely under a compatibility window, and the legacy single-name form is rejected only after generated-output and content evidence show nothing still depends on it. Planning only: this file does not authorize implementation. ## Requirements checklist - [ ] R1: Posts support a single canonical structured author field representing an ordered list of authors; it replaces the single-name `author` field as the supported authoring model. (Exact shape per approved decision in `### Implementation decisions and open questions`.) - [ ] R2: The post page layout renders every author of a post, for both single-author and multi-author posts. - [ ] R3: The feed emits an author element for every author of every post, preserving the currently emitted author-text semantics. - [ ] R4: Archives, tag pages, the home listing, and the sitemap keep rendering all posts (title/link) unchanged through the migration; they have no author dependence and are regression-protected. - [ ] R5: The authoring tool (`scripts/new-post.js`) generates the structured form for new posts. - [ ] R6: During the transition, legacy single-name posts and structured-form posts coexist: both build and render correctly, with no content loss and no broken generated pages at any intermediate state. - [ ] R7: Existing posts (`content/posts/first.md`, `content/posts/second.md`) are migrated to the structured form with their URLs and rendered author output preserved. - [ ] R8: Evidence exists for the new model, the compatibility behavior, and the migration: unit tests for normalization and the authoring tool, plus production-build integration tests over post pages, feed, and archives that include multi-author and legacy/new mixed cases without adding test-only content to production `content/`. - [ ] R9: The legacy single-name form is rejected only after gate evidence — a content scan showing zero legacy usage and green generated-output evidence — and the rejection is an explicit, documented build failure. - [ ] R10: Maintained documentation reflects the author model, the transition state, and the final rejection state, kept in the same reviewed changes as the code that makes each claim true. ## Subtasks - [ ] tasks/20260919-author-metadata-migration/010-author-model-and-compat.md - [ ] tasks/20260919-author-metadata-migration/020-templates-feed-and-archives.md - [ ] tasks/20260919-author-metadata-migration/030-authoring-tool.md - [ ] tasks/20260919-author-metadata-migration/040-migrate-existing-posts.md - [ ] tasks/20260919-author-metadata-migration/050-legacy-gate-and-rejection.md ## Open questions and decisions These change scope or outcomes and must be resolved (by approval of this plan or explicit instruction) before the affected subtask executes. 1. **Structured shape (R1, blocks 010).** Recommend: `authors` as an ordered YAML list of display-name strings, e.g. `authors: ["Ada Example"]`, always a list (no scalar shorthand for the new field; the authoring tool always emits a list). Alternative: entries as objects with at least `name` (optionally `url`) if per-author attributes beyond the display name are required now. Choose one before 010 executes. 2. **Rejection mechanism (R9, blocks 050).** Recommend: a build-time check in the Eleventy data path that fails the build with an error listing files that still define legacy `author:`, so rejection is machine-enforced and matches documentation. Alternative: silently ignoring/stripping the legacy field (rejected recommendation: hides authoring mistakes). 3. **Feed Atom validity (R3, affects 020 scope).** The current feed emits bare text inside `` (not an Atom-valid `` child). Recommend: preserve current semantics (one `` per author, same text form) and defer any Atom-validity rework out of this migration. Confirm or expand 020 scope. ## Supporting details Verified facts from inspection (2026-09-19): - Author touchpoints (complete): - `content/posts/first.md:3` — legacy scalar `author: "Ada Example"`. - `content/posts/second.md:3` — legacy scalar `author: "Grace Example"`. - `_includes/layouts/post.njk:2` — renders scalar `{{ author }}` inside `

`. - `content/feed.xml.njk:5` — `{{ post.data.author }}` per post in `collections.posts`. - `scripts/new-post.js:1-3` — pure `frontMatter(title, author)` emits the legacy scalar string form. - `tests/author-output.test.js`, `tests/archive-output.test.js` — comment-only placeholders, no assertions. - Author-independent generated surfaces: `_includes/postslist.njk` renders title + url only; `content/index.njk`, `content/blog.njk`, and `content/tag-pages.njk` all include `postslist.njk`; `content/sitemap.xml.njk` renders URLs only. - Data cascade: `content/posts/posts.json` sets only `layout` and `tags: ["posts"]`; there is no directory-level author default. - Build config (`eleventy.config.js`): input `content`, includes `../_includes`, output `_site`; provides a `head` filter; passthrough-copies `public` (directory does not exist — pre-existing condition, not in scope). - Test harness: `npm test` runs `node --test tests/*.test.js`; both files currently collect and exit cleanly (verified with node v20.19.5) but assert nothing. Generated output (`_site/`) is gitignored. - Dependencies are not installed in this worktree (`node_modules` absent); execution must start with `npm install` (`@11ty/eleventy ^3.0.0`). - Documentation surface: root `README.md` describes build outputs; `docs/development/index.md` and `docs/development/documentation.md` are maintainer guidance; there is no `docs/index.md`. Author-model documentation belongs in the author-facing surface (`README.md`) per `docs/development/documentation.md` rules. - `UPSTREAM.md`: fixture adapted from Eleventy Base Blog. Constraints: - No test-only posts may be added to production `content/`; multi-author and mixed-form build coverage must come from a separate fixture site (see 020). - For single-author posts, the new pipeline must produce equivalent generated output to the current build, which allows before/after comparison as transition evidence. - New public documentation claims must land in the same reviewed change as the code that makes them true (repository documentation guidance). ## Execution plan Status: Draft Layered migration: normalize both author forms behind one data view, migrate all consumers (post layout, feed) to that view with generated-output tests, migrate the authoring tool, migrate existing content, then evaluate the legacy-dependency gate and reject the legacy form. Consumers are changed before content so that migrated posts render correctly the moment they are converted; the legacy path is removed last, after evidence. Sequence and boundaries: 1. **010 — model + compatibility.** Install dependencies, capture a baseline production build of the current content (comparison artifact), then introduce the canonical `authors` model with a normalization step that yields a uniform authors list from either the new form or the legacy scalar. Templates do not change yet. Unit tests cover normalization of both forms. 2. **020 — consumers.** Post layout renders all authors (joined display, existing `p.author` element class retained); feed emits one author element per author with current text semantics; archives are regression-covered (posts listed with titles/links, not just existence). Generated-output tests cross the real build boundary via a fixture site that includes a multi-author post, a new-form single-author post, and a legacy post, so the compat path is exercised; real-content build checks cover first/second. 3. **030 — authoring tool.** `frontMatter` emits the structured list form; unit test pins the exact emitted front matter. 4. **040 — content migration.** Convert `first.md` and `second.md` to the structured form; compare generated output against the 010 baseline (same URLs, same rendered author text, archive/feed/sitemap intact). 5. **050 — gate + rejection.** Evidence gate: content scan shows zero legacy `author:` usage in `content/`, authoring tool no longer emits it, all build-boundary tests green. Only then remove legacy acceptance from the normalization path, add the explicit build-time rejection error, re-run the full suite and production build, and update `README.md` to the final rejection state (removing the transitional note added earlier). Risks: - Normalization must integrate with the Eleventy data cascade without shadowing unrelated post data; `posts.json` has no author keys, so risk is low but the integration tests must catch regressions. - Feed output for multi-author posts necessarily differs from the legacy single-element output; single-author output must remain text-equivalent (R3/R7 comparison evidence). - Removing the legacy path before the gate would break transition guarantees; subtask ordering (050 strictly after 030/040 evidence) enforces the gate. - Fresh `npm install` and an Eleventy 3 build in this worktree are prerequisites; if the build cannot run, the gate cannot be evaluated and the plan stops at the blocked subtask with the blocker reported. ### Implementation decisions and open questions - D1 (open, needs approval): field shape — recommend `authors` list of display-name strings, always a list. See top-level question 1. - D2 (open, needs approval): rejection mechanism — recommend explicit build-time error listing offending files. See top-level question 2. - D3 (open, needs approval): feed keeps current bare-text `` semantics, one element per author; Atom-validity rework deferred. See top-level question 3. - D4 (resolved locally): multi-author post-page display joins author names with a comma inside the existing `p.author` element; element/class retained so page structure and styling hooks are unchanged. - D5 (resolved locally): canonical form is list-only; legacy scalar is accepted only by the compatibility path during the transition window and is not a shorthand for the new field. - D6 (resolved locally): generated-output tests build a small fixture site under `tests/` (own content, real templates/config) rather than adding test-only posts to production `content/`; real-content builds cover the actual posts. - D7 (resolved locally): test builds write to a gitignored/temporary output directory so the working tree stays clean. ### Documentation - Audience: post authors/contributors (front-matter model, authoring tool behavior, legacy rejection state). Maintainers get context from this task tree. - 010/020: `README.md` gains a short author-metadata section describing the structured `authors` model with an example and the transitional note that the legacy single-name form is still accepted. - 030: same section notes the authoring tool emits the structured form. - 050: the section is updated in the same change as the rejection code — transitional note removed, legacy `author:` documented as rejected with an explicit build error, with an example of the accepted form. - No new documentation directories or pages; smallest structure per `docs/development/documentation.md`. ### Task checklist - [ ] tasks/20260919-author-metadata-migration/010-author-model-and-compat.md - [ ] tasks/20260919-author-metadata-migration/020-templates-feed-and-archives.md - [ ] tasks/20260919-author-metadata-migration/030-authoring-tool.md - [ ] tasks/20260919-author-metadata-migration/040-migrate-existing-posts.md - [ ] tasks/20260919-author-metadata-migration/050-legacy-gate-and-rejection.md ### Requirement verification - R1 → unit tests for normalization (both forms) plus generated-output tests showing structured posts build and render (010, 020). - R2 → fixture-site build test: multi-author post page contains every author name; single-author post page contains its author (020). - R3 → fixture-site build test: feed contains one `` element per author per post; single-author feed text matches the pre-migration form (020, 040 comparison). - R4 → archive/tag/home build tests assert full post lists (title + link), not existence only; sitemap URLs unchanged (020, 040). - R5 → unit test pinning `frontMatter` output to the structured list form (030). - R6 → fixture-site test includes a legacy post and a new-form post building side by side and rendering correctly (020, 040). - R7 → real-content build comparison against the 010 baseline: same URLs, same rendered author text, archives/feed intact (040). - R8 → full `node --test tests/*.test.js` run collecting all unit and build-boundary tests cleanly (010–040;
